name: NUI.Affix
comment:
Naive UI's `Affix`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Affix exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Affix.view theme
        { defaults | affixed = True, top = Just 12 }
        [ NUI.Button.view theme NUI.Button.defaults [ Element.text "Sticky" ] ]

The element carries the `.n-affix` BEM classes, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's
exact CSS.

**Runtime.** Upstream decides `affixed` (and the sticky `top` / `bottom`) from
`scroll` events on a listen target. This library is pure, so the caller owns that
state and passes it in: `affixed` toggles `.n-affix--affixed` (`.n-affix--absolute-positioned`
with `position = Absolute`), and `top` / `bottom` are emitted as inline offsets
only while affixed — exactly upstream's `mergedstyle`.

@docs Options, Position, defaults, view

unions.name: Position
unions.comment: Naive UI's `position` — how the affixed element is pinned.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The affix options. `affixed` is the caller-owned pinned state (upstream
derives it from `scroll` events on the listen target); `top` / `bottom` are
the sticky offsets, emitted as an inline style only while affixed; `position`
switches the pinning mode (`Absolute` adds `n-affix--absolute-positioned`).
aliases.type: { affixed : Basics.Bool, position : NUI.Affix.Position, top : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int, bottom : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: defaults
values.comment: Un-pinned defaults: `Fixed` positioning, no offsets, no extra attributes.

values.name: view
values.comment:
Render the affix wrapper around `children`. While `affixed` the element
carries `n-affix--affixed` (plus `n-affix--absolute-positioned` when
`position = Absolute`) and the `top` / `bottom` offsets as an inline style —
exactly upstream's `mergedstyle`; at rest it is a bare `n-affix` column
carrying `attributes`.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Affix.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Alert
comment:
Naive UI's `Alert`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Alert exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Alert.view theme
        NUI.Alert.defaults
        [ Element.text "Just as in the original component." ]

    NUI.Alert.view theme
        { defaults
            | kind = T.Success
            , title = Just "Success"
            , closable = True
            , onClose = Just Dismiss
        }
        [ Element.text "Just as in the original component." ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-alert` BEM classes
and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

Naive UI's alert has no `primary` type, so `T.Primary` falls back to the un-suffixed
(default) theme variables.

@docs Options, defaults, view

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The alert options. `kind` picks the colour set (Naive UI's `type`; no
`primary` alert exists, so `T.Primary` shares the default vars), `title` and
the children fill `n-alert-body__title` / `__content`, `closable` adds the
close button (firing `onClose`), `showIcon` toggles the kind icon (or `icon`
when set), `bordered` adds the `__border` decoration, `rtl` mirrors the
layout.
aliases.type: { kind : NUI.Types.Kind, title : Maybe.Maybe String.String, bordered : Basics.Bool, closable : Basics.Bool, showIcon : Basics.Bool, icon : Maybe.Maybe (Element.Element msg), onClose : Maybe.Maybe msg, rtl : Basics.Bool }

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults — `type: 'default'`, bordered, icon shown, not
closable, no title, LTR.

values.name: view
values.comment:
Render the alert: `role="alert"` root with the `n-alert` BEM classes,
Naive UI's `--n-*` variables (theme-coloured per `kind`), the close button
first, then the border and icon decorations, then the body (optional title,
content). `children` are the content paragraph's inline elements.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Alert.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Anchor
comment:
Naive UI's `Anchor` / `AnchorLink`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Anchor as Anchor

    NUI.Anchor.view theme
        { Anchor.defaults | activeHref = Just "#basic" }
        [ Anchor.Link
            { title = Just "Demos"
            , titleSlot = Nothing
            , href = Just "#demos"
            , children =
                [ Anchor.Link
                    { title = Just "Basic"
                    , titleSlot = Nothing
                    , href = Just "#basic"
                    , children = []
                    , onClick = Nothing
                    , attributes = []
                    }
                ]
            , onClick = Nothing
            , attributes = []
            }
        ]

The element carries the `.n-anchor` BEM classes (rail + bar, link-background,
`.n-anchor-link` / `__title`, the `--block` / `--show-rail` modifiers) and the
twelve `--n-*` custom properties on the root, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's
exact CSS.

**Runtime.** Upstream tracks the scroll position (a throttled capture-phase
`scroll` listener), reduces the collected link offsets (`bound` / `ignoreGap` /
`offsetTarget`) to the active href, and imperatively positions the rail bar and
the link background. This library is pure, so the caller owns that state:
`activeHref` is the input (it drives `n-anchor-rail__bar--active` and
`n-anchor-link--active`, exactly upstream's `activeHrefRef`), and the bar /
background render style-less — upstream only writes their inline styles after
mount (the `NUI.Affix` / `NUI.Scrollbar` caller-owned-runtime precedent).
`scrollTo`, `bound`, `ignoreGap` and `offsetTarget` are therefore not modelled;
the click seam is per-link `onClick` (upstream's `handleClick` calls
`setActiveHref` with the link's href).

**Affix mode.** Upstream's `affix` prop wraps the anchor in `NAffix` (and
flattens the affix props into the anchor's props). Pass `affix = Just` affix
options to compose `NUI.Affix.view` around the anchor root — the pinned state
(`affixed` / offsets) stays caller-owned there too.

**Documented gaps:**

  - A link without `href` renders its title as a non-anchor element — an
    upstream `<a>` without the `href` attribute is inert, and the cssr styles
    `.n-anchor-link__title` by class, not tag (the `NUI.Breadcrumb` precedent).
  - `internalScrollable` (upstream's undocumented scrollbar wrapper, the stale
    spec name `naiveScrollbar`) wraps the anchor in `NUI.Scrollbar.view` with
    default options, exactly upstream's bare `<NScrollbar>`.
  - The `title` tooltip attribute follows `getTitleAttribute`: an empty string
    omits the attribute (upstream also accepts numbers; the port's title is a
    string). A `titleSlot` replaces the title content but never the attribute.
  - Derived colours (`linkColor` = `changeColor(primary, α .15)`) are pinned
    literals in `NUI.Theme.Anchor` (toolchain convention, cf. Tag) — a `common`
    override re-derives `railColorActive` but not `linkColor`.

@docs Link, Options, Type, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

unions.comment:
Naive UI's `AnchorLink`, wrapped because a recursive record cannot be a
type alias (the `NUI.Cascader.Option` precedent) — `title` is the prop (tooltip
attribute + fallback content), `titleSlot` the `#title` slot (content only),
`children` the nested links, `onClick` upstream's `handleClick` seam.

unions.name: Type
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `type` — `Rail` draws the sider rail (default), `Block` draws
active links as colour chips.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The anchor options. `type_` picks the rail / block rendering, `showRail`
and `showBackground` toggle the rail and link background, `activeHref` is the
caller-owned active link (upstream's scroll-reduced `activeHrefRef`),
`internalScrollable` wraps in `NUI.Scrollbar`, `affix` composes
`NUI.Affix.view` around the root, `attributes` land on the anchor root.

values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults — rail type, rail and background shown, no active
link, not scrollable, not affixed.

values.comment:
Render the anchor: the `n-anchor` root (the `--block` / `--show-rail`
modifiers, the twelve `--n-*` vars) with the link background and rail when
shown, then the links. Optionally wrapped in the internal scrollbar and /
or the caller's `NUI.Affix` options.

name: NUI.AutoComplete
comment:
Naive UI's `AutoComplete` — an `NUI.Input` trigger plus a caller-mounted
`NUI.SelectMenu` body. Upstream (`AutoComplete.tsx`) mounts `NInput` in a
VBinder target and `NInternalSelectMenu` in the follower — AutoComplete is
NOT an `NInternalSelection` consumer (the trigger really is a plain input;
the `NUI.Select` composition minus the BaseSelection couplings).

    import NUI.AutoComplete as AutoComplete
    import NUI.SelectMenu

    AutoComplete.view theme
        { AutoComplete.defaults | onInput = Just Typed }
    AutoComplete.menu theme AutoComplete.menuDefaults
        [ AutoComplete.fromString "Drive My Car"
        , SelectMenu.Option
            { value = "nomc"
            , label = "Norwegian Wood"
            , disabled = False
            , attributes = []
            }
        ]

Trigger (`view`) DOM — the `.n-auto-complete` wrapper is bare (no vars, no
state classes; all styling lives on the `.n-input` and the menu). The
caller's `attributes` land on an OUTER elm-ui node (the explicit-width
seam in `view`'s docstring — the wrapper's `width: 100%` cssr beats an
elm-ui width class on the same node):

    div (caller width)
        └─ div.n
        - auto
        - complete
        └─ NUI.Input.view (see its docstring for the full tree)

`view` maps per-field: `value` / `onInput` (typing; the clear icon fires
`onInput ""` — upstream `onUpdateValue(null)`, null ≡ "" here), `placeholder`
(default baked `"Please Input"`, the en-US locale upstream resolves on the
input when the prop is absent), `size` (small / medium / large — upstream
`AutoCompleteSize` has no tiny; keys the INPUT only), `status` (re-bound to
`NUI.Input.Status`), `disabled`, `bordered`, `clearable`, `loading` (the
INPUT's suffix spinner — `n-base-loading.n-base-suffix`; never a menu
`__loading` row, unlike Select), `prefix` / `suffix`, `rtl` (the input's
`--rtl`; the wrapper and menu classes are the only other rtl surface —
upstream's own cssr has no rtl block), `inputAttributes` (upstream
`inputProps`, onto the inner `<input>`), and `attributes` (wrapper).

Menu (`menu`) DOM — the `NUI.SelectMenu` body carrying AutoComplete's own
class and vars (the `NUI.Select.menu` composition with the select couplings
removed):

    div.n-base-select-menu .n-base-select-menu--medium-size
        [--rtl] .n-auto-complete-menu [fade-in-scale-up-transition-*]
      tabindex = -1   (NOT focusable — upstream omits the prop,
                       InternalSelectMenu defaults it false → -1;
                       Select hardcodes true, AutoComplete does not)
      style = 23 menu vars at Medium → --n-menu-box-shadow
              (24 declarations; upstream also re-emits --n-bezier here —
              same value, the port emits it once)
      └─ NUI.SelectMenu rows — value stays `Single Nothing`: no row is ever
         `--selected` and no checkmark NODE renders (`--show-checkmark`
         still lands on rows, the padding rule needs it); `multiple =
         False`; `loading = False` (the menu is untouched by loading)

The menu is hardcoded Medium (upstream `size="medium"`, `AutoComplete.tsx`
`:487`) — the trigger's `size` never keys it. `--rtl` rides the menu through
config upstream (`useRtl` inside InternalSelectMenu); here `MenuOptions.rtl`.

`menuVars` = the 23 `NUI.SelectMenu` vars at Medium + `--n-menu-box-shadow`
(AutoComplete's single own var; `NUI.Theme.AutoComplete` is the Select twin
— 1 var, light = dark derivation).

Options are `NUI.SelectMenu.Option` verbatim: upstream's
`AutoCompleteOption` record is the strict `LeafOption` subset (value and
label both strings), bare-string options go through `fromString`, groups
map 1:1, `renderLabel` / `renderOption` become label strings / `Custom`
rows. Upstream's group mapper folds the deprecated `name` into
`label`/`value`/`key` — the caller's data-conversion step.

Caller-owned runtime (the port-wide convention): the whole show gate —
`active = (getShow ? getShow (value || "") : value ≠ "") && focused-typed
&& (showEmpty || options non-empty)`; `focused-typed` turns true on
focus / input and false on blur, outside click and any select (focus alone
never opens the menu; AutoComplete does NO filtering of its own — it renders
every option it is given, demos derive options from the input prefix);
positioning / mounting (`placement` default `bottom-start`,
`width="target"` hardcoded, `to` / `zIndex` teleport); keyboard (Enter
selects the pending node — skipped while IME-composing; ArrowUp / ArrowDown
= menu next / prev; nothing else, closing is pure blur / clickoutside);
pending (`--pending` via per-option `attributes`, init to the first
available option); the select commit — fire `onSelect option.value` always,
then `clearAfterSelect` → value null, else label commit (`append` ⇒
`value ++ label`), deactivate, optional `blurAfterSelect` blur; focus /
blur inst methods; IME. When you implement the gate, `getShow` receives
`value || ""` (upstream's null-safe call shape).

Dropped: the deprecated `onInput` alias of `onUpdate:value` (`warnOnce`
upstream); the `default` custom-input slot (render your own input + `menu` —
upstream wires handleInput / handleFocus / handleBlur into the first slot
vnode only); `onInput`-alias, `to` / `zIndex`. `scrollbarProps` has no
`NUI.SelectMenu` seam (the plain option-wrapper path is the port's render)
— the field stays for the caller, the `NUI.Select` precedent. Values are
`String` (upstream `string | null`; null ≡ "").

@docs MenuOptions, Options, Size, Status, defaults, fromString, menu, menuDefaults, menuVars, view

Naive UI's defaults (`size: 'medium'` via the form/config merge,

Upstream's bare-string option (`utils.ts` maps `string` →

values.name: menu
values.comment:
The `n-auto-complete-menu` body — `NUI.SelectMenu.view` carrying
`extraClasses = ["n-auto-complete-menu", transition?]`, `focusable = False`
(upstream omits the prop → tabindex -1), `value = Single Nothing` (never

style. Mount it in the caller's positioned wrapper when the show gate is
open.

values.name: menuDefaults
values.comment: The menu defaults (everything false / empty).

values.name: menuVars
values.comment:
The menu's root style — the 23 `NUI.SelectMenu` vars at Medium plus
AutoComplete's one own var (`--n-menu-box-shadow`). The trigger's 50 vars
live in `NUI.Input.cssVars`.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The bare `.n-auto-complete` wrapper + the `NUI.Input` trigger, mapped
per the module docstring.

**Explicit-width seam** (the `NUI.Mention` precedent, fix2-misc): the
wrapper's cssr is `.nui-root.nui-root .n-auto-complete { width: 100% }`
(specificity 0,3,0), which beats elm-ui's own `Element.width (px n)`
class on the same node (`.we.width-px-n`, 0,1,0) — an explicit trigger
width `Element.width`ed onto `attributes` was silently dropped and every
trigger rendered full-width. The caller's `attributes` therefore land on
an OUTER elm-ui node and the `n-auto-complete` wrapper stays on the inner
one: a caller width sizes the outer node (no competing rule) and the
inner wrapper still fills it via its `width: 100%` rule (upstream's
display: inline-flex is preserved by the wrapper keeping its class). The
default (no caller width) fills the available width (`Element.width
Element.fill` prepended — elm-ui reverses the attribute list and keeps
the FIRST `Width` attribute it reaches, so a caller `Element.width` in
`attributes` still wins over the default fill).

name: NUI.Avatar
comment: Naive UI's `Avatar`, rebuilt on elm-ui. import NUI.Avatar exposing (defaults) NUI.Avatar.view theme { defaults | src = Just "https://example.com/avatar.png" } [] NUI.Avatar.view theme NUI.Avatar.defaults [ Element.text "N" ] Text children are centered the way Naive UI's `fitTextTransform` does after its initial measurement. Upstream then _scales_ oversized text down to fit the tile (a runtime measurement we cannot take in a pure view), so this port instead lets a text avatar grow to fit its label: the tile is `min-width` its configured size and `width` its content, so `Rounded` renders on one line inside a slightly wider tile rather than clipped edge-to-edge mid-glyph (short labels — `T`, `A`, `+3` — stay exactly the configured square). A `src` image renders as a CSS `background-image` tile rather than an ``: a failed load then falls back to the avatar's own colour tile (upstream's `renderFallback` / `fallback-src` behaviour) instead of leaking the browser's broken-image glyph. Loaded images look identical (stretched to fill, matching upstream's `.n-avatar img { width/height: 100% }`). @docs AvatarSize, Options, defaults, view

unions.comment:
Naive UI's avatar `size`: a preset name (including `huge`, which only Avatar
uses) or an explicit pixel number.

aliases.name: Options

The avatar options. `size` keys the tile dimensions (and the round /
circle radius), `round` / `circle` both render `border-radius: 50%` (upstream
quirk), `bordered` adds `--n-border`, `color` overrides the theme tile colour,
`src` renders the image tile instead of text children, `attributes` land on
the `n-avatar` root.

Naive UI's defaults — medium square tile, no border, no image, themed
colour.

Render one avatar: the `n-avatar` root with the `--n-*` vars. Text children
land in `n-avatar__text`; a `src` renders the background-image tile; neither
is present when both are unset. See the module doc for the text-fit trade-off.

name: NUI.BackTop
comment:
Naive UI's `BackTop`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.BackTop exposing (defaults)

    NUI.BackTop.view theme
        { defaults | show = True, onClick = Just ScrollToTop }
        []

The element carries the `.n-back-top` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS (including the
`fade-in-scale-up-transition` rules).

**Runtime.** Upstream decides `show` from a scroll listener, teleports the button
to `body`, and compensates for the locked scrollbar width. This library is pure,
so the caller owns `show` (the button renders only while true) and the offsets;
the `fade-in-scale-up-transition` phase is caller-owned too (pass `transition`).
The `to` / `listen-to` teleport target and the scrollbar-width calc are not
reproduced.

`transitionDisabled` skips them; `onClick` fires on click; `attributes` land
on the button.

the default arrow icon.

name: NUI.Badge
comment:
Naive UI's `Badge`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    NUI.Badge.view theme
        { defaults | value = Just (Number 20), max = Just 9 }
        [ NUI.Button.view theme NUI.Button.defaults [ Element.text "Mail" ] ]

    NUI.Badge.view theme
        { defaults | dot = True, type_ = Info }
        []

    NUI.Badge.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = Just (Number 200)
            , max = Just 99
            , processing = True
            , color = Just "#36ad6a"
        }
        []

(`defaults` must be bound to a local name first — Elm's record update syntax
does not accept a qualified `NUI.Badge.defaults` there.)

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-badge` BEM
classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive
UI's exact CSS (including the `_internal` slot-machine and wave rules).

The children are the content the badge annotates (Naive UI's `default` slot);
with none, the badge renders "as is" (`n-badge--as-is`). Structure mirrors
`Badge.tsx`'s render — children first, then a `sup.n-badge-sup` carrying
`NBaseSlotMachine`'s digit DOM and, when `processing`, an `NBaseWave`:

    div.n-badge
    ├── children …
    └── sup.n-badge-sup                     when the badge is shown
        ├── span.n-base-slot-machine        numeric value (never for dots)
        │   ├── span                        TransitionGroup wrapper
        │   │   └── span.n-base-slot-machine-number … per digit
        │   └── span.n-base-slot-machine-number … the "+" over max
        └── div.n-base-wave                 when processing

Runtime behaviour is data-driven — the caller owns the state (and its timers),
and the view emits exactly Naive UI's DOM for it:

  - RTL — `rtl` adds `n-badge--rtl` and mirrors the offset base to `50%`.
  - Digit scroll — `previousValue` renders the previous digits (aligned by place
    value) and the `--up-scroll` / `--down-scroll` classes on the slot machine.
    The classes are attached while `previousValue` is set and differs from
    `value`, and stay attached for as long as it keeps differing (upstream keeps
    them on after a change too, only dropping them on the _next_ change). So to
    replay the animation the caller must move `previousValue` between renders —
    e.g. clear it to `Nothing` (or set it equal to `value`) between changes.
  - Mount / leave transition — `transition` (a `NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase`)
    adds the `fade-in-scale-up-transition-*` class on the sup; a leave phase
    keeps the sup mounted after the badge is hidden.
  - Wave replay — `waveActive` adds `n-base-wave--active`.

Still out of scope: Naive UI's `value` slot (custom sup content) — `value`
renders it; and the TransitionGroup / expand mount animations for digits added
when the digit count grows (e.g. `99` → `100`), where upstream animates the new
leading cell and the `+` cell (the resting DOM we render matches).

name: NUI.BaseSelection
comment:
Naive UI's internal selection trigger (upstream `NInternalSelection`,
`_internal/selection/`) — the support module `NUI.Select` renders (and,
later, Cascader / TreeSelect — the actual `NInternalSelection` consumers
upstream; AutoComplete / Mention / DatePicker / TimePicker all trigger
through a plain `NInput` instead; the `NUI.SelectMenu`
precedent: static DOM/theme fidelity is the bar, runtime is caller-owned).

    div.n-base-selection
        [--rtl] [--{status}-status] [--active] [--selected] [--disabled]
        [--multiple] [--focus]
      style = 52 css vars (below)
      ├─ body — one of four variants:
      │   single, not filterable:
      │     div.n-base-selection-label [tabindex 0 | —]
      │       (selected → div.n-base-selection-input [title=label]
      │                     > div.n-base-selection-input__content {label})
      │       (else     → div.n-base-selection-placeholder.n-base-selection-overlay
      │                     > div.n-base-selection-placeholder__inner {placeholder})
      │       suffix
      │   single, filterable:
      │     div.n-base-selection-label [title=label unless active]
      │       > input.n-base-selection-input
      │           [value = active ? pattern : "", placeholder="",
      │            readonly|disabled, tabindex=-1]
      │       (selected && !active → div.n-base-selection-label__render-label
      │           .n-base-selection-overlay > div.__wrapper {label})
      │       (placeholder-rule   → div.n-base-selection-placeholder
      │           .n-base-selection-overlay > div.__wrapper {selected?label:placeholder})
      │       suffix
      │   multiple:
      │     div.n-base-selection-tags [tabindex 0 | —]
      │       > div.n-base-selection-tag-wrapper > NTag{size, closable=!tag.disabled,
      │           disabled, onClose}                                   — per tag
      │       > div.n-base-selection-tag-wrapper > NTag{size, disabled} {+N}
      │                                                                  — iff ellipsisTag
      │       (filterable → div.n-base-selection-input-tag
      │           > input.__input [value=pattern, tabindex=-1, disabled]
      │           + span.__mirror {pattern})
      │       suffix
      │     (placeholder-rule, SIBLING after the tags div:
      │       div.n-base-selection-placeholder.n-base-selection-overlay
      │         > div.n-base-selection-placeholder__inner {placeholder})
      └─ [bordered] div.n-base-selection__border
         [bordered] div.n-base-selection__state-border

Suffix (upstream `Suffix.tsx`, a fragment): `NBaseLoading`
(`div.n-base-loading.n-base-suffix`, strokeWidth 24, scale 0.85 — the
`NUI.Button` loading idiom) whose idle slot is, iff `showArrow`, `NBaseClear`
(`div.n-base-clear` > `__clear [data-clear]` when `showClear`, else
`__placeholder`) with the placeholder slot `div.n-base-icon
.n-base-suffix__arrow` > ChevronDown svg (the `arrow` override replaces the
svg content).

Placeholder rules (upstream exact): single non-filterable — placeholder iff
no label. Single filterable — `active ? !hasPattern : !selected` shows the
placeholder (its `__wrapper` holds the SELECTED label while one exists, the
`filterablePlaceholder` quirk), `selected && !active` shows the
`__render-label` overlay. Multiple — `!selected && (!active || pattern == "")`.

`--selected` = has selection (`!List.isEmpty tags` / `selectedLabel /= Nothing`)
`|| (active && pattern /= "")`. Everything runtime stays caller-owned: focus
and `--focus`, hover (feeds `showClear`), IME composition, the mirror-width
sync (`__input` width tracks `__mirror`), `input-tag` visibility (CSS keeps
it `display:none`; upstream JS flips it to inline-block on input focus), the
responsive maxTagCount overflow and its preview popover (numeric
`ellipsisTag` is the static seam), `tabindex=-1` while the pattern input
holds focus. `title` on the filterable label drops while `active`
(upstream: while the pattern input is focused — same states statically).

The 52 `--n-*` vars, upstream cssVarsRef order: `--n-bezier`, `--n-border`,
`--n-border-active`, `--n-border-focus`, `--n-border-hover`,
`--n-border-radius`, `--n-box-shadow-active`, `--n-box-shadow-focus`,
`--n-box-shadow-hover`, `--n-caret-color`, `--n-color`, `--n-color-active`,
`--n-color-disabled`, `--n-font-size`, `--n-height`, `--n-padding-single-top`,
`--n-padding-multiple-top`, `--n-padding-single-right`,
`--n-padding-multiple-right`, `--n-padding-single-left`,
`--n-padding-multiple-left`, `--n-padding-single-bottom`,
`--n-padding-multiple-bottom`, `--n-placeholder-color`,
`--n-placeholder-color-disabled`, `--n-text-color`, `--n-text-color-disabled`,
`--n-arrow-color`, `--n-arrow-color-disabled`, `--n-loading-color`,
`--n-color-active-warning`, `--n-box-shadow-focus-warning`,
`--n-box-shadow-active-warning`, `--n-box-shadow-hover-warning`,
`--n-border-warning`, `--n-border-focus-warning`, `--n-border-hover-warning`,
`--n-border-active-warning`, `--n-color-active-error`,
`--n-box-shadow-focus-error`, `--n-box-shadow-active-error`,
`--n-box-shadow-hover-error`, `--n-border-error`, `--n-border-focus-error`,
`--n-border-hover-error`, `--n-border-active-error`, `--n-clear-size`,
`--n-clear-color`, `--n-clear-color-hover`, `--n-clear-color-pressed`,
`--n-arrow-size`, `--n-font-weight`. Size-keyed: `--n-height` /
`--n-font-size` switch on `size` (tiny 22px/12px … large 40px/15px); the
paddings split `paddingSingle`/`paddingMultiple` per side (seemly
`getPadding`, the `NUI.SelectMenu.paddingSides` 1–4-part forms).

comment:

    import NUI.Button exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Button.view theme NUI.Button.defaults

    NUI.Button.view theme

    -- `spin*` fields port upstream's `spinProps` spread over its

            | loading = True
            , spinStrokeWidth = Just 6

name: NUI.Calendar
comment:
Naive UI's `Calendar`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Calendar exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Calendar.view theme
        { defaults
            | panel = { year = 2026, month = 7 }
            , now = { year = 2026, month = 7, day = 15 }
            , value = Just { year = 2026, month = 7, day = 20 }
        }

The element carries the `.n-calendar` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. The header buttons are real
`NUI.Button`s in an `NUI.ButtonGroup` (small, like upstream), and the month grid
reproduces the `dateArray` layout from Naive UI's date-picker (`strip` mode):
whole display month, previous-month days in front, next-month days padded to
28 / 35 / 42 cells.

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream keeps the displayed month (`monthTs`), the
selected value and "now" in Vue refs; this library is pure, so all three are
options and every state change is a message you wire yourself:

  - `panel` — the displayed month. The prev / today / next header buttons emit
    `onPanelChange` with the **target** panel (upstream mutates `monthTs` itself
    and then fires `onPanelChange`); set `panel` from the payload to follow.
    The today button only emits when the panel would actually change, exactly
    like upstream's `oldYear !== newYear || oldMonth !== newMonth` guard.
  - `value` / `onUpdateValue` — the selected date. Clicking a cell emits the
    clicked `Date`; disabled cells emit nothing. Upstream additionally fires
    `onPanelChange` when an other-month cell is clicked (it moves the panel to
    that month) — a single Elm message cannot fire both, so apply that panel
    change in your `onUpdateValue` handler when the date's month differs from
    `panel`.
  - `now` — the reference date for the `--current` cell and the today button.
    `defaults` cannot know it; always set `panel` and `now`.

**Locale** replaces upstream's `useLocale('DatePicker')` + date-fns locale:
weekday names (the first grid row's `format(ts, 'EEE')` labels), month names,
the header title formatter and `firstDayOfWeek` (Naive UI convention: 0 is
Monday … 6 is Sunday; `enUS` is 6, so weeks start on Sunday). The grid walks
backwards through the previous month until the day **before** the configured
first day — a byte-for-byte port of `dateArray`'s `getDay` loop.

**Slots.** Upstream's `header` slot is a plain `Maybe (Element msg)` (it cannot
react to the panel), and the default cell slot is `cell : Maybe (Date -> …)`
(receives the cell's date; upstream passes `{ year, month (1-based), date }`).

Two deliberate divergences, both invisible in the browser: upstream's
`DateItem.month` is 0-based while `Date` here is 1-based; and upstream also
emits `n-calendar-cell--not-allowed` next to `--disabled`, a marker class no
CSS rule targets (both are emitted here; `--disabled` carries the styles).

    -- with options (bind `defaults` first: Elm has no qualified record update)
    myCard : NUI.Card.Options msg
    myCard =
        { defaults
            | title = Just (Element.text "Card")
            , headerExtra = Just (Element.text "#header-extra")
            , footer = Just (Element.text "#footer")
            , action = Just (Element.text "#action")
        }

    NUI.Card.view theme myCard [ Element.text "Card Content" ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-card` BEM classes and
Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Sizes.** Naive UI's card takes `small | medium | large | huge`, which does not match
`NUI.Types.Size` (`tiny … large`), so this module defines its own `CardSize`.

**Closable.** The close button is Naive UI's internal `n-base-close`. Its stylesheet is
not part of the generated CSS yet, so its structural rules are ported inline here
(`:hover` / `:active` colour shifts cannot be inlined and are currently missing).

**Composition seams.** `extraClasses` (appended after the card's own classes,
like a Vue fallthrough class) and `attributes` let wrapper components merge
themselves onto the card root — `NUI.Modal`'s card preset uses them for the
`n-modal` class, `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`. `style` carries
upstream's fallthrough style fragment (merged into the root `style` AFTER
the `--n-*` vars — the `NUI.Dialog.rootStyleAttr` precedent; a second
`style` attribute would clobber the vars in the DOM).

name: NUI.Carousel
comment:
Naive UI's `Carousel`, rebuilt as a pure state machine + geometry engine.

    import NUI.Carousel as Carousel
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    opts : Carousel.Options msg
    opts =
        { Carousel.defaults | slidesPerView = Carousel.PerView 3 }

    slides : List (Html.Html msg)
    slides =
        [ Html.div [] [ Html.text "one" ], Html.div [] [ Html.text "two" ] ]

    view :
        { state : Carousel.State, opts : Carousel.Options msg }
        -> Element.Element msg
    view model =
        Carousel.view Theme.default
            model.opts
            (Carousel.resize model.opts { width = 1000, height = 400 } (Carousel.init model.opts 2))
            slides

The DOM is Naive UI's own: the root `div.n-carousel` (the 8 `--n-*` vars),
the `div.n-carousel__slides` track (`transition-duration` + `transform`), the
`div.n-carousel__slide` options (`--current` / `--prev` / `--next`), the
`div.n-carousel__dots` tablist, and the `div.n-carousel__arrow-group` pair.
`css/naive-ui.css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Rendering strategy (settled).** The whole carousel is ONE raw `Html` tree
wrapped in a single `Element.html`. The cssr owns the track's `display:flex`
(and `flex-direction:column` under `--vertical`); an elm-ui Element would emit
competing inline layout styles, and there is no public `Element -> Html`.
Consequence: slides are `List (Html msg)` (upstream slides are arbitrary
vnode content; the `NCarouselItem` scoped-slot flags are exposed as the pure
`slideInfo` helper instead).

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream drives a `setInterval` clock, rAF mount
flag, `document`-level drag listeners, `ResizeObserver` measurement, focus and
capture-phase click suppression. This library is pure, so the port exposes the
render surface and the pure `State -> State` mirrors; the host app owns the
effects (the same service/caller pattern `NUI.Upload` uses for XHR):

  - **Autoplay**: caller `Time.every interval` -> `next` while
    `env.autoplayEnabled`; root hover pauses via `onRootMouseEnter` /
    `onRootMouseLeave`.
  - **Measurement**: `resize` feeds the measured INNER container size
    (upstream `calculateSize(innerOnly=true)`), `setSlideSizes` feeds the
    per-slide sizes in `'auto'` mode. Examples/tests feed fixed sizes so the
    static DOM is deterministic.
  - **Drag**: caller subscribes to document move/end, decodes points with
    `decodeDragPoint`, and calls `dragMove` / `dragEnd`. `wheel`,
    `dotKeyAction`, `indexChange`, `slideInfo` are the remaining pure ports.

**Accepted divergences (documented edges):**

1.  No Vue `<Transition>` machinery: `transitionProps` is dropped; `effect:
    custom` hides inactive slides with `display: none` (no enter/leave
    classes).
2.  Measurement, timer, focus management, capture-phase click suppression and
    the `globalDragging` singleton are caller-side.
3.  `transitionStyle` is narrowed to the two keys upstream `keep()`s
    (`transitionDuration` + optional `transitionTimingFunction`).
4.  `prevSlideStyle` / `nextSlideStyle` accept the **string** form only
    (upstream also allows a CSSProperties object; `normalizeStyle` joins it —
    strings cover the typed use).
5.  The `isMounted` rAF flag is caller-set state (`markMounted`); static output
    matches upstream SSR (fade/card slides carry no transition props until
    mounted).

**Oracle round (`tasks/recon/carousel-oracle.md`) — 4 S findings fixed here:**

  - `[oracle S1]` usercontrol renders `wrapper div > div.n-carousel__slide`
    (upstream maps the ITEM vnodes into plain wrappers,
    `Carousel.tsx:1035-1043`); `vShow`'s `display: none` lives on the inner
    item, and BOTH usercontrol styles are the early-return branch — size
    only, no margin.
  - `[oracle S2]` `dragEnd`'s flick branch reproduces Vue's ASYNC
    `realIndex` watcher (`flush: 'pre'`): the sync `fixTranslate` runs first,
    the queued watcher body lands after it — the final translate is the
    loop-jump clone target, `transitionend` snaps back to the real slide.
  - `[oracle S3]` the track carries NO style attribute for non-sequence
    effects (upstream `translateStyleRef` stays `{}`); the live drag translate
    is sequence-only (`Carousel.tsx:657`).
  - `[oracle S4]` `onSlideClick` fires on the card-effect gate
    (`allowClick && effect=='card' && !isRealActive`, `Carousel.tsx:565-577`);
    the listener is attached only when the gate passes (the closed gate emits
    nothing either way; the `preventDefault` suppression half is caller-side).

Non-divergences worth noting: controlled usage is supported exactly as
upstream (`opts.currentIndex` wins over `state.displayIndex` via
`useMergedState`; route the same events through `to`). `to`'s upper clamp is
`totalView` (not `-1`) upstream — faithful, harmless (re-clamped by
`toRealIndex`).

**Port-surface notes (vs `tasks/recon/carousel-2-elm.md` §3):**

  - `init` takes `Options` + the slide count so the `defaultIndex` seed follows
    the evident INTENT (pins §A6): `displayIndex =
    getDisplayIndex(getRealIndex(defaultIndex, duplicatedable), totalView,
    duplicatedable)` with the TRUE total view. Upstream seeds during setup
    with `slideElsRef` still empty (`totalView` 1 -> every `defaultIndex`
    lands on display 0); nothing re-seeds it post-mount. The port documents the
    upstream setup-order quirk and pins the intended semantics.
  - `State` carries the slide count (`slideCount`) so the navigation functions
    (`to` / `prev` / `next` / `transitionEnd` / `dragEnd` / …) stay
    self-contained; `envOf` still takes the count explicitly (its documented
    signature) and internal callers pass `state.slideCount`.
  - `applyIndexChange` (the `realIndex` watcher body) takes the watcher's
    `lastRealIndex` as an extra `Int`: Vue reactivity supplies it upstream and
    there is no pure equivalent otherwise.
  - `dragEnd` takes the elapsed drag time (`Float` ms) — upstream reads
    `Date.now()`, which is a runtime concern.
  - `getLastViewTranslate`'s "auto" gate is upstream's NARROW
    `displaySlidesPerView == auto` (`Carousel.tsx:480`) — NOT `Env.autoSlideSize`.
    Consequence: `centeredSlides + slidesPerView:auto` (displaySpv forced to 1)
    takes the numeric branch `translates[totalView - 1]`. Pins §A4 re-derived
    from bytes and CORRECTED (1500, not 900 — orchestrator re-check vs
    Carousel.tsx:186-189, 478-497; the feat lane had flagged the divergence).
  - Inline style strings: the root uses the house `NUI.Internal.renderVars`
    form (joined `k:v` with `;`, no spaces); the track/slide styles mirror
    upstream Vue's serialization (`key: value; key: value`) since they are the
    byte-fidelity contract's target. `[oracle D]` The inline-theme `themeClass`
    is never emitted (house-wide).

Upstream refs: `carousel/src/Carousel.tsx` (props :73-146, `.tsx` state
machinery :156-894, render :1000-1063), `CarouselItem.tsx`,
`CarouselDots.tsx:27-94`, `CarouselArrow.tsx:6-33`,
`utils/duplicatedLogic.ts`, `utils/index.ts:20-37`,
`styles/index.cssr.ts`.

trigger, the `NUI.Select` lane) plus the multi-column menu body, exactly

    import Cascader exposing (Option(..), defaults)

    Cascader.view theme
        { defaults | multiple = True }
        [ Option
            { value = "drive"
            , label = "Drive"
            , disabled = False
            , children =

                        { value = "car"
                        , label = "Car"
                        , disabled = False
                        , children = Nothing
                        }

value flows out through the menus' `onToggle`, not a trigger field.

         per the module docs — path labels, fallback keys, tag slicing)

      style = 17 vars → --n-menu-mask-color

      │    │    style = getColumnStyle level (iff columnStyle)

      │    │        └─ div.n-cascader-option [--pending] [--disabled]
      │    │                       [--show-prefix]             — per option
      │    │            ├─ div.n-cascader-option__prefix      — iff showCheckbox
      │    │            │    > NCheckbox{checked, indeterminate, disabled,
      │    │            │        focusable=false}             — inert (below)
      │    │            ├─ span.n-cascader-option__label {label}
      │    │            └─ div.n-cascader-option__suffix
      │    │                 > div.n-cascader-option-icon-placeholder
      │    │                     > branch: NBaseLoading(scale .85, strokeWidth 24,
      │    │                       show=isLoading) > arrow | placeholder
      │    │                       > leaf: checkmark iff checkStrategy = Child
      │    │                         && !(multiple && cascade) — with the
      │    │                         fade-in-scale-up phase class
      │    └─ div.n-base-menu-mask {mask}                     — iff mask
      ├─ div.n-cascader-menu__empty {empty | NUI.Empty}      — iff column 0 empty
      ├─ div.n-cascader-menu-action [data-action]            — iff action
      └─ div[width:0;height:0][tabindex 0]                   — NFocusDetector, inert

Select menu (`selectMenu`) DOM — the filterable flat body (`showSelectMenu`
upstream = `filterable && pattern /= ""`; the caller mounts this instead of
`menu`): the `NUI.SelectMenu` root carrying `extraClasses =
["n-cascader", …]`… exactly `["n-cascader-menu", transition?]`, the merged
`selectMenuVars` (23 + 17, last-wins superset — the `NUI.Select.menu`
precedent) and `focusable = False` (upstream passes no `focusable`).

Caller-owned runtime (the port-wide convention): show state and follower
positioning (mount the body in your own positioned wrapper), the
`fade-in-scale-up-transition` phases, keyboard navigation (`keyboardKey`)
and hover expansion (`hoverKey` — its path is what paints `--pending`),
`pattern` + `onPatternInput` (filtering runs through `filterOptions`),
`remote`/`onLoad` orchestration (`loadingKeys` paints the per-option
spinners; the option tree itself is the loaded state, so treemate's
`SubtreeNotLoadedError` and `allowCheckingNotLoaded` are moot), the mask's
`showOnce` timing (render `mask` while the message shows; its
`fade-in-transition` classes are not driven), `autoPending` and the select
menu's keyboard `prev`/`next`/`enter` (inject `--pending` through the flat
rows' `attributes` — the `NUI.SelectMenu` seam), the responsive
`maxTagCount` overflow and its preview popover (numeric is the static seam
here, as in `NUI.Select`), `ellipsisTagPopoverProps`, form-item
size/disabled/status merging, IME, `onFocus`/`onBlur`/`onTabout`, column
scrolling, `virtualScroll`'s windowing (`virtual` only adds the
`--virtual` width class; the full column renders).

Not ported: `renderLabel` / `renderPrefix` / `renderSuffix` / `arrow`-
adjacent custom render slots beyond `arrow` itself; `leafOnly` /
`onChange` (deprecated upstream); `valueField` / `labelField` /
`childrenField` / `disabledField` (fixed record names — the
`NUI.SelectMenu` limitation); a custom `filter` (pass pre-built flat rows
to `selectMenu` instead of `filterOptions`' output); treemate group /
ignored nodes. The checkbox renders states only: Elm has no
`stopPropagation` hook (the `NUI.Tabs` note), so a wired checkbox would
double-fire with the row's own `onToggle` — branch checks arrive through
the row click instead. `Cascader.Size` is upstream's three-size scale (no
`tiny`); the menu carries no size variant (heights flow through the vars),
and neither body has an `rtl.cssr` upstream (the trigger's `rtl` rides
`NUI.BaseSelection`).

values.comment:
Upstream `doCheck`'s multiple branch — treemate's `check`: the key's
subtree joins the checked set, then the strategy normalization runs. The
result list IS the new value (upstream writes it straight through
`doUpdateValue`).

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults (`size: 'medium'` via the form/config merge,
`showPath` / `cascade` on, `checkStrategy: 'all'`, `separator: ' / '`,
placeholder = the en-US locale `'Please Select'`, `value = Single Nothing`
= null, `bordered` on via the config default; everything else `False` /
empty — upstream declares those booleans `undefined` (inert, only
truthy-checked) rather than `false`, which `False` matches).

values.name: filterOptions
values.comment:
Upstream's default filter pipeline (`createSelectOptions` + the default
`filter`): the tree flattens root-first (disabled nodes never list), each
non-disabled node becoming a row under `All` / `Parent` and each leaf only
under `Child` (upstream `isLeaf || !checkStrategyIsChild`), labeled with
its path label; a non-empty pattern keeps the rows whose PATH contains the
needle (case-insensitive substring on any non-empty node label — the row
label itself is never matched).

values.name: getCheckedKeys
values.comment:
treemate's `getCheckedKeys` — normalize raw keys against the tree. With
`cascade`, each key extends to its whole enabled subtree and the parents
aggregate bottom-up (`indeterminateKeys` collects the partial ones);
`checkStrategy` then collapses the result (`All` keeps every level,
`Parent` the topmost checked ancestor, `Child` leaf levels only — exactly
treemate's synthetic-set walk). Without `cascade` the keys pass through
`merge` / `minus` semantics and nothing is indeterminate.
values.type: Basics.Bool -> NUI.Cascader.CheckStrategy -> List.List String.String -> List.List NUI.Cascader.Option -> NUI.Cascader.CheckResult

values.name: menuVars

The 17 `--n-*` custom properties both menu roots carry (upstream
`cssVarsRef`, declaration order — the same set rides the flat select menu
through the follower's style merge). `--n-menu-mask-color` is

values.comment:
The filterable flat body — the `NUI.SelectMenu` root carrying the
`n-cascader-menu` class (its `.n-cascader-menu` rules apply to this root
too), the transition phase, and the merged `selectMenuVars` superset.

name: NUI.Checkbox
comment:
Naive UI's `Checkbox`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Checkbox exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Checkbox.view theme NUI.Checkbox.defaults
        [ Element.text "Banana" ]

    NUI.Checkbox.view theme
        { defaults
            | checked = True
            , onCheck = Just Toggled
        }
        [ Element.text "Apple" ]

The list of child elements is the label slot (`naive-ui`'s default slot / `label`
prop); when it is empty no label element is rendered and the component shows only
the box.

`privateInsideTable` is upstream's internal prop of the same name — a pure class
effect (`n-checkbox--inside-table`, emitted between `--indeterminate` and
`--show-label`) with no theme-var story, set by the data table's header and body
checkboxes. `onCheckEvent` carries the salient bits of upstream's
`onUpdateChecked(value, e)` — `(checked, shiftKey)` — which the data table's
shift-click range selection needs; it wins over `onCheck` when both are set.

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-checkbox` BEM
classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's
exact CSS.

name: NUI.Code
comment:
Naive UI's `Code` (`n-code`), rebuilt as a pure renderer over a caller-supplied highlight.js (`Hljs`). import NUI.Code as Code hljs : Code.Hljs hljs = { getLanguage = (== "javascript") , highlight = \code _ -> "" ++ code ++ "" } Code.view theme { Code.defaults | code = "const x = 1", language = Just "javascript", hljs = Just hljs } [] The visual result is Naive UI's own: the root carries the `.n-code` BEM classes and Naive UI's 15 `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. Highlighting needs `highlight.js` injected — this port never ships it; the caller passes the same two methods upstream consumes (`getLanguage`, `highlight`). **Raw-Html root (the `NUI.Highlight` / `NUI.Carousel` precedent).** Upstream's root is a plain `` whose children are inserted imperatively (`innerHTML` / `textContent` / a `pre.__code__`); the port reproduces that DOM as ONE raw `Html` tree, so `view` returns an `Element` only through `Element.html` and its `attributes` field is a `List (Html.Attribute msg)` (an `Element.Attribute` cannot attach to a raw node). **⚠ `[D]` Raw HTML is parsed, not injected.** `Code.tsx` embeds the highlighter's output with `el.innerHTML = html`; elm/html blocks that path — the VirtualDom kernel remaps the `innerHTML` property key (`_VirtualDom_noInnerHtmlOrFormAction`) and `setAttribute "innerHTML"` is a no-op. The port instead runs the SAME resolved string through `NUI.Internal.RawHtml.nodes`, a pure parser of the highlight.js / KaTeX output shapes (its grammar and recovery semantics are docstringed there). Real highlight.js output containing `` markup therefore renders as elements, faithfully; the class / style / line-number structure stays byte-faithful. (Recon-2 §5(b) claimed `HA.property "innerHTML"` works; empirically it does not.) **Static image of `setCode`.** Upstream writes the code content imperatively on mount; there is no pure render path for it. `view` therefore emits the state `setCode` would settle into (the decision tree of `Code.tsx:62-108`), which is also what the DOM probes assert: - a caller `children` list (Log's slot path) short-circuits `setCode` (`Code.tsx:63`) — the line-numbers `
` is rendered, then the children
    untouched;
  - otherwise `inline` puts the highlighted string as the `` root's
    children (parsed — `[D]`), or the plain code as a text node
    (`textContent`);
  - the block form renders the line-numbers `
` then a `pre.__code__`
    carrying the highlighted string (parsed — `[D]`) or the plain code as
    text (`textContent`).

**Caller-owned runtime.** The `uri` / `inline` / `wordWrap` / `showLineNumbers`
/ `internalFontSize` / `internalNoHighlight` props are all modelled exactly;
`internalFontSize` / `internalNoHighlight` exist only for `NUI.Log`'s embedding
(Log passes `Just fontSize` + `True`). `internalNoHighlight` makes the port skip
highlighting entirely (LogLine does its own per-line highlight).

**Divergences (`[D]`):**

  - `[D]` URI decode: upstream `window.decodeURIComponent(props.code)` THROWS on
    a malformed string (an uncaught crash). `Url.percentDecode` returns
    `Nothing`; the port falls back to the RAW string.
  - `[D]` `lineNumbers` runs over the RAW `props.code`, **not** the URI-decoded
    string (`Code.tsx:172-189` uses `props.code`; `setCode` decodes a local).
    This upstream quirk is kept.
  - `[D]` `themeClass` (the `useThemeClass` inline-theme handle) is never emitted
    (house-wide: the port has no `inlineThemeDisabled`).
  - `[D]` `codeHtml`'s "language" is `Maybe String`; upstream's
    `!(language && hljs.getLanguage(language))` treats an EMPTY string as "no
    language" (`Code.tsx:49-50`), so `Just ""` returns `Nothing` here too.

name: NUI.ColorPicker
comment:
Naive UI's `ColorPicker` — a colour trigger (`view`) plus a caller-mounted
placeholder panel (`panel`): the 2-D S/V square, a hue rail and an optional
alpha rail, an optional 30×30 preview with the native `<input type="color">`,
the numeric mode inputs (an `NInputGroup` of small `NInput`s) and an optional
swatch grid, then the action / undo-redo rows.

    import NUI.ColorPicker as ColorPicker

    ColorPicker.view theme
        { ColorPicker.defaultOptions
            | value = Just model.color
            , onUpdateShow = Just (\_ -> ShowPanel)
        }

    -- the body is a separate element — mount it yourself when `show`
    ColorPicker.panel theme
        { ColorPicker.defaultOptions | value = Just model.color }

Trigger (`view`) DOM:

    div.n-color-picker [--disabled]                       ← the 10 --n-* vars
      └─ div.n-color-picker__fill
         ├─ div.n-color-picker-checkboard
         ├─ div (absolute, background-color = hsla string or unset)
         └─ div.n-color-picker__value (white/black via getWCAGContrast)

Panel (`panel`) DOM:

    div.n-color-picker-panel [fade-in-scale-up-transition class] [tabindex 0]
      ├─ div.n-color-picker-control
      │   ├─ div.n-color-picker-pallete (2 gradient layers + optional handle)
      │   ├─ div.n-color-picker-preview
      │   │   ├─ div.n-color-picker-preview__sliders (hue rail + optional alpha)
      │   │   └─ div.n-color-picker-preview__preview (optional)
      │   ├─ div.n-color-picker-input (__mode label + NInputGroup of units)
      │   └─ div.n-color-picker-swatches (optional)
      ├─ div.n-color-picker-action (actions confirm/clear, optional)
      ├─ div.n-color-picker-action (actionSlot's custom row — or, when no
      │   slot is given, the internalActions undo/redo row; the slot wins)
      └─ the inert focus detector (last child)

`show`, closing and positioning stay caller-owned (the `NUI.DatePicker`
convention): the trigger emits `onUpdateShow True`; the panel never emits a
show/closing message — a confirm/clear emits ONE message (`onConfirm`/`onClear`
when set, else the committed value on `onUpdateValue`) and the caller closes.

**`[oracle D]` divergences (documented, not bugs):**

1.  **clickoutside-capture → focus detector.** Upstream closes via a
    `clickoutside` directive in the capture phase (`ColorPicker.tsx:745-759`);
    the port instead appends the house inert focus-detector sentinel as the
    panel's last child (`DatePicker.elm:1303-1305`) and leaves closing to the
    caller.

2.  **named-colour swatches.** Upstream resolves a bare colour name with a
    canvas (`ColorPickerSwatches.tsx:20-26`); the port uses the static 149-entry
    seemly table (`NUI.Internal.Color`), so CSS _system_ colours that a canvas
    could resolve fall back to `'#000000'`, and a name resolves to that table's
    hex form (e.g. `red` → `#F00`) rather than a canvas' `#ff0000`.

3.  **undo/redo stack is caller-owned.** Upstream keeps `undoStackRef`/
    `valueIndexRef` as runtime state (`ColorPicker.tsx:322-324, 518-530`); the
    port takes `undoable`/`redoable` flags and `onUndo`/`onRedo` msgs.

4.  **`normalizeHue` clamps `360 → 359`** (upstream `utils.ts:99` vs seemly
    `roundDeg`'s `360 → 0`). Kept as-is; both live in `NUI.Internal.Color`.

5.  The cssr header comment (`styles/index.cssr.ts:5-13`) lists only 9 vars —
    it omits `--n-border`; the port emits all 10 (the actual `cssVarsRef` set).

6.  Upstream's `slots.default` is declared but never read (`ColorPicker.tsx:
    143`); it has no port counterpart.

7.  **No pointer-drag wiring in the view.** Upstream binds document
    `mousemove`/`mouseup` on `mousedown` and reads `getBoundingClientRect`
    (`Pallete.tsx:34-52`, `HueSlider.tsx:36-60`, `AlphaSlider.tsx:35-58`);
    the port emits an `onMousedown PointerPress` signal (area + press
    coordinates + the pressed surface's size and viewport origin, all read
    synchronously inside the event decoder, so a press commits immediately
    the way upstream's `handleMouseDown` does) and exports the pure geometry
    (`svFromPoint`, `hueFromPoint`, `alphaFromPoint`) for the caller to run
    against that captured rect. The surfaces' purely visual children
    (gradient layers, handles, the alpha checkboard rail) carry
    `pointer-events: none` so a press always targets the surface itself —
    upstream's rect read is target-independent (`railRef`, absolute
    `clientX`), while the port's `offsetX` is target-relative and would
    skew by the child's own offset. The `pointerAreaIds` seam still puts
    inert `id`s on the three drag surfaces (test anchors / caller
    instrumentation), and the panel-root `attributes` seam (raw `Html`
    attributes, appended after the component's own) carries e.g. an `id`
    for the whole panel.

8.  **Unit inputs commit on input, not on change.** Upstream `ColorInputUnit`
    parses on `change`/blur (`ColorInputUnit.tsx:112-163`); the port's embedded
    `NInput` has no change seam, so `onUnitInput index raw` fires per keystroke
    and the caller normalizes with the exported unit normalizers.

9.  **`padding: 0 4px` on the unit inputs** — upstream passes
    `builtinThemeOverrides.inputThemeOverrides` (`ColorInputUnit.tsx:46-48,
    157`) to the embedded `NInput`; the port threads it through
    `Input.varOverrides` (`[ ( "--n-padding-left", "4px" ), ( "--n-padding-right", "4px" ) ]`
    — the vars upstream's theme-peers chain lands in), so the unit inputs
    carry the narrow padding.

10. **panel `ondragstart` `preventDefault` is not ported** (`ColorPicker.tsx`
    `renderPanel`): `elm/html` cannot `preventDefault` without a message seam.

11. **Swatch keyboard select (Enter) is not ported** (`ColorPickerSwatches.tsx:
    94-97`); `elm/html` has no `onKeyDown`, and a decoder seam would need a
    no-op message. Swatches stay clickable and focusable.

12. **Upstream's `onComplete` has no port option.** Upstream fires it after a
    drag mouse-up and after an input commit (`ColorPicker.tsx` `handleComplete`);
    both moments are caller-owned here (drag runs via `onMousedown` + the pure
    geometry helpers, input commits via `onUnitInput`), so the caller fires its
    own complete — an option the panel could never trigger would be dead
    config.

13. **Displayed H/α/S/V are value-derived per render.** Upstream keeps
    `displayedHueRef`/`displayedAlphaRef`/`displayedSvRef` resynced to the
    parsed value on change (`ColorPicker.tsx:322-324, 531-545`); the port
    derives them from `value` each render (identical steady state; during a
    drag the caller owns it, see 7). Consequence: `defaultOptions.displayedMode
    = Rgb` matches upstream's computed default only while `value` is unset —
    with a `value`, upstream derives the mode from it (`ColorPicker.tsx:
    234-236`), so set `displayedMode` alongside `value`.

14. **Peer theme overrides are not plumbed.** Upstream threads
    `mergedTheme.peers.Input`/`peers.Button` into the embedded unit inputs and
    action buttons (`ColorInputUnit.tsx:155-156`); the port reads
    `NUI.Theme.Input`/`NUI.Theme.Button` directly (the `NUI.DatePicker`
    precedent).

15. **The panel root carries `tabindex 0`** (house overlay convention,
    `DatePicker.elm:1145`, pairing with 1); upstream `renderPanel` has none.

16. **The trigger colour layer omits the empty `background-color`** upstream
    always emits when the value is mode-less (`backgroundColor: hsla ? … : ''`,
    `ColorPickerTrigger.tsx:47-55`) — visual no-op, the attribute string
    differs.

17. **`getWCAGContrast` exposes only the default-args form**
    (`contrastColor = [255, 255, 255]`, `level = 'AA'`; `utils.ts:58-61`) —
    the only call site (the trigger label) uses the defaults.

18. **`deriveDefaultValue`'s `__DEV__` warn is dropped** (`utils.ts:38-39`) —
    a dev-only `console.warn`, no-op in production.

aliases.name: PointerPress
aliases.comment:
The drag surface a `onMousedown` signal came from, with the press
geometry read synchronously inside the event decoder:

  - `x`/`y` — the pointer relative to the pressed surface (offsetX/Y;
    exactly upstream's `e.clientX - rect.left` against a fresh
    `getBoundingClientRect`)
  - `width`/`height` — the surface's size (currentTarget.clientWidth/Height)
  - `left`/`top` — the surface's viewport origin (clientX − offsetX), so the
    caller can convert later `mousemove` client coords without any DOM read

Everything the geometry helpers need rides on the event itself — a press
commits in the same tick (upstream `Pallete.tsx handleMouseDown` calls
`handleMouseMove(e)` on press; a click without any move still selects) and
drags track per-frame with zero layout reads.
