values.name: remove
values.comment:
Splice the item out — call it on after-leave (upstream
`handleAfterLeave` removes by key once the modal's leave transition ends).
This is what empties the container DOM.

values.name: success
values.comment: `useDialog().success(options)` — kind stamped after the options.

values.comment:
The queue rendered: one full modal tree per item (upstream's Fragment of

name: NUI.Drawer
comment:
Naive UI's `Drawer` — the mount-body **sibling** of `NUI.Modal`: like Modal
it renders its own fixed full-viewport tree (no trigger/follower), but the
body is **edge-anchored** (`.n-drawer` is `position: absolute` pinned to a
side by `placement`, sized on the placement's axis) instead of flex-centred.
Upstream `Drawer.tsx` orchestrates `DrawerBodyWrapper.tsx` (the component
named `NDrawerContent` in its `name` field — the body wrapper) whose default
slot receives `DrawerContent.tsx` (the inner header/body/footer unit):

    div.n-drawer-container (role=none, the 25 css vars [+ z-index])
      div.n-drawer-mask (aria-hidden) [--invisible]      — iff showMask ≠ Hidden
      div role=none (unclassed host)                      — the body gate
        div.n-drawer [--rtl --{p}-placement] role=dialog aria-modal
          div.n-drawer__resize-trigger [--hover]          — iff resizable
          (content wrapper — see nativeScrollbar below)
            the caller's content (usually `NUI.DrawerContent`)

    import NUI.Drawer as Drawer
    import NUI.DrawerContent as DrawerContent
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Drawer.view Theme.default
        { Drawer.defaults | show = True }
        [ DrawerContent.view Theme.default
            { DrawerContent.defaults
                | title = Just (Element.text "Title")
                , closable = True
            }
            [ Element.text "Content" ]
        ]

**Everything runtime is caller-owned** (the popover-family precedent, applied
to the mount-body family — upstream provides the `*BodyInjectionKey`s, it
consumes nothing):

  - **Mounting and `show`.** The caller decides where the tree lives and owns
    the show state (`displayDirective: 'if'` semantics only). `show = False`
    with no leave phase renders a bare container — unmount the view when fully
    closed; the keep-mounted `display: none` variant is not modelled
    (caller `attributes` can carry it).
  - **Transitions.** The mask (`fade-in-transition`) and the body
    (`slide-in-from-{placement}-transition`, derived from `placement`) run on
    the same clock the caller drives: pass the phase through
    `maskTransition`/`bodyTransition` and keep the view mounted while either
    is a leave phase (`I.isLeavePhase`). The mask/body nodes render only while
    `show || isLeavePhase …`. Upstream timings: mask `.2s`; body enter `.3s`,
    leave `.2s` (fixed beziers, not the `--n-bezier-*` vars — unlike the
    mask, which reads `--n-bezier-in/out`). The body phase class is forced
    **last** on `.n-drawer`'s class list (the house invariant).
  - **Mask clicks ARE interactive** (the divergence from `NUI.Modal`, whose
    fixed body-wrapper overlays an inert mask): upstream's mask carries
    `onClick=handleMaskClick` (`Drawer.tsx` — `.n-drawer` is out of flow, so
    the zero-height body host does not cover it). Pass `onMaskClick` for the
    primary close surface; `maskClosable` reduces to "pass your close msg".
    Esc (`closeOnEsc`), focus trap, `blockScroll` and the `clickoutside`
    (only when the mask is hidden) stay caller runtime.
  - **Resizable drag.** The trigger node (`resizable = True`) and its
    `--hover` modifier (`showResizeTriggerHover`) are DOM; the drag itself
    (global mousemove/mouseup, min/max clamping, `--unselectable` while
    dragging) is caller runtime — set `unselectable` while your drag is
    active to reproduce upstream.
  - **z-index.** No `zindexable` auto-increment: pass `zIndex` (rendered as
    `z-index` appended after the vars).

**`showMask`** is upstream's `boolean | 'transparent'`: `Visible` (the
default) renders the mask, `Transparent` renders it with
`n-drawer-mask--invisible`, `Hidden` omits the node entirely.

**`nativeScrollbar`** (upstream default **true**) selects the content seam:
`True` renders a plain `div.n-drawer-content-wrapper` (no scrollbar node —
unlike `NUI.Modal`, the default tree embeds no `NUI.Scrollbar`); `False`
embeds `NUI.Scrollbar` with `contentClass = "n-drawer-content-wrapper "` +
your `contentClass`. **Sizing**: `width` (left/right) / `height`
(top/bottom) resolve per axis with the `defaultWidth`/`defaultHeight`
fallback (upstream `251`), emitted as the single inline `style` on
`.n-drawer` (exact upstream pin: `width: 600px;`). Upstream's deprecated
`drawerStyle`/`drawerClass` and the `scrollbarProps` escape hatch are not
modelled; `attributes` is the container passthrough (the `NUI.Modal` house
rule — upstream's `$attrs` land on `.n-drawer` instead).

`NUI.DrawerContent` is the composition unit (upstream `NDrawerContent`) — see
its module. Upstream has no `preset` prop (Modal's `Preset` has no analog
here): the slot is the third `view` argument.

name: NUI.DrawerContent
comment:
Naive UI's `NDrawerContent` (upstream `DrawerContent.tsx`) — the drawer's
composition unit: the header/body/footer content rendered inside the drawer's
content wrapper (`NUI.Drawer`'s slot). Upstream `NDrawer`'s default slot
typically receives exactly this component:

    import NUI.Drawer as Drawer
    import NUI.DrawerContent as DrawerContent
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Drawer.view Theme.default
        { Drawer.defaults | show = True }
        [ DrawerContent.view Theme.default
            { DrawerContent.defaults
                | title = Just (Element.text "Title")
                , closable = True
            }
            [ Element.text "Body" ]
        ]

    div.n-drawer-content [--native-scrollbar]
      div.n-drawer-header [headerClass] (role=none)     — iff header/title/closable
        div.n-drawer-header__main role=heading aria-level=1   {header || title}
        div.n-base-close.n-base-close--absolute.n-drawer-header__close — iff closable
      (body — see nativeScrollbar below)
        div.n-drawer-body-content-wrapper [bodyContentClass]   {default slot}
      div.n-drawer-footer [footerClass] (role=none)    — iff footer slot

**Body seam** (`nativeScrollbar`, upstream default **true** — mirrors
`NUI.Drawer`'s own content seam): `True` renders
`div.n-drawer-body > div.n-drawer-body-content-wrapper` (plain divs, no
scrollbar node); `False` embeds `NUI.Scrollbar` with the class
`n-drawer-body` **on the scrollbar root** (via its `extraClasses` seam, not a
wrapper) and `contentClass = "n-drawer-body-content-wrapper "` + your
`bodyContentClass` — content nodes are then grandchildren of the scrollbar
content (`NUI.Scrollbar`'s `display: contents` wrapper). Upstream quirk kept
faithful: in the scrollbar branch `bodyClass`/`bodyStyle` are **not** applied
(upstream passes only the static `n-drawer-body` class there), and the
`scrollbarProps` escape hatch is not modelled.

**Close button.** `closable = True` renders the header close button
(`n-base-close n-base-close--absolute n-drawer-header__close`, the
`NUI.Card` inline-close precedent); pass `onClose` for its message (upstream
wires it to `doUpdateShow(false)` unconditionally). `aria-level` is pinned
to `1`, matching upstream's render.

The `*Class`/`*Style` fields are upstream's `headerClass`/`headerStyle`/
`bodyClass`/`bodyStyle`/`bodyContentClass`/`bodyContentStyle`/`footerClass`/
`footerStyle` props (`Nothing` = omitted).

flex-direction: column` and `.n-drawer-body` with `flex: 1 0 0; overflow:
hidden` — the footer stays anchored and the body absorbs the remaining panel
height. The port's elm-ui nodes carry `min-height: min-content` (the `.s.c >
.s` rule; the bridge restores only `flex-basis`), which blocks every level
from shrinking and pushes the footer past a height-constrained panel edge.
The inline `min-height: 0` (port-first, caller style after — the caller wins)
restores upstream's sizing on the native path.

name: NUI.Dropdown
comment:
Naive UI's `Dropdown` — the `n-dropdown-menu` body. Upstream the component
is the popover runtime with the body swapped (`internalRenderBody`,
`Dropdown.tsx`): the popover contributes the trigger/show/positioning machinery,
the shared classes (`n-popover-shared` + overlap/arrow modifiers) and half the
CSS vars; the dropdown contributes the menu DOM, the `n-dropdown` /
`n-dropdown--{size}-size` markers and its own theme vars.

    import NUI.Dropdown as Dropdown
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Dropdown.view Theme.default
        Dropdown.defaults
        [ Dropdown.Option
            { key = "feedback"
            , label = "Feedback"
            , icon = Nothing
            , disabled = False
            , children = Nothing
            , attributes = []
            }
        , Dropdown.Divider { attributes = [] }
        ]

**Everything in `NUI.Popover`'s docstring about the caller-owned runtime
applies** — show state, trigger, delay/positioning, the `v-placement` wrapper
(use `placementAttribute`), the `--v-offset-*` note. The dropdown default
placement is `Bottom` (upstream overrides the popover's top).

**The caller-owned submenu contract** (beyond the popover's omissions):

  - Submenu open state, the 300 ms hover defer, and submenu positioning are
    yours. The port renders the (inert) `n-dropdown-offset-container` scaffold
    inside submenu options; you mount each submenu's `view` (same options, the
    children list) inside your own positioned wrapper, upstream-style in a
    `div.n-dropdown-menu-wrapper` you own. Submenus use the
    `"fade-in-scale-up-transition"` family (rules are scoped
    `.n-dropdown-menu.fade-in-scale-up-*`), the root uses
    `"popover-transition"` — hence `transition` carries the family explicitly.

**Documented gaps** (beyond the popover's):

  - `key` is required per option (upstream generates keys for keyless options);
    with duplicate keys the first match wins for `value` highlighting. Keys of
    dividers / customs never participate (upstream treemate ignores them).
  - `label`/`icon` replace upstream's `label|title` + render hooks;
    `renderLabel`/`renderIcon`/`renderOption`/`nodeProps`/`menuProps` become
    per-option `attributes` (they land on the option body, upstream's
    `option.props`), the `Custom` variant, and root `attributes`. `extra` /
    `titleExtra` (Menu features) and the `labelField`/`keyField`/
    `childrenField` overrides are not modelled.
  - `onSelect` fires on leaf clicks (non-disabled, non-submenu); closing the
    menu afterwards is your model change (upstream closes automatically).
  - Pending (hover) option state is runtime — inject
    `n-dropdown-option-body--pending` classes via the option's `attributes`.
  - `keyboard` navigation, `show === false` filtering (just omit the option),
    and group-in-group (dropped, as upstream nulls it) are not modelled.
  - Derived colours (`optionColorActive` = `changeColor(primary, …)`) are
    pinned literals in `NUI.Theme.Dropdown` — computed at the default theme;
    a `common` override does not re-derive them (toolchain convention, cf. Tag).
  - The submenu chevron SVG is inlined here (house style, cf. `NUI.Collapse`).

name: NUI.DynamicInput
comment:
Naive UI's `DynamicInput`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.DynamicInput exposing (inputDefaults, pairDefaults, removeAt)

    -- preset `input`: a list of plain strings
    NUI.DynamicInput.viewInput theme
        { inputDefaults
            | value = model.strings
            , onUpdateValue = Just SetStrings
            , onRemove = Just RemovedString
        }

    -- preset `pair`: a list of (key, value) tuples
    NUI.DynamicInput.viewPair theme
        { pairDefaults
            | value = model.pairs
            , onUpdateValue = Just SetPairs
            , showSortButton = True
        }

An empty list renders the block "Create" button; otherwise every entry renders
as a `.n-dynamic-input-item` — the preset body (one `NUI.Input` for `input`, a
key / value pair of them for `pair`) followed by
`.n-dynamic-input-item__action`, a `NUI.ButtonGroup` of circle icon buttons in
upstream's order: remove, add, and — when `showSortButton` — up (disabled on
the first entry) and down (disabled on the last). The peers (Input / Button)
render with the theme you pass in — upstream injects `theme.peers.*`, which a
pure port has no equivalent of.

**Runtime (caller-owned).** Upstream keeps the value array in a ref; here the
list lives in your model and every change reports through a message. The
`insertAt` / `removeAt` / `moveUp` / `moveDown` helpers are upstream's array
edits exposed pure, so an `onRemove`-style handler can apply them itself:

  - `onUpdateValue` — typing inside a preset input (that entry replaced —
    upstream `handleValueChange`), a create press (the new entry inserted —
    upstream `createItem`), a sort press (upstream `move`), and — when
    `onRemove` is `Nothing` — a remove press (the entry spliced out).

  - `onRemove` — a remove press when set, receiving the entry's index.
    Upstream's `remove` fires `onRemove(index)` and _then_ splices; one click
    carries one message here, so when `onRemove` is set it owns the press and
    you apply `removeAt index` yourself (when it is `Nothing` the press maps
    straight to `onUpdateValue` with the entry removed instead). The button is
    disabled under upstream's `len <= min` guard either way.

  - `onCreate` — a value producer (not a message): the entry a create press
    inserts, given the insertion index (upstream calls `onCreate(index + 1)`).
    When `Nothing`, `viewInput` inserts `""` and `viewPair` inserts
    `( "", "" )` — upstream's preset defaults.

The `min` / `max` guards are upstream's computeds: `insertionDisabled` (max
set and reached) disables the Create / add buttons, `removeDisabled`
(`len <= min`) the remove buttons. That disable is the only enforcement —
upstream's `createItem` / `remove` also no-op under the same guards before
mutating, but the pure `insertAt` / `removeAt` helpers apply unconditionally
(they are the splice itself); a caller driving them past `max` / under `min`
owns that guard. Likewise, with `onUpdateValue = Nothing` create / remove /
sort presses emit no message, so `onCreate` is never consulted on that path
(upstream invokes `onCreate(index + 1)` on every create).

**Not ported** (upstream props with no counterpart in a pure port):

  - the `default` / `action` / `create-button-default` / `create-button-icon`
    slots — the two presets ARE this port's item rendering; there is no
    render-your-own-item contract in v1;

  - `keyField`, the `globalDataKeyMap` WeakMap keys and the matching `key` /
    `data-key` attributes — they feed upstream's form injection and WeakMap
    bookkeeping, and this port has no form module;

  - form-item injection (the presets' `parentPath` / `path` props; the
    `.n-form-item` rules nested under `.n-dynamic-input` are extracted into
    the stylesheet but inert here);

  - `createButtonProps`, the deprecated `onClear` / `onInput` props, and
    `defaultValue` / uncontrolled mode (the value is caller-owned);

  - `mergedComponentProps.DynamicInput.buttonSize` — undefined by default
    upstream, so every button (Create and the action circles) is fixed at
    `medium`, `NUI.Button`'s own default (our `ButtonGroup` has no size option
    either; the size lives on the buttons);

  - the locale system — the Create label is upstream's `enUS` default,
    `"Create"`;

  - `placeholder` / `keyPlaceholder` / `valuePlaceholder` keep upstream's
    empty-string defaults as `Nothing` (an empty placeholder renders nothing
    in either).

**Markup divergences** (DOM details the port cannot reproduce exactly):

  - the pair preset wraps each of its two inputs in a
    `div.n-dynamic-input-pair-input`. Upstream puts that class on the `NInput`
    root itself; `NUI.Input.Options` has no class passthrough, so the class —
    and with it the CSS `:first-child` margin-right (and its `--rtl` flip) —
    moves to the wrapper, which carries an inline `flex: 1` to reproduce the
    geometry the `width: 100%` input root has as a shrinkable flex item
    upstream;

  - the root's custom properties keep upstream's unprefixed names —
    `--action-margin` / `--action-margin-rtl`, the only component vars without
    the `--n-` prefix — and both are emitted unconditionally, exactly like
    upstream's `cssVarsRef` (the RTL one is only read under
    `.n-dynamic-input--rtl`);

  - the extracted `.n-dynamic-input-item__action--icon` modifier
    (`cursor: pointer`) is dead CSS — upstream's default render never applies
    it either, and neither does this port;

  - root / item / wrapper elements are elm-ui elements whose flex scaffolding
    Naive UI's scoped rules override (`width`, `display`, `flex`, `margin`),
    which is this library's standard bridge.

name: NUI.DynamicTags
comment:
Naive UI's `DynamicTags`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.DynamicTags exposing (defaults)

    NUI.DynamicTags.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = [ "hello", "world" ]
            , onUpdateValue = Just SetTags
            , onActivate = Just ShowInput
            , onConfirm = Just ConfirmTag
            , onInputValue = Just SetDraft
        }
        []

The root is an `NUI.Space` (`size small`) carrying the `n-dynamic-tags` class
and the `--n-input-width` variable; one `NUI.Tag` renders per entry, followed by
the add trigger (a dashed `NUI.Button` with Naive UI's add icon) or the input.
The peers (Space / Tag / Input / Button) are rendered with the theme you pass
in — upstream injects `theme.peers.*`, which a pure port has no equivalent of.
The stylesheet's own rule `.n-dynamic-tags .n-input { min-width:
var(--n-input-width) }` constrains whichever input renders inside the root:
the built-in one or the custom input slot.

**Runtime (caller-owned).** Upstream keeps three refs — the tag list, whether
the input is showing, and the input's draft text. This library is pure, so all
three live in your model and the view reports through messages:

  - `onActivate` — the add trigger was clicked (upstream `handleAddClick`);
    set `showInput = True`.

  - `onInputValue` — the built-in input's text changed; store it in
    `inputValue`.

  - `onConfirm` — the built-in input was confirmed (Enter key or blur —
    upstream `handleInputConfirm`); append the draft, hide the input and clear
    it:
    update Confirm model =
    { model
    | tags =
    if model.draft == "" then
    model.tags

                  else
                      model.tags ++ [ model.draft ]
              , showInput = False
              , draft = ""
          }

  - `onUpdateValue` — a tag's close button was clicked (upstream
    `handleCloseClick`), receiving the full next list (the closed tag removed).

The trailing `view` argument is upstream's `input` slot: non-empty, its
elements render in place of the built-in input when `showInput = True` — you
own their events. Likewise `trigger` replaces the add button; wire its click to
whatever sets `showInput = True`. The built-in input is wrapped in a plain
element carrying the Enter / blur confirm listeners (the input component takes
no event attributes of its own).

**Not modelled** (upstream props with no pure-view counterpart): `renderTag`,
`onCreate` (the string port needs no label transform), `DynamicTagsOption`
objects (tags are plain strings), the `tagClass` / `tagStyle` / `inputClass` /
`inputStyle` / `inputProps` passthroughs, form-item disabled merging, the IME
`isCompositing` guard on Enter, `internalForceFocus`, and NSpace's
`itemStyle="display: flex;"` (our Space renders children directly, so there are
no item wrappers to style).

name: NUI.Ellipsis
comment:
Naive UI's `Ellipsis`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Ellipsis exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Ellipsis.view theme
        { defaults | lineClamp = Just 2 }
        [ Element.text "Long text that will be clamped to two lines…" ]

    NUI.Ellipsis.view theme
        { defaults | expandOnClick = True, onToggle = Just Toggle }
        [ Element.text "Click to expand or collapse" ]

The element carries the `.n-ellipsis` BEM classes and, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive
UI's exact CSS.

**State.** Upstream tracks `expanded` internally and measures the element to decide
whether a tooltip is needed; this library is pure, so the caller owns `expanded`
and the view emits the same classes and inline style upstream computes
(`text-overflow: ellipsis`, or `-webkit-line-clamp` at the clamp). Countdown-style
tooltip and cursor-measurement behavior is not reproduced.

Countdown-style measurement aside, Ellipsis declares **no** `--n-*` variables.

**Divergence (single-line clamp):** upstream's single-line mode relies on
`text-overflow: ellipsis` with `white-space: nowrap` inheriting into the slot
text. elm-ui wraps every text child in its own `div.t` and its stylesheet pins
`.s.p .t { white-space: normal }` there, so the inherited `nowrap` never
reaches the text and the paragraph wraps out to four lines. This port also
emits `-webkit-line-clamp: 1` (+ the `-webkit-inline-box` display the clamp
needs) for the same end state — one line, ellipsis glyph — through the same
mechanism the multi-line rows already use (which the `.t` wrapper cannot
defeat).

comment:
Naive UI's `Empty`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Empty exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Empty.view theme NUI.Empty.defaults []

    NUI.Empty.view theme
        { defaults
            | description = Just "Nothing here"
            , size = NUI.Empty.Huge
        }
        []

Children fill the description slot; when they are empty the `description`
option is rendered instead, falling back to Naive UI's localized default
("No Data").

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-empty` BEM
classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive
UI's exact CSS.

Empty also accepts a `huge` size, so it keeps its own `Size` instead of
`NUI.Types.Size` (and Naive UI renders no size class on the root — the size
only feeds `--n-icon-size` / `--n-font-size`).

The root fills its parent's width: upstream's `.n-empty` is a block-level flex
column (`align-items: center`), so the icon/description centre inside whatever
width the mount provides — a content-sized elm-ui root would hug the left edge
instead (the `.n-empty__icon` would left-align the whole placeholder).

name: NUI.Equation
comment:
Naive UI's `Equation` (`n-equation`), rebuilt as a pure renderer over a caller-supplied KaTeX. import NUI.Equation as Equation katex : String -> String katex value = "" ++ value ++ "" Equation.view theme { Equation.defaults | value = "E = mc^2", katex = Just katex } Upstream's `NEquation` renders the KaTeX `renderToString` output after peeling off its outer wrapper tag, then re-emitting it around the inner HTML. This port reproduces that with two module-level regexes; there is **no `n-equation` class and no stylesheet of its own** (the root IS whatever tag/class KaTeX returns, e.g. `` or `
`). **⚠ `[D]` Raw HTML is parsed, not injected.** Upstream renders the peeled KaTeX HTML with Vue's `innerHTML`; elm/html blocks that path (the VirtualDom kernel remaps the `innerHTML` key, `_VirtualDom_noInnerHtmlOrFormAction`, and `setAttribute "innerHTML"` is a no-op). The port therefore runs the SAME peeled string through `NUI.Internal.RawHtml.nodes` — a pure parser of the KaTeX (and highlight.js) output shapes, its grammar and recovery semantics docstringed there. A real KaTeX output (nested `` markup) therefore renders as elements; the outer tag/class are still reproduced from the regex peel above. (Recon-2 §5(b) claimed `HA.property "innerHTML"` works; empirically it does not.) **Caller-bound KaTeX.** Upstream resolves `props.katex || configProvider.katex` and calls `renderToString(value, { throwOnError: false, ...katexOptions })`. The port takes the already-bound closure (`katex : Maybe (String -> String)`) — the caller bakes `{ throwOnError: false, ...options }` in, exactly as that spread does (so their options OVERRIDE `throwOnError`). `Nothing` (or a falsy render) falls back to the literal `"no katex provided"`. **Theme is ignored.** `equationLight.self = () => ({})` upstream is EMPTY, so `NUI.Equation.view` takes a `Theme` only for call-site uniformity (the `NUI.Highlight` precedent). `NUI.Theme.Equation` exists with an empty `Vars` record for the same reason. **Divergences (`[D]`):** - `[D]` The `||` in `renderToString(...) || 'no katex provided'` is JS truthiness: an EMPTY render also falls back. Kept (an empty render is indistinguishable from no KaTeX over the wire). - `[D]` Elm's `Regex` has `multiline = False` by default, matching JS without the `m` flag for `^` — except JS `$` also matches before a single trailing `\n`; a KaTeX output ending in `\n` would strip differently. KaTeX does not emit a trailing newline, so the divergence is unreachable in practice. - `[D]` the inner HTML is parsed into nodes (see the injection note above). @docs Extracted, Options, defaults, extract, view

name: NUI.Flex
comment:
Naive UI's `Flex`, rebuilt on elm-ui — the flexbox primitive that supersedes
`NUI.Space`.

    import Element exposing (Element)
    import NUI.Button
    import NUI.Flex exposing (defaults)

    row : Theme -> Element msg
    row theme =
        NUI.Flex.view theme
            { defaults | justify = NUI.Flex.SpaceBetween }
            [ NUI.Button.view theme NUI.Button.defaults [ Element.text "Ok" ] ]

Naive UI's Flex ships no base stylesheet rule — it is a plain flex container
styled inline (`display`, `flex-direction`, `justify-content`, `align-items`,
`flex-wrap`, `gap`). This module reproduces exactly those declarations as inline
styles on an elm-ui `row`/`column`, so the rendered layout is pure inline
flexbox; only the RTL rule is extracted, as `.n-flex--rtl`.

name: NUI.FloatButton
comment:
Naive UI's `FloatButton`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.FloatButton exposing (defaults)

    NUI.FloatButton.view theme
        { defaults | type_ = NUI.FloatButton.Primary }
        [ Element.text "+" ]

    NUI.FloatButton.view theme
        { defaults | menuTrigger = Just NUI.FloatButton.Click }
        [ Element.text "+" ]

The element carries the `.n-float-button` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*`
custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Runtime.** The floating position, size and side offsets are caller-owned (as in
Naive UI); `showMenu` is caller-owned too — the view emits the same classes and
inline style upstream computes, and reports opening/closing through
`onUpdateShowMenu` when `menuTrigger` is set. Upstream's group (`float-button-group`)
injection and the menu's click-propagation guard are not reproduced.

name: NUI.FloatButtonGroup
comment:
Naive UI's `FloatButtonGroup`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.FloatButtonGroup exposing (defaults)

    NUI.FloatButtonGroup.view theme
        defaults
        [ NUI.FloatButton.view theme NUI.FloatButton.defaults [ Element.text "1" ] ]

    NUI.FloatButtonGroup.view theme
        { defaults
            | shape = NUI.FloatButton.Square
            , right = Just (NUI.FloatButton.Px 40)
            , bottom = Just (NUI.FloatButton.Px 40)
        }
        [ NUI.FloatButton.view theme NUI.FloatButton.defaults [ Element.text "1" ] ]

The group is Naive UI's own markup — `div.n-float-button-group` (`role="group"`)
with the `--{shape}-shape` modifier, the `--n-*` custom properties, and the
inline `position` / `left` / `right` / `top` / `bottom` Naive UI merges into the
same `style` attribute.

`NFloatButton` child follows it; `NUI.FloatButton` takes its own `shape`, so
pass the group's value to each button yourself.

`display: flex; flex-direction: column` comes from the extracted stylesheet
(which out-specifies elm-ui's own classes), and the circle shape stacks its
buttons the way a block container would — an `Element.column` root reproduces
both.

name: NUI.Form
comment:
Naive UI's `Form` + `FormItem`, rebuilt on elm-ui: a pure validation engine
plus the two views.

    import NUI.Form as Form exposing (Value(..))

    -- rules (upstream `rules` on the NFormItem)
    nameRules =
        [ { Form.defaultRule | required = True, message = Just "Name is required" }
        , { Form.defaultRule | min = Just 2, message = Just "Too short" }
        ]

    -- the item: the value is passed in already validated (see the recipe below)
    Form.item theme
        { Form.itemDefaults
            | label = Just "Name"
            , feedback = Just (String.join " " (List.map .message model.nameFeedback))
            , validation = Just model.nameFeedback
        }
        [ NUI.Input.view theme { NUI.Input.defaults | value = model.name } ]

The module has the same split as `NUI.Countdown` / `NUI.LoadingBar`: a **pure
engine** (`validateValue` / `validateForm` / `isRequired`) that returns
`Feedback`s, and the views (`view` = the `form.n-form`, `item` = one
`n-form-item`) which render what the engine produced. Upstream keeps validation
state inside the form item and validates as a side effect; here the caller owns
it — state lives in your model and transitions through your `update`.

**The caller-owned validation recipe** (upstream's blur/change wiring, made
explicit). Upstream's `NFormItem` subscribes to its child input's
`update:value` / `blur` / `focus` events and runs the matching `trigger`ed
rules, writing the result into internal state. A pure port has no such channel,
so you wire it:

1.  the input's events become `Msg`s you already own (`onInput`, `onBlur`, …);
2.  in `update`, call `validateValue (Just trigger) field rules (Just value)`
    — `OnBlur` from a blur `Msg`, `OnChange` from a change `Msg`, `Nothing` for
    a manual submit-time validate of every rule;
3.  store the returned `List Feedback` in your model (e.g.
    `{ model | nameFeedback = feedback }`);
4.  pass it back down as `ItemOptions.validation`; the item renders the
    messages and resolves the status from them.

Because the engine is pure, this composes with anything (debounce, async
lookups, cross-field rules) without a registry or provide/inject.

**Markup divergences** (DOM details the port cannot reproduce exactly):

  - `view` returns a real `<form class="n-form">`, but its children are
    `Element`s and elm-ui has no public `Element` → `Html` conversion, so each
    child is embedded through `Element.layoutWith` (with
    `Element.noStaticStyleSheet`, so the per-child _static_ stylesheet is not
    re-emitted — only elm-ui's small dynamic font sheet remains; see the note
    on `embedChild`) — a wrapper `div` carrying elm-ui's root styles. The
    wrapper gets an inline `display: contents` (so the child participates
    directly in the form's flex/grid) and inline `font` / `color: inherit`
    (best-effort neutralisation of elm-ui's class-based root font; jsdom drops
    the `font` shorthand from the serialised attribute). This mirrors
    `NUI.DynamicInput`'s pair-input wrapper: geometry preserved, one extra DOM
    node per child.

  - `item` / its label / blank / feedback wrapper are built in elm-ui /
    `Element.html` land. The item root and the blank are elm-ui elements whose
    flex scaffolding (`display: flex`) would normally fight the extracted
    stylesheet; as everywhere in this library the doubled `.nui-root.nui-root`
    scoping wins (`.n-form-item { display: grid }`), and the label / feedback
    wrapper are raw `Html` nodes so the exact tag and class strings survive.

  - `onSubmit` maps to `Html.Events.onSubmit` with **no** implicit
    `preventDefault` — upstream calls `event.preventDefault()` itself; here the
    caller decides (return a `Msg` that re-renders, or none).

**Divergences** (engine / API only; documented, not accidental):

  - the engine is the port of async-validator@4.2.5's exercised subset. Not
    ported: `asyncValidator`, `transform`, `defaultField` / nested fields,
    `renderMessage`, `first`, nested rule trees, the `validateMessages`
    override, and the `url` / `email` / `date` / `method` / `regexp` /
    `integer` / `float` / `object` / `hex` types (and `pattern`-as-a-type).

  - no form-item registry and no provide/inject cascade: the item's `size`,
    `disabled`, `showLabel`, `showFeedback`, … are not inherited from a parent
    form, no input is told to validate on blur/change, there is no path
    watch/restore and no `ignorePathChange`. `validateForm` is the pure analog
    of upstream's `form.validate`.

  - `pattern` uses elm/regex; an **uncompilable** source makes the rule FAIL
    with `rule.message` (fallback `"Validation error on field %s"`) instead of
    upstream's runtime throw — fail loudly, in band.

  - `LabelWidth` has no `'auto'` (upstream measures the widest child label in
    the DOM); only `Px Int` / `Custom String` are ported.

  - the success validation status is not ported (`success` feedback styling);
    `level` is `ErrorLevel` / `WarningLevel` only.

  - the `feedback` / `label` **slots** are not ported (`feedback : Maybe String`
    and `label : Maybe String` cover the string forms), `labelProps` beyond
    `for` are not ported, and the deprecated `FormItemRow` / `FormItemCol` /
    `FormItemGridItem` components have no counterpart.

  - the fade-down transition between feedback states exists in the stylesheet
    but is **not driven** — the port swaps instantly. As an optional upgrade,
    the caller can own the phase: keep the previous feedback, render the
    outgoing lines under `"fade-down-transition-leave-active"` for one frame via
    `NUI.Internal.transitionClass "fade-down-transition"`, then mount the new
    lines under the enter classes (exactly the caller-driven pattern of
    `NUI.LoadingBar`).

values.name: validateForm
values.comment:
Validate every (filtered) rule path — the pure analog of upstream's
`form.validate`. Each path in `rules` (restricted to `paths` when given, kept
in `rules` order) is emitted with its feedback list — empty when the path is
valid. Values are looked up first-match-wins; a path with no value is absent.

values.name: validateValue
values.comment:
Validate one field's rules against one value.

`trigger` is the event that fired: `Nothing` is a manual validate and runs
**every** rule; `Just t` runs only rules whose `trigger` list contains `t`
(a rule with `trigger = Nothing` is dropped under a passed trigger — upstream's
`rule.trigger === trigger` is false for `undefined`). `field` is
interpolated into the messages. `value = Nothing` is an absent field.

Error-level rules are evaluated first; if any error feedback is produced the
warnings are dropped, otherwise the warning feedbacks are returned. Order is
preserved within each level.
values.type: Maybe.Maybe NUI.Form.Trigger -> String.String -> List.List NUI.Form.Rule -> Maybe.Maybe NUI.Form.Value -> List.List NUI.Form.Feedback

name: NUI.Grid
comment:
Naive UI's `Grid` and `GridItem`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Grid exposing (defaults, item)

    NUI.Grid.view
        { defaults | cols = NUI.Grid.Number 12, xGap = NUI.Grid.Number 16 }
        [ { item | span = NUI.Grid.Number 6, content = [ Element.text "Half" ] }
        , { item | span = NUI.Grid.Number 6, content = [ Element.text "Half" ] }
        ]

A collapsed form grid with a suffix (Naive UI's `collapsed` demo):

    import NUI.Grid exposing (defaults, item)

    NUI.Grid.view
        { defaults
            | cols = NUI.Grid.Custom "1 s:2 m:3"
            , itemResponsive = True
            , collapsed = True
            , collapsedRows = 1
            , query = NUI.Grid.ByKeys (NUI.Grid.breakpointKeys NUI.Grid.defaultBreakpoints 800)
        }
        [ { item | span = NUI.Grid.Custom "1 s:2 m:3" }
        , { item | span = NUI.Grid.Custom "1 s:2 m:3" }
        , { item | span = NUI.Grid.Custom "1 s:2 m:3" }
        , { item | suffix = True, content = [ Element.text "…" ] }
        ]

Naive UI's Grid ships no CSS at all: the container is an inline `display:grid`
div (`n-grid` has no stylesheet rule) and every item is a plain `<div>` whose
`grid-column` / `margin-left` / `display` come from the span/offset/collapse
algorithm in `Grid.tsx`, ported verbatim below. No theme argument is needed.

**Responsive props.** `cols`, `xGap`, `yGap` and each item's `span` / `offset`
take a `GridValue`: a plain `Number` or a responsive string like
`"1 s:2 m:3"` resolved against `defaultBreakpoints` (`s: 640` … `xxl: 1920`)
or any threshold keys you choose (numeric keys work too: `"2 768:3"`).

Naive UI resolves those strings at runtime, from the grid's own measured
width (`responsive = Self`, a `ResizeObserver`) or the window
(`responsive = Screen`, vooks' `useBreakpoints`). This library is pure, so the
caller measures once and passes the result as `query`:

  - `responsive = Self` → `query = ByWidth containerWidth` (and `NoQuery`
    before the first measurement — upstream's `undefined`).
  - `responsive = Screen` →
    `query = ByKeys (breakpointKeys breakpoints windowWidth)`.
  - When nothing responsive is in play (no `itemResponsive` and plain numeric
    `cols`/`xGap`/`yGap` — upstream's `isResponsive` check), the query is
    ignored entirely, exactly like upstream.

`viewWithOverflow` also returns the grid-level `overflow` flag Naive UI feeds
the item slot: `True` when `collapsed` hid some items (the usual condition for
an expand/collapse toggle). Items themselves are records, so per-item slot
data collapses into that one flag.

@docs GridValue, Item, Options, Query, Responsive, breakpointKeys, defaultBreakpoints, defaultCols, defaultSpan, defaults, item, itemDefaults, parseResponsivePropValue, view, viewWithOverflow

unions.name: GridValue
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `number | string` responsive props (`cols`, `xGap`, `yGap`,
`span`, `offset`): a plain `Number 24` (unitless — spans/columns, or pixels
for gaps) or a `Custom "1 s:2 m:3"` responsive string. A bare token in a
string is the empty-key default (`"2 768:3"` is `2` below 768).

unions.name: Query
unions.comment:
The responsive query the caller owns (upstream's `responsiveQueryRef`):
the container width in `Self` mode (`ByWidth`), the active breakpoint keys in
`Screen` mode (`ByKeys` — see `breakpointKeys`), or `NoQuery` for upstream's
`undefined` (before the first measurement, or whenever the props are not
responsive at all).

unions.name: Responsive
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `responsive` prop: measure the grid's own width (`Self`, the
default) or the window (`Screen`). It only selects where upstream's runtime
query comes from; here you supply the measured `query` yourself, so pick the
matching constructor — `ByWidth` for `Self`, `ByKeys` for `Screen`.

aliases.name: Item
aliases.comment:
One `n-grid-item`. `span` / `offset` mirror the props (resolved against
the grid's query when `itemResponsive`), `suffix` pins the item to the row's
end (`privateColStart`), `show = False` is upstream's `v-show="false"` (the
item stays in the flow with span 0), and `content` is the item's slot.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The grid options — Naive UI's NGrid props: `cols`, `xGap`, `yGap`
(each a responsive `GridValue`), `itemResponsive`, `layoutShiftDisabled`
(upstream's `layout-shift-disabled`), `collapsed` + `collapsedRows`, the
per-item `itemStyle`, and the caller-owned responsive inputs `responsive` /
`query` / `breakpoints`, plus `attributes`.
aliases.type: { cols : NUI.Grid.GridValue, responsive : NUI.Grid.Responsive, itemResponsive : Basics.Bool, layoutShiftDisabled : Basics.Bool, collapsed : Basics.Bool, collapsedRows : Basics.Int, itemStyle : List.List (Element.Attribute msg), xGap : NUI.Grid.GridValue, yGap : NUI.Grid.GridValue, query : NUI.Grid.Query, breakpoints : List.List ( String.String, Basics.Float ), attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: breakpointKeys
values.comment:
vooks' `useBreakpoints(breakpoints)` for a given width: the keys whose
`min-width: <threshold>px` media query matches, i.e. threshold `<=` width.
The input order is kept (vooks uses object key order), so with
`defaultBreakpoints` the result is ascending — the order `ByKeys` resolution
needs (the widest active key last).
values.type: List.List ( String.String, Basics.Float ) -> Basics.Float -> List.List String.String

values.name: defaultBreakpoints
values.comment:
Naive UI's `defaultBreakpoints` (`config-provider/src/config.ts`), as an
ascending `( key, threshold-in-px )` list. `breakpointKeys` consumes it.

values.name: defaultCols
values.comment: Upstream `defaultCols = 24`.

values.name: defaultSpan
values.comment: Upstream `defaultSpan = 1` (`grid/src/config.ts`).

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults: 24 columns, `Self` responsiveness with no query yet,
no item-level responsiveness, no layout-shift suppression, not collapsed
(1 row when it is), no item style, no gaps, the standard breakpoints, no
extra attributes.

values.name: item
values.comment:
The blank item every customization starts from: a 1-column span, no
offset, not the suffix, shown, no extra attributes, empty content.

values.name: itemDefaults
values.comment: Alias of `item`, for the `defaults` / `itemDefaults` naming taste.

values.name: parseResponsivePropValue
values.comment:
seemly's `parseResponsivePropValue(prop, activeKeyOrSize)`, ported
verbatim. `"prefix:value …"` parses into a map (a bare token becomes the
`""` key); `Number n` is the `""` key. Resolution by query:

  - `NoQuery` → the `""` entry;
  - `ByKeys keys` → the first present key scanning keys from last to first
    (upstream's `xs s m` array: the widest active key wins), else the `""`
    entry;
  - `ByWidth w` → the entry with the largest numeric key `<= w` (the `""`
    key counts as `0`, like JS `Number('')`).

`Nothing` when nothing matches.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-grid` element — `viewWithOverflow` with the `overflow` flag
dropped.
values.type: NUI.Grid.Options msg -> List.List (NUI.Grid.Item msg) -> Element.Element msg

values.name: viewWithOverflow
values.comment:
`view`, plus the grid-level `overflow` flag upstream delivers through the
item slot: `True` iff some item was reached after `collapsed` filled
`collapsedRows` (note upstream's exact rule — the item that trips the limit
is hidden but does not set `overflow`; only items after it do).
values.type: NUI.Grid.Options msg -> List.List (NUI.Grid.Item msg) -> ( Element.Element msg, Basics.Bool )

name: NUI.Heatmap
comment:
Naive UI's `Heatmap`, rebuilt on elm-ui: a GitHub-style contribution
calendar. Real `<table>` markup (via `Element.html`, the `NUI.Highlight`
precedent for raw nodes) with week labels down the side, month labels across
the top, one rect per day coloured by `value / maxValue`, and a footer with the
less/more colour indicator.

    import NUI.Heatmap exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Heatmap.view theme
        { defaults
            | data =
                [ { timestamp = Time.millisToPosix 1735689600000, value = Just 3 }
                , { timestamp = Time.millisToPosix 1736121600000, value = Just 7 }
                ]
            , zone = Time.utc
            , now = Time.millisToPosix 1735689600000
        }
        []

The element carries the `.n-heatmap` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS (plus the bridge's static
loading keyframes — see below).

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream reads the wall clock (`new Date()`) in three
places; this library is pure, so the caller owns time:

  - `zone` — every date computation (week alignment, gap filling, month
    grouping) is local-timezone, exactly like date-fns without UTC mode. Pass
    the same zone you render with.
  - `now` — only feeds `createLoadingMatrix`'s dead timestamps (upstream
    `Date.now()`); it never reaches the DOM. Upstream also derives the week
    labels and loading month-label dates from `new Date()`, but their rendered
    output (weekday names, month names) depends on nothing but the rotation
    and the caller-supplied label lists, so `now` is not consulted there.

**Locale** replaces upstream's `useLocale('Heatmap')` + date-fns locale:

  - `weekdayLabels` — 7 strings indexed by date-fns weekday number
    (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday), matching `format(ts, 'eee')` output order.
    The component rotates them by the (transformed) week start itself; rows
    1/3/5 are visible, exactly like upstream's `i % 2 !== 0`.
  - `monthLabels` — 12 strings indexed 1–12, matching `format(ts, 'MMM')`.
  - `indicatorLessText` / `indicatorMoreText` — the indicator labels
    (upstream `enUS`: `"less"` / `"more"`).

**`firstDayOfWeek`** keeps Naive UI's own convention (0 = Monday … 6 =
Sunday, like `NUI.Calendar`); the `(n + 1) % 7` shift to date-fns numbering
(0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday) is applied internally, exactly like upstream's
`transformNaiveFirstDayOfWeekToDateFns` calls. The pure core below speaks
date-fns numbering.

**Pure core.** The upstream `src/heatmap/src/utils` functions are exposed for
reuse and testing (`NUI.Grid` / `NUI.Highlight` precedent): `calcColorByValue`,
`completeDataGaps`, `createDayRect`, `createSparseMatrix`, `createLoadingMatrix`,
plus `dataMonthLabels` / `loadingMonthLabels`. `view` uses exactly these.

**Slots.** `footer` (rendered inside the inner `.n-heatmap__footer` wrapper,
only when present) and `indicator` (replaces the whole colour indicator
block). The default indicator renders only when `showColorIndicator` is set,
matching upstream's `resolveSlot` fallback.

**Divergences from upstream** (everything else is a faithful port):

  - **Tooltip is not ported.** Upstream wraps each rect in `n-tooltip` when
    the `tooltip` prop is set; tooltips are outside this library's contract,
    so the caller owns hover UX. Rects render exactly upstream's trigger
    `div.n-heatmap-rect` (with the inline `--n-rect-color`).
  - **`undefined` vs `null` values collapse.** Upstream's
    `value?: number | null` lets `{ value: undefined }` (which renders a rect
    in the _minimum_ colour — `calcColorByValue` treats it like `≤ 0`, but the
    render checks `!== null`) differ from `{ value: null }` (which renders
    `.n-heatmap__empty-cell`). Elm's `Maybe Float` has one `Nothing`, so
    missing values always render the empty cell — one rect _emptier_ than
    upstream for `undefined`-valued data.
  - **The empty-data guard moved inside `completeDataGaps`.** Upstream's util
    crashes on `[]` (`sortedData[0]` of nothing) and `Heatmap.tsx` guards at
    the call site; here the util returns `[]` itself.
  - **Day keys are civil-day numbers, not epoch-millis.** Upstream keys its
    data map by `startOfDay(ts).getTime()`; this port keys by the calendar
    day index in `zone`. The two agree unless the zone's UTC offset changes
    mid-range (a DST-style zone), which `Time.customZone` cannot express and
    no caller supplies — and under such a change the civil-day keys behave
    more sensibly than epoch-millis. Review-confirmed unreachable divergence.
  - **The loading animation is static.** Upstream mounts a runtime stylesheet
    with a color-hashed class (`heatmap-loading-<hash>`) plus keyframes; the
    port ships the same animation verbatim on the existing `--loading`
    modifier (`tools/bridge.css`), so no hashed class is emitted.
  - **`xGap` / `yGap` are visually swapped** — upstream's
    `border-spacing: var(--n-y-gap) var(--n-x-gap)` swaps the axes relative to
    the prop names. Kept verbatim (do not "fix").
  - Quirks kept on purpose: month labels spanning fewer than 3 columns are
    dropped (`weekCount >= 3`); duplicate timestamps are last-wins (JS `Map`
    construction over the sorted data); `value <= 0`, `null`, or
    `maxValue == 0` all paint `colors[0]`; bucketing is `ceil`, not `floor`;
    the loading matrix is a dead 7×53 grid (`timestamp = now`, `value = 0`,
    `color = '#000000'`); `maxValue` always comes from `data`, even while the
    matrix shows `loadingData` (so a loading matrix without `data` paints
    every rect `colors[0]`); and `loadingData = Just []` counts as _present_
    (a JS `[]` is truthy), which yields the loading matrix but **data**-derived
    month labels, while `Nothing` yields the 12 fixed loading labels.

values.name: calcColorByValue
values.comment:
Upstream's `calcColorByValue` — `maxValue == 0`, a `Nothing`/`≤ 0` value,
or an empty palette all yield `colors[0]`; otherwise
`colors[min(ceil(min(value / maxValue, 1) * (len - 1)), len - 1)]` — ceil
bucketing, clamped at both ends. (Upstream reads `colors[0]` of an empty list
as `undefined`; here it is `""` — unreachable through `view`, which always
prepends a minimum colour.)
values.type: List.List String.String -> Maybe.Maybe Basics.Float -> Basics.Float -> String.String

values.name: completeDataGaps
values.comment:
Upstream's `completeDataGaps`, with the empty-list guard moved inside
(upstream crashes; `Heatmap.tsx` guards at the call site).

`completeDataGaps zone data weekStartsOn fillCalendarLeading` sorts `data` by
timestamp, then returns one item per calendar day from the start of the first
item's week to the end of the last item's week: original items win on their
day (duplicates last-wins), days within `[firstDate, lastDate]` (or from the
week start, with `fillCalendarLeading`) are filled with `Just 0`, and the
remaining padding days with `Nothing`. Gap-day timestamps are local midnights.

Only the calendar day of each timestamp in `zone` matters (upstream compares
`startOfDay` keys), except upstream's exact-instant `isWithinInterval` bounds
— and the one edge those could distinguish (the first/last data day itself) is
always covered by the data map, so day-granularity comparison is equivalent.
values.type: Time.Zone -> List.List NUI.Heatmap.HeatmapDataItem -> Basics.Int -> Basics.Bool -> List.List NUI.Heatmap.HeatmapDataItem

values.name: createDayRect
values.comment:
Upstream's `createDayRect` — positions one item in the grid:
`colIndex = differenceInCalendarDays(item, calendarStartDate) // 7`,
`rowIndex = (getDay(item) - weekStartOn + 7) % 7`, colour via
`calcColorByValue`.
values.type: Time.Zone -> NUI.Heatmap.HeatmapDataItem -> Time.Posix -> Basics.Int -> List.List String.String -> Basics.Float -> NUI.Heatmap.DayRect

values.name: createLoadingMatrix
values.comment:
Upstream's `createLoadingMatrix` — a dead 7×53 grid: every timestamp is
`now` (upstream `Date.now()`; the value never reaches the DOM), every value is
`Just 0`, every colour `#000000`.

values.name: createSparseMatrix
values.comment:
Upstream's `createSparseMatrix` — `rows` rows, each item placed at its
column index. Duplicate positions are last-wins (JS `row[col] = item`
iteration order); holes and short rows become `Nothing`, and a row's length is
its highest occupied column + 1 — exactly upstream's sparse arrays, whose
`.map` renders no `<td>` for holes.
values.type: Basics.Int -> List.List item -> (item -> Basics.Int) -> (item -> Basics.Int) -> List.List (List.List (Maybe.Maybe item))

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The raw `--n-*` custom properties a heatmap with these options attaches.
`view` uses exactly this list. `xGap` / `yGap` win over the size defaults when
set (a pixel count, matching `pxfy`); the size-dependent `--n-*` values follow
`createKey('<var>', size)` — including `--n-border-radius`, which reads the
per-size `borderRadiusSmall/Medium/Large`, not the bare `borderRadius`.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Heatmap.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: dataMonthLabels
values.comment:
Upstream's `dataMonthLabelsRef` — for each column, the month of its first
non-null cell scanning down the rows; columns grouped by month, groups
spanning fewer than 3 columns dropped, one `{ month, colSpan }` per surviving
group in chronological order (`Dict` key order equals upstream's `'yyyy-MM'`
string sort for real dates).

Holes and short rows are skipped (`Nothing`); they cannot occur from
gap-filled data, and upstream would crash formatting `undefined` anyway.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults: no data (hence no loading matrix), no leading fill,
weeks starting Monday, not loading, the theme colours, indicator and both
label rows shown, `medium` size, no gaps, LTR, UTC at epoch, the enUS
"less"/"more" + `"Sun"…"Sat"`/`"Jan"…"Dec"` labels, no slots, no extra
attributes.

values.name: loadingMonthLabels
values.comment:
Upstream's `loadingMonthLabelsRef` — all 12 months (the name only depends
on the month; upstream's `new Date(currentYear, i, 1)` contributes nothing
else), with fixed colSpans chosen for consistent label widths; they sum to 53,
the loading matrix width.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-heatmap` element — the `__content` calendar table (month labels
row, 7 day rows, one `.n-heatmap-rect` per valued day, `__empty-cell`
otherwise) plus the `__footer` (optional `footer` slot, colour indicator when
`showColorIndicator`). The `children` list is unused (upstream has no default
slot).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Heatmap.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Highlight
comment:
Naive UI's `Highlight`, rebuilt on elm-ui: plain `text` with every
occurrence of `patterns` wrapped in `highlightTag` (a `<mark>` by default).

    import NUI.Highlight exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Highlight.view theme
        { defaults | text = "Naive UI is awesome", patterns = [ "Naive", "UI" ] }
        []

    -- case-insensitive matching and a customized mark
    NUI.Highlight.view theme
        { defaults
            | text = "naive-ui is written in TypeScript"
            , patterns = [ "naive", "typescript" ]
            , caseSensitive = False
            , highlightClass = Just "my-mark"
            , highlightStyle = [ ( "color", "red" ) ]
        }
        []

Highlight carries no CSS and no `--n-*` variables, so the `theme` argument is
ignored (it exists so call sites are uniform); upstream has no default slot,
so the `children` list is ignored too.

**The root is raw HTML.** Upstream renders a plain
`<span class="n-highlight">` whose children are bare text nodes and
`highlightTag` nodes; this port reproduces that DOM exactly with
`Element.html` and `Html.node` rather than elm-ui helper elements. That is
also why the library's uniform `attributes` field cannot be honored — an
`Element.Attribute` cannot attach to a raw node — so the field exists for
record parity and is unused.

**Regex.** Upstream builds `new RegExp("(" + patterns.join("|") + ")",
"g" | "gi")` and throws on an invalid pattern. `Regex.fromStringWith` compiles
the same source with the same flags (Elm's kernel always adds `g`;
`caseInsensitive = not caseSensitive` supplies `i`) and returns `Nothing`
instead of throwing, which renders as the unmarked `text` — the same output
as the empty-`patterns` branch, and the closest safe equivalent of
upstream's crash. `Regex.find` and `String.slice` share JS's code-unit
arithmetic (`matchAll` / `String.prototype.slice`), so offsets agree even
outside the BMP. The engines diverge only on zero-width matches: JS steps
past them, while Elm's kernel breaks the loop — and a joined alternation of
caller patterns can match the empty string only when a pattern itself can
(`"a*"` with `autoEscape = False`), so that is unreachable for realistic
`patterns`.

The pure core — upstream's `splitAndMarkByRegex` plus the component's
regex construction, exposed for reuse and testing (see `NUI.Grid` for the
precedent).

`splitAndMarkByRegex text patterns caseSensitive autoEscape` joins the
optionally escaped patterns as `(p1|p2|…)`, finds every match and returns the
text split into `Chunk`s in document order — an occurrence as
`isMatch = True`, the stretches between as `isMatch = False` (leftmost-first
alternation follows the engine, as in JS).

  - `patterns == []` short-circuits to one unmarked chunk (upstream's
    component never builds the degenerate `()` regex);
  - empty `text` yields `[]`, exactly like upstream's util;
  - an invalid pattern yields one unmarked chunk instead of upstream's
    `throw`.

The `n-highlight` element — a raw `span.n-highlight` whose children are

name: NUI.Icon
comment:
Naive UI's `Icon`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Icon exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Icon.view theme NUI.Icon.defaults
        [ mySvg ]

    NUI.Icon.view theme
        { defaults
            | size = Just (NUI.Icon.Px 40)
            , depth = Just NUI.Icon.Depth2
        }
        [ mySvg ]

The element carries the `.n-icon` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. Pass the glyph itself —
usually an `svg` — as the child (upstream's `component` prop is the same thing
one level up).

**Divergences.** elm-ui renders the root as a `<div>` rather than upstream's
`<i>`; `.n-icon` is targeted by class, so all of Naive UI's rules apply — the
only visible difference is `<i>`'s browser-default italic for text children.
Upstream's `depth` also accepts the strings `'1'`–`'5'`; those select the same
opacities, which `Depth` covers. Upstream's dev-only "don't wrap `n-icon`
inside `n-icon`" warning is not reproduced.

name: NUI.Image
comment:
Naive UI's `Image`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs ObjectFit, Options, cssVars, defaults
@docs errorReplacesImg, loadingValue, resolveSrc, view

    import NUI.Image exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Image.view theme NUI.Image.defaults

    NUI.Image.view theme
        { defaults
        | src = Just "https://example.com/pic.jpeg"
        , width = Just "200"
        , objectFit = NUI.Image.Contain
        }

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-image` BEM
classes and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

The state machine is caller-owned (Split/Rate/Slider precedent): the port
exposes the render surface and the pure branches of upstream's `showError` /
`loaded` / `shouldStartLoading` logic, and the caller drives those flags
through their own `Msg` from the `onError` / `onLoad` seams plus their
intersection-observer or native-lazy runtime.

Preview seam (batch 1): upstream wraps the img in `NImagePreview`, whose
modal surface is teleported to the body. The port keeps the flow content
byte-equivalent (`n-image` root > img) and hands the caller the preview's
`cssVars` (upstream emits the five `--n-*` vars on the preview container,
not the `n-image` root) plus the click seam to open their preview runtime.

Upstream transition rules the caller owns (the port renders the state;
only the caller can reproduce these, `Image.tsx` setup):

  - `onError` early-returns while `intersectionObserver` is set and
    `shouldStartLoading` is False — errors on not-yet-intersected lazy
    images are swallowed, or every off-screen image flips to error.
  - `onError` sets BOTH `showError = True` and `loaded = True` — the
    latter is why an error hides the placeholder (upstream spec: "should
    not show placeholder slot when image fails to load").
  - `onLoad` sets `loaded = True` after the handlers.
  - A `src` change resets `showError = False` (upstream `watchEffect`),
    so retries start clean.
  - `shouldStartLoading` initializes to `not lazy` — flip it yourself
    when `lazy = True`; `defaults` hardwires `True` for the eager case.

Event seams: upstream fires `props.onLoad` then `imgProps.onLoad` (same
for `onError`); the port folds both into the single `onLoad`/`onError`
seam — handlers attached via `imgAttributes` are Elm last-wins, not
additive.

Accepted edges (documented divergences, kept for batch-1 scope):

  - No `NImagePreview` child and no `NImageGroup` context yet. Upstream's
    flow DOM for a non-group image is the same `img` under the root; the
    modal (toolbar / overlay / drag / keyboard) is the preview batch.
    `previewedImgProps` (the NImage-level prop the preview consumes via
    `imageContextKey`) also rides with that batch.
  - The img always carries `data-group-id=""` — upstream sets it on mount
    even outside a group (`Image.tsx` `onMounted`).
  - `loading` assumes native lazy support (`isImageSupportNativeLazy`,
    true in every browser this port targets).
  - Upstream's `loadDescription` prop is declared but never consumed —
    not ported.
  - Upstream `width`/`height` take `string | number`; the port takes the
    string bytes (`Just "200"`). Upstream's JS `||` falsy fall-throughs
    (`width = 0`, `alt = ""`) are unreachable in practice.

Note: record updates bind `defaults` to a local first, then patch fields.

unions.name: ObjectFit
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `objectFit` prop — the values of CSS `object-fit` (`fill`, the
default, `contain`, `cover`, `none`, `scale-down`), emitted as the img's
inline `object-fit` style by the style pack below.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-image` props. The three state flags (`shouldStartLoading` /
`loaded` / `showError`) are caller-owned — see the module docs for the
transition rules that drive them. `width` / `height` / `alt` take the string
bytes of upstream's `string | number` props; `imgAttributes` is upstream's
`imgProps` spread and `attributes` land on the root.

values.name: cssVars
values.comment:
The five `--n-*` vars upstream emits on the image-preview **container**
(ImagePreview.tsx `cssVarsRef`), in emission order. The `n-image` root
itself carries no inline vars — apply these to the caller's preview
surface until the preview batch lands.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Upstream's mount state: no src, `Fill`, no lazy loading, and
`shouldStartLoading = True` — the eager case's `not lazy` initialization
(upstream flips it to `False` itself when `lazy = True`; the caller owns that
flip here, `Image.tsx` setup).

values.name: errorReplacesImg
values.comment:
The error slot replaces the whole img node when shown
(`showError && errorNode.length`).

values.name: loadingValue
values.comment:
`isImageSupportNativeLazy && lazy && !intersectionObserverOptions
? 'lazy' : 'eager'`, with the env flag hardwired to true (native lazy
support is universal in targeted browsers).

values.name: resolveSrc
values.comment:
Upstream's src ternary (Image.tsx render):

    showError            -> fallbackSrc
    lazy && observerOpts -> (shouldStartLoading ? loadSrc : undefined)
    otherwise            -> loadSrc

where `loadSrc = src` (upstream also folds `imgProps.src` in; set `src`).
`Nothing` means the attribute is omitted.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-image` root: the img (or the whole-node `error` slot when
`errorReplacesImg`) plus the placeholder layer while not `loaded`, with the
border pair's absence this template has (upstream's root carries no border
nodes). Pure — the state flags come in through `Options`.

name: NUI.ImageGroup
comment:
Naive UI's `ImageGroup`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Options, currentId, currentUrl, defaults, go, imageIds
@docs nextIndex, prevIndex, previewOptions, showImage, urlMap, view

    import NUI.ImageGroup as ImageGroup

    ImageGroup.view theme
        { ImageGroup.defaults
            | srcList = [ url1, url2, url3 ]
            , current = 0
            , show = True
            , onPrev = Just PrevMsg
            , onNext = Just NextMsg
            , onClose = Just Closed
        }

Upstream `NImageGroup` renders its children (the `n-image`s) as
`NImagePreview`'s slot and mounts the preview container via LazyTeleport.
The port keeps both halves explicit (no teleport, `NUI.Modal` precedent):
you render the `n-image` children in flow yourself, and `view` renders the
preview container — `ImageGroup.view` emits exactly the
`NUI.ImagePreview` tree fed from the group state, so mount it under the
same rules (unmount when fully closed, keep mounted through leave phases).

Two url registries, byte-faithful to upstream's merged map:

  - `srcList` — the `p${index}` keys (`p0`, `p1`, …). When non-empty it
    WINS over the registered map, and upstream throws if a child `n-image`
    registers anyway (a caller-side contract here — don't mix them).
  - `registered` — the `r`-scheme entries the child `n-image`s contribute,
    as `(imageId, url)` pairs. Model it as upstream's keyed map: keep the
    imageIds UNIQUE and let a later registration overwrite (upstream's
    `registerImageUrl` double-prefixes its `has('r' + sid)` check, so the
    `set` always runs — re-registration overwrites the url); and treat
    unregistration as a no-op (upstream's `unregisterPreviewUrl` deletes
    only when the key is NOT present, so it never deletes — unmounted
    children stay walkable in the wrap space). The port does not dedupe
    for you; duplicate ids would double-count in `imageIds` and skew the
    walk's index space.

Index walk (all pure, upstream bytes):

  - `nextIndex` / `prevIndex` wrap around, skipping falsy urls
    (empty strings) — `Just index` only when some url exists.
  - `go 1` / `go -1` is upstream's `go(step)`: step 1 moves to `nextIndex`
    (and is what upstream's toolbar "next" fires, `onPreviewNext` along the
    way), step -1 to `prevIndex`.
  - `showImage imageId` is `toggleShow`'s `setCurrentId` half: index of the
    id, set only when it differs. `toggleShow` also opens (`show = True`) —
    do both in your msg handler.
  - `currentId` / `currentUrl` read the merged registry.

Prev/next wiring (upstream has TWO paths with different resets): the
toolbar switch buttons route through `handleSwitchPrev/Next` — reset the
zoom (`NUI.ImagePreview.switchReset`), then fire `go`. The document
keyboard handlers (←/→) fire the RAW prev/next — `go` WITHOUT the reset.
So the `onPrev` / `onNext` msgs here are YOUR toolbar msgs (reset + go);
keep the keyboard path reset-free by mapping `NUI.ImagePreview.keyAction`
Prev/Next to `go` only.

`NUI.ImagePreview`'s `previewedImgProps` do not apply: in group mode
upstream's preview gets no `imageContext` (the inject fails), so the img
carries no controlled class/style — the port omits those fields entirely.

Accepted edges:

  - Child `n-image`s don't auto-register (no injection in a pure tree) —
    you thread their urls into `registered` yourself; their thumbnails keep
    `data-group-id=""` (upstream stamps a random `c<uuid>` there, which is
    not byte-pinnable).
  - `groupId`, `renderToolbar`, `showToolbarTooltip`, `keepDragOffset` ride
    the preview's seams/edges (see `NUI.ImagePreview`).

Note: record updates bind `defaults` to a local first, then patch fields.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-image-group` props — the group's url registries, the walk state,
and the preview-surface flags threaded straight into `NUI.ImagePreview`
(`zoom` IS the preview's `Zoom`, the three `*Transition` phases hold its
nodes mounted through leave fades, `wrapperStyle` feeds `syncTransformOrigin`).
The `onPrev` / `onNext` msgs are the toolbar switch msgs (reset + `go`);
the keyboard path fires `go` only (see the module docs).
aliases.type: { srcList : List.List String.String, registered : List.List ( String.String, String.String ), current : Basics.Int, show : Basics.Bool, showToolbar : Basics.Bool, zoom : NUI.ImagePreview.Zoom, dragging : Basics.Bool, imgDerived : Basics.Bool, imgTransition : Basics.Bool, overlayTransition : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase, toolbarTransition : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase, wrapperTransition : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase, wrapperStyle : List.List ( String.String, String.String ), onPrev : Maybe.Maybe msg, onNext : Maybe.Maybe msg, onClose : Maybe.Maybe msg, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: currentId
values.comment: `currentId` — the key at `current`, `Nothing` when out of range.

values.name: currentUrl
values.comment:
`currentUrl` — upstream's `src` for the preview. Falsy (empty) urls are
returned as `Just ""` here; the walk in `nextIndex`/`prevIndex` skips them.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
A closed, hidden group: empty registries, `current = 0`, toolbar on, the
preview's initial zoom and all leave phases clear.

values.name: go
values.comment:
`go(step)`: step 1 → `nextIndex`, step -1 → `prevIndex`; `current`
unchanged when the walk finds nothing. Upstream also fires
`onPreviewNext`/`onPreviewPrev` — fold that into the msg that calls `go`.

values.name: imageIds
values.comment: The registry's key list, in order — the index space `current` walks.

values.name: nextIndex
values.comment:
`nextIndex`: scan `current + 1 .. count - 1` for the first entry with a
truthy (non-empty) url, then wrap `0 .. current - 1`.

values.name: prevIndex
values.comment:
`prevIndex`: the mirror scan (`current - 1 .. 0`, then wrap from the
tail).

values.name: previewOptions
values.comment:
The `NUI.ImagePreview.Options` the group state maps onto — exposed for
pins and for callers that need to style the container through the preview's
richer fields.

values.name: showImage
values.comment:
`setCurrentId` (the `toggleShow` half): index of `imageId`, written only
when it differs from `current`. Unknown ids leave the state untouched
(upstream's `indexOf` → -1 → differs → would set -1; here out-of-range ids
are refused — a `-1` current is unreachable through the public API).

values.name: urlMap
values.comment:
The merged registry, `srcList` winning over `registered` exactly as
upstream's `mergedImageUrlMap`. Keys follow upstream's scheme: `p${index}`
for the list, the caller's image ids for the registered entries.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The preview tree fed from the group state — the exact
`NUI.ImagePreview.view` this renders is upstream's group-mounted preview.
Mount it next to your `n-image` children (upstream renders the children as
its slot, then the container).

name: NUI.ImagePreview
comment:
Naive UI's `ImagePreview` (the `n-image` modal), rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs HorizontalDirection, KeyAction, MoveStrategy, Options, Rect
@docs VerticalDirection, Viewport, Zoom, cssVars, defaults, derivedOffset
@docs imgStyle, keyAction, maxScale, moveStrategy, originalSizeScale
@docs resizeToOriginalSize, rotateClockwise, rotateCounterclockwise
@docs switchReset, toggleOriginalSize, toolbarButtons, transformStyle, view
@docs zoom0, zoomIn, zoomOut

    import NUI.ImagePreview as ImagePreview

    ImagePreview.view theme
        { ImagePreview.defaults
            | show = True
            , src = Just "https://07akioni.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/07akioni.jpeg"
            , zoom = ImagePreview.zoom0
            , onClose = Just Closed
        }

The element is the `.n-image-preview-container` overlay tree: container
(the five `--n-*` preview vars), `.n-image-preview-overlay` (click-to-close
seam), `.n-image-preview-toolbar` (prev/next when `onPrev` is set — upstream
keys both on `onPrev` alone — then rotateCCW, rotateCW, original size,
zoomOut, zoomIn, download, close, each an `i.n-base-icon`), and
`.n-image-preview-wrapper` holding `img.n-image-preview`. `NUI.Css` ships
Naive UI's exact CSS (the whole preview family came with the image batch).

The runtime is caller-owned (Modal/Slider precedent):

  - **Mounting.** No teleport — mount `view` wherever you like and unmount
    when fully closed (`displayDirective: 'if'` semantics). While a leave
    phase runs, keep it mounted: pass the phase through
    `overlayTransition` / `toolbarTransition` (`fade-in-transition`) or
    `wrapperTransition` (`fade-in-scale-up-transition`) and the matching
    node stays rendered with its phase class.
  - **Zoom / drag state.** `zoom` is the whole upstream vector
    (`scale`/`scaleExp`/`offsetX`/`offsetY`/`rotate`, init `zoom0`). The
    transforms are exported pure: `zoomIn` / `zoomOut` /
    `resizeToOriginalSize` / `toggleOriginalSize` (dblclick — does NOT touch
    `scaleExp`, upstream bytes) / `rotateCounterclockwise` /
    `rotateClockwise` / `switchReset` (prev/next switch: scale 1, exp 0,
    offsets 0, rotate 0). `maxScale` / `originalSizeScale` take the img
    natural size plus the viewport (`BLEEDING = 32` lives inside).
    `zoomOut`'s upstream dance (measure the rect at the new scale, clamp
    offsets, restore) is the caller's two-step: apply `zoomOut`,
    re-measure, then `derivedOffset` + write `zoom.offsetX/Y`.
  - **The img style.** Upstream derives the style pack ONLY on interaction
    (every zoom/rotate/resize/dblclick/drag handler calls
    `derivePreviewStyle`; nothing derives on mount or on `show`), so a
    freshly opened preview's img carries just `previewedImgProps.style` —
    no inline cursor/transform. The port mirrors that: set `imgDerived`
    (in every interaction handler, alongside the zoom/drag transforms) and
    the full pack renders; before that, only the controlled pairs.
    `transformStyle` is the exact transform fragment (raw floats —
    `String.fromFloat` ≡ `String(number)`) and the pack renders
    `cursor: grab`/`grabbing` in upstream order (dragging: `transition:
    none` BEFORE the transform, else AFTER, and only when the transition
    is suppressed). `previewedImgStyle` is the controlled prefix (upstream
    `previewedImgProps.style`); pass keys already kebab-cased.
  - **Drag.** `moveStrategy` + `derivedOffset` port `getMoveStrategy` /
    `getDerivedOffset` (the viewport clamp); bind `onImgMousedown` and run
    them in your update. `keepDragOffset` is simply "skip the
    `derivedOffset` application on mouseup". Two upstream guards the seam
    leaves to you: mousedown starts a drag only for the primary button
    (`event.button !== 0` early-returns), and dragstart is ALWAYS
    preventDefault-ed — guard both in your decoders (a custom
    `Events.on` / `preventDefault` decoder via `previewedImgAttributes`,
    since the plain `onImgMousedown` seam carries no button info).
  - **Keyboard.** Upstream binds `keydown` on `document`; bind it in your
    own runtime and feed `keyAction` (Space → preventDefault only, ←/→ →
    prev/next, ↑/↓ → zoom in/out, Escape → close). ←/→ fire the RAW
    `onPrev`/`onNext` upstream — keyboard navigation does NOT reset
    zoom/offset/rotate (only the toolbar switch buttons route through
    `handleSwitch*`), so apply `switchReset` on the toolbar path only.
  - **`syncTransformOrigin`.** Measure the thumbnail's bounding-rect center
    and write it into `wrapperStyle` as `("transform-origin",
    "<tx>px <ty>px")` on enter/before-leave.
  - **Wheel.** Upstream only `preventDefault`s on the container — attach it
    yourself via `attributes` (`Html.Events.custom "wheel"` with
    `preventDefault = True`).

Accepted edges (documented divergences):

  - Toolbar tooltips (`showToolbarTooltip`) are not wired: upstream wraps
    each icon in a renderless Binder, so the closed-state DOM is identical;
    the open tooltip body is the caller's `NUI.Tooltip` seam.
  - `renderToolbar` is not modelled; `toolbarButtons` exposes the exact
    default node list so a caller can recompose it.
  - The download button renders; the browser download itself is the
    caller's msg (upstream `_utils` `download`).
  - `zindexable` is the caller's `attributes` seam — upstream's directive
    writes an inline `z-index` while shown; put the rule (or a style
    override) on the container yourself.
  - Vue's `key={previewSrc}` (img node re-created on src change) is not
    modelled; Elm re-renders the attribute.
  - The container in group mode is identical (`NUI.ImageGroup` composes
    this view); `previewedImgProps` only flow in standalone mode upstream
    (group's preview gets no `imageContext`) — the group passes none.

Note: record updates bind `defaults` to a local first, then patch fields.

unions.name: HorizontalDirection
unions.comment:
The sign of a drag's horizontal delta: positive (dragged right-to-left)
→ `HorizontalLeft`, else `HorizontalRight`.

unions.name: KeyAction
unions.comment:
The `document` keydown mapping (`handleKeydown`): Space only
`preventDefault`s; ←/→ fire prev/next without preventing; ↑/↓ prevent and
zoom; Escape closes.

unions.name: VerticalDirection
unions.comment:
The sign of a drag's vertical delta: positive → `VerticalTop`, else
`VerticalBottom`.

aliases.name: MoveStrategy
aliases.comment:
`getMoveStrategy`'s output: drag deltas plus the directions their signs
imply.
aliases.type: { deltaHorizontal : Basics.Float, deltaVertical : Basics.Float, horizontal : NUI.ImagePreview.HorizontalDirection, vertical : NUI.ImagePreview.VerticalDirection }

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The preview-surface props. `show` mounts the overlay / toolbar / wrapper
(gated per-node: the overlay and toolbar render while `show` or their leave
phase runs, the wrapper always renders — upstream's `v-show` seat); `zoom` +
`dragging` + the two `img*` flags drive the img's inline style pack; the
`Maybe msg` seams are the toolbar / overlay / img event handlers (all
optional — an unset seam renders the icon with no handler, exactly like
upstream's `null` slots).

`cssVarsRef`), identical entry-for-entry to the image batch's emission —
delegated to `NUI.Image.cssVars`.

values.comment:
A closed, empty preview: toolbar on, the initial zoom, no drag, no
derived img style (the fresh-open state — upstream derives nothing on mount
or on `show`), all transitions clear.

`getDerivedOffset` — "avoid image move outside viewport". Without a
strategy (the zoom-out clamp call) the fallback branch reads `max(-half,
start)`/`max(-half, start)` on each axis, matching upstream's undefined
destructure.

The full `style` pack `derivePreviewStyle` writes onto the preview img,
split into declarations in upstream order:

  - the controlled prefix (`previewedImgStyle`) first,
  - `cursor: grabbing; transition: none;` then the transform while dragging,
  - else `cursor: grab;` transform, and `transition: none` appended only

Upstream's `handleKeydown` as a pure decoder: Space → `SpacePrevent`
(preventDefault only), ←/→ → `Prev` / `Next` (the raw prev/next — no zoom
reset; see `switchReset` for the toolbar path), ↑/↓ → `ZoomInKey` /
`ZoomOutKey` (both preventDefault), Escape → `Close`. Any other key is
`Nothing`.

values.name: maxScale
values.comment:
`Math.max(3, heightMaxScale * 2, widthMaxScale * 2)` where each
maxScale is `Math.max(1, natural / (inner - 32))`.

values.comment: `getMoveStrategy`: `delta = mouseDown - mouseUp`; positive → Left/Top.
