values.comment:
`getOrignalImageSizeScale` (sic): 1 when the image fits, else the larger
overshoot ratio.

values.name: resizeToOriginalSize
values.comment:
`resizeToOrignalImageSize` (sic): scale to `originalSizeScale`,
`scaleExp = ceil(ln scale / ln 1.5)`, offsets zeroed.

values.name: rotateClockwise
values.comment: Rotate 90° clockwise: `rotate + 90`.

values.name: rotateCounterclockwise
values.comment:
Rotate the image 90° counterclockwise (upstream `rotateCounterclockwise`
toolbar action): `rotate - 90`.

values.name: switchReset
values.comment:
The prev/next switch reset (`handleSwitchPrev/Next` before their `onPrev`
/ `onNext` fire): scale 1, exp 0, offsets 0, rotate 0.

values.name: toggleOriginalSize
values.comment:
Dblclick toggle: `scale === originalSizeScale ? 1 : originalSizeScale`
— `scaleExp` deliberately untouched (upstream bytes).

values.name: toolbarButtons
values.comment:
The default toolbar node list, in upstream order — prev+next when (and
only when) `onPrev` is set, then rotateCCW, rotateCW, original size, zoomOut,
zoomIn, download, close. Exposed for `renderToolbar`-style recomposition.

values.name: transformStyle
view
values.comment:
The overlay tree: container > (overlay? toolbar? wrapper). Mount it
while `show` or any leave phase runs; unmount once fully closed.

values.name: zoom0
values.comment:
Upstream's init zoom — `scale = 1`, `scaleExp = 0`, no offset, no
rotation. Every switchReset returns here.

values.name: zoomIn
values.comment:
Zoom in: guarded by `scale < maxScale`; `scaleExp += 1` then
`scale = min maxScale (1.5 ^ scaleExp)`.

values.name: zoomOut
values.comment:
Zoom out's scale step: guarded by `scale > 0.5`; `scaleExp -= 1` then
`scale = max 0.5 (1.5 ^ scaleExp)`. The viewport-clamp of the offsets is the
caller's follow-up (`derivedOffset`), matching upstream's measure-at-new-scale
dance.

name: NUI.Input
comment:
Naive UI's `Input` (plus `InputGroup` and `InputGroupLabel`), rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs InputType, Options, PairSource, Status
@docs defaults, group, groupLabel, view

The component owns its value: pass the current string in `value` and receive
updates through `onInput`.

    Input.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = model.value
            , onInput = Just GotInput
            , placeholder = Just "Basic Input"
        }

    -- textarea / password / sizes / statuses
    Input.view theme
        { defaults
            | type_ = Input.Textarea
            , rows = 4
            , status = Just Input.Warning
        }

    Input.view theme
        { defaults
            | type_ = Input.Password
            , clearable = True
            , round = True
            , size = NUI.Types.Small
            , prefix = Just (Element.text "¥")
            , suffix = Just (Element.text "RMB")
        }

Input groups (Naive UI's `n-input-group` / `n-input-group-label`):

    Input.group
        [ Input.groupLabel theme
            { size = NUI.Types.Medium, bordered = True }
            [ Element.text "https://" ]
        , Input.view theme { defaults | placeholder = Just "website" }
        , Input.groupLabel theme
            { size = NUI.Types.Medium, bordered = True }
            [ Element.text ".com" ]
        ]

(`defaults` must be bound to a local name first — Elm's record update syntax
does not accept a qualified `Input.defaults` there.)

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the elements carry the `.n-input` BEM
classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive
UI's exact CSS.

Three seams beyond the basic props:

  - `varOverrides` — upstream's per-instance `builtinThemeOverrides` as a
    key/value patch over the resolved `--n-*` vars (a known key is swapped
    in place, an unknown one appended — `NUI.Button.varOverrides` is the
    same seam); `NUI.InputOtp`'s slots use it for upstream's
    `{ paddingTiny, …, paddingLarge: '0' }` zeroing (`InputOtp.tsx` render:
    `--n-padding-left/right: 0`).

  - `autosize` — upstream `autosize: Boolean | {minRows?, maxRows?}`
    (`Input.tsx:89`); here `Bool` only. `True` emits `n-input--autosize`
    on the root and suppresses `n-input--resizable` (upstream
    `Input.tsx:1130-1131` gates `--resizable` on `resizable && !autosize`
    and fires `--autosize` on the flag alone, ungated on `type`). The
    height measurement itself (`Input.tsx:339-375` — the minRows/maxRows
    math, `overflow` toggling) is runtime DOM sizing — caller-owned; the
    object form maps to the caller setting `rows` / CSS.

  - `loading` — upstream renders its `NBaseSuffix` spinner whenever the
    `loading` prop is set (`Input.tsx:1345-1352`); here `loading = True`.
    DOM (the `NUI.BaseSelection` suffix idiom): `div.n-base-loading
    .n-base-suffix` (strokeWidth 24, scale 0.85, `role="img"
    aria-label="loading"`) > `__transition-wrapper` > `__container` > the
    spinner svg. It renders inside `.n-input__suffix` — which now appears
    for loading alone too — in upstream order `[clear, loading, suffix
    slot]` (`internalLoadingBeforeSuffix` defaults true).

  - `inputAttributes` — upstream's `inputProps`: raw attributes onto the
    inner `<input>` / `<textarea>` element (upstream demos pass
    `autocomplete='disabled'`, `id`, `max`). The field-owned attributes
    (`type` / `value` / `placeholder` / `maxlength` / `minlength` /
    `disabled` / `readonly` / `rows` / the input event) always render
    FIRST and win duplicate names (HTML keeps the first occurrence; the
    raw list appends after) — pass only attributes the fields above don't
    own.

Picker-trigger seams (all default-off — the standalone input renders
byte-identically without them; upstream drives them from the picker
components' `NInput` invocations):

  - `passivelyActivated` / `activated` — the manual-activation focus split
    (upstream `Input.tsx:1140-1143` on the root, `:1203` / `:1273` / `:1410`
    on the inner elements): while `passivelyActivated && !activated` the ROOT
    carries `tabindex 0` (iff not disabled) and the inner input / textarea
    carry `tabindex -1`. Enter / Escape activation
    (`handleWrapperKeydownEnter` / `...Esc`) and programmatic focus
    (`focus()` / `activate()`) are caller-owned runtime — no ports in house
    style; flip `activated` yourself.

  - `internalForceFocus` — upstream's visual-only focus seam (`mergedFocus`,
    `Input.tsx:283-285`): adds `n-input--focus` to the root. Upstream has NO
    `--active` / `--hover` classes at all (hover is pure CSS `:hover`,
    activation is state-only).

  - `textDecoration` — inline `text-decoration` on the input / textarea
    element (upstream `:1208` / `:1269`; the pickers pass `'line-through'`
    while the value is invalid).

  - `attrSize` — the native `size` attribute on the `<input>` only (upstream
    `:1288`; the default 20 equals the HTML default, so it is emitted only
    when set — TimePicker passes `format.length + 4`). Never the textarea.

  - `onFocus` / `onBlur` — raw focus / blur events on the input / textarea
    element; in pair mode BOTH inputs carry them (upstream `Input.tsx:1289` /
    `:1422` binds focus/blur on each pair input — mirrored into `pairEvents`
    2026-10 after the live smoke found a pair trigger wired like DatePicker's
    daterange could never hear a focus).

  - pair mode — upstream `Input.tsx:1395-1465`. Set `pairValue = Just (
    start, end )` and the root gains `n-input--pair` and the body becomes
    `div.n-input-wrapper` (input 1, NO suffix) → `span.n-input__separator`
    (`separatorNode`) → `div.n-input-wrapper` (input 2 + the pair-only
    `div.n-input__suffix`). Input 1 carries the `attrSize` `size` attribute and
    `pairTextDecoration`'s first half; input 2 carries neither (`Input.tsx:1434`
    — no `inputProps` spread, no `size`). Typing emits through `onPairInput`
    with the whole pair and a `PairSource` tag (`PairFirst` / `PairSecond`; the
    clear control emits `("", "")` + `PairClear`, upstream's `0 | 1 | 'clear'`).
    Standalone single-input bytes are unchanged — every field defaults off.

  - `extraRootClasses` — upstream's fallthrough `class` merge onto the
    `.n-input` root (the pickers pass their own marker here, e.g.
    `n-date-panel-date-input`); appended after the component classes.

  - `extraRootAttributes` — upstream's fallthrough `style`/attrs onto the
    root (ColorPicker's alpha unit passes `flex-grow: 1.25` here,
    `ColorInputUnit.tsx:162`); appended after the component's own, so a
    duplicate name wins HTML's first-occurrence rule against them — pass
    only attributes the component does not own.

  - `clearIconPlaceholder` — upstream's `clear-icon-placeholder` slot: the
    content shown inside `NBaseClear`'s placeholder while the clear button
    is hidden. `NBaseClear` renders iff `clearable` OR this is set (upstream
    `:1324-1346`), but the `.n-input__suffix` wrapper itself still needs
    `clearable` / a suffix / loading (upstream's own suffix condition,
    `:1316-1320`) — exactly as upstream. A picker's icon rides this slot
    when `clearable` (it swaps to the clear icon over a value) and `suffix`
    otherwise. The port's `NBaseClear` DOM diverges from upstream only in
    carrying the `_internal/clear` rules as inline styles (that cssr is not
    part of the generated stylesheet — the existing clear implementation's
    divergence); an `Element` here embeds with `display:contents`
    (`clearPlaceholder` is the raw-`Html` twin).

unions.name: Status
unions.comment:
Naive UI's form validation `status` (`success` | `warning` | `error`).
Upstream's input cssr only renders `warning` / `error` (`input.cssr.ts:349`,

gray border. The port closes that gap in-component (`statusVars`): the
`success` status rebinds the same resting / hover / focus border vars the base
rules read to the success family, so the border turns green without new CSS.

`onInput` is `Nothing` when you want a read-only-looking render with no

name: NUI.InputNumber
comment:
Naive UI's `InputNumber`, rebuilt on elm-ui: a text input for numbers with
clamp-to-`min`/`max`, `precision` formatting and add / minus buttons (real
`NUI.Button`s, rendered in the input's suffix — or split around it for
`Both` — with Naive UI's add / remove base-icon glyphs).

@docs ButtonPlacement, DeriveArgs, DerivedValue, NumberContext, Options
@docs addUpdate, addable, contextOf, createValidValue, defaults
@docs deriveValueFromDisplayedValue, displayedValueFor, displayedValueInvalid
@docs format, getMaxPrecision, getPrecision, inputUpdate, isWipValue
@docs minusUpdate, minusable, parse, parseNumber, toFixedJs, validator, view

    import NUI.InputNumber exposing (defaults)

    NUI.InputNumber.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = model.number
            , onChange = Just SetNumber
            , onInput = Just NumberInput
        }
        []

    NUI.InputNumber.view theme
        { defaults
            | min = Just 0
            , max = Just 10
            , step = 0.01
            , precision = Just 2
            , size = NUI.Types.Small
            , buttonPlacement = NUI.InputNumber.Both
        }
        []

**Caller-owned runtime** (same contract as `NUI.Calendar`'s `now` / `panel`).
Upstream keeps a `displayedValueRef` text buffer and derives everything from
it; this library is pure, so the caller owns the buffer and the value:

  - `displayedValue : Maybe String` — **the text buffer, the option that
    carries the typing state.** `Nothing` means "not typing": the view derives
    the text from `value` exactly like upstream's `deriveDisplayedValueFromValue`
    (see `displayedValueFor`). `Just raw` means the user is mid-edit: the raw
    text is shown verbatim (including wip values like `"0."` or `"-0"`).
  - `onInput` fires with the raw text of every keystroke. Store it
    (`displayedValue = Just raw`) and, when `updateValueOnInput` is on and no
    `precision` is set, apply `inputUpdate opts raw` to `value` — the port of
    upstream's `handleUpdateDisplayedValue` live-sync guard and all.
  - `onChange` fires with upstream's `doUpdateValue` payload. The add / minus
    buttons emit it via `addUpdate` / `minusUpdate`; on receipt set
    `value = payload` and `displayedValue = Nothing` (the buffer re-derives).
  - What stays with the caller: the blur / Enter commit
    (`deriveValueFromDisplayedValue ctx { offset = 0, doUpdateIfValid = True,
    fixPrecision = True, isInputing = False }` — upstream's exact `doBlur` /
    Enter-key call), the ArrowUp / ArrowDown keys (commit, then
    `addUpdate` / `minusUpdate`), and the hold-to-repeat timers (800 ms
    threshold, 100 ms interval — each tick is one `addUpdate` / `minusUpdate`).
    `NUI.Input` exposes no focus / blur / keydown hooks, so those cannot be
    wired from `view`.

**Slots.** The children model upstream's `prefix` / `suffix` slots: the first
child is the prefix slot, the second the suffix slot (both optional). While
`showButton` is on, upstream wraps slot content in `n-input-number-prefix` /
`n-input-number-suffix` spans — so does `view`.

**Upstream utils, ported faithfully and exposed** (a tester asserts them):
`parse`, `isWipValue`, `validator`, `format`, `parseNumber` from
`input-number/src/utils.ts`, plus `toFixedJs` (JavaScript's
`Number.prototype.toFixed`, computed from the exact decimal expansion of the
double — `String.fromFloat` is already byte-identical to JS `String(number)`,
verified against Node). `parse` keeps upstream's null-vs-NaN distinction:
empty / whitespace-only input is `Nothing` (upstream `null`, which clears the
value), while unparseable text is `Just (0/0)` (upstream `NaN`, which is
invalid and commits nothing) — `deriveValueFromDisplayedValue` behaves
differently for the two, exactly like upstream.

**Gaps vs upstream (documented, not worked around):**

  - Upstream narrows the inner input's padding through `builtinThemeOverrides`
    (`small "0 8px 0 10px"`, `medium "0 8px 0 12px"`, `large "0 8px 0 14px"`);
    `NUI.Input` has no padding option (see `NUI.InputOtp`'s header), so the
    input renders with its own defaults (`"0 10px"` / `"0 12px"` / `"0 14px"`)
    — the right padding is 2–6 px wider than upstream when buttons show.
  - Upstream strikes invalid text through (`textDecoration = 'line-through'`
    when `displayedValueInvalid`); `NUI.Input` has no text-decoration option.
  - `NUI.Input`'s `prefix` / `suffix` are single `Element`s, so a slot holding
    both a span and the buttons needs one extra wrapper `div` (an unclassed
    flex row — visually inert inside the inline-flex `n-input__suffix`).
  - Upstream sets `focusable={false}` on the buttons; `NUI.Button` always
    renders `tabindex 0` when enabled.
  - Upstream props not carried by this API: `autofocus`, `loading`,
    `clearable`, `round`, `keyboard`, `inputProps`, `bordered` and the custom
    `parse` / `format` / `validator` functions.

Upstream's `buttonPlacement` prop: `right` (both buttons after the input)
or `both` (minus before, add after).

Upstream's `null | number | false` return: `NullValue` is `null` (the
value clears), `NumberValue` is a number (with `doUpdateIfValid = True` this

values.name: addUpdate
values.comment:
Upstream `doAdd` as a pure function: `Nothing` when the button would not
fire (not addable — the button renders disabled then); `Just payload`
otherwise — `createValidValue` when the value is empty, else the `+step`
derivation with `doUpdateIfValid` / `fixPrecision`.

values.name: addable
values.comment:
Upstream `addableRef`: whether the add button is enabled — the current
displayed value yields a number under a `+step` offset.

values.name: contextOf
values.comment:
The resolved context: `min` / `max` as given, `step` as upstream's
`mergedStepRef` (`abs`, and `0` becomes `1`), and `displayedValue` as the
caller-owned buffer or its derivation from `value`.

values.name: createValidValue
values.comment:
Upstream `createValidValue`: the value an empty input takes when a button
is pressed — `max(0, min)`, else `min(0, max)`, else `0`.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Upstream's initial state: empty value and buffer, no bounds, `step = 1`,
no precision, medium size, both buttons after the input, live update on.

values.name: deriveValueFromDisplayedValue
values.comment:
Upstream `deriveValueFromDisplayedValue`, verbatim: the wip guard, the
null / NaN split, the precision gate (`precision < currentPrecision` blocks
unless `fixPrecision`), the offset with `toFixed` at the resolved precision,
the `min` / `max` clamping (`doUpdateIfValid` and not `isInputing` turn an
out-of-range result into the bound instead of `false`), and the `validator`
checks. The custom `props.validator` predicate has no counterpart in this API
(see the module gaps).

values.name: displayedValueFor
values.comment:
Upstream `deriveDisplayedValueFromValue` (without the custom-`format`
branch this API does not carry): the text the input shows for `value` —
`""` for no value, `String(v)` unless a set `precision` fits it, else
`toFixed(v, precision)`, and `"NaN"` for a NaN value.

values.name: displayedValueInvalid
values.comment:
Upstream `displayedValueInvalidRef` (drives the `line-through` that
`NUI.Input` cannot render — see the module gaps).

values.name: format
values.comment:
Upstream `format`: `''` for no value, `String(value)` without a precision
(`String.fromFloat` is byte-identical to JS `String(number)`), `toFixed`
with one.

values.name: getMaxPrecision
values.comment:
Upstream `getMaxPrecision(currentValue)`: the maximum decimal count of
`min`, `max`, `step` and the current value (absent ones count `0`). This is
the precision used when the `precision` option is unset — upstream resolves
`precision ?? getMaxPrecision(parsedValue)`, it does **not** take a max of the
option and the step.

values.name: getPrecision
values.comment:
Upstream `getPrecision(value)`: the decimal count of `String(value)`
(`0.1 → 1`, `1e-7 → 0` — exponent forms carry no fraction).

values.name: inputUpdate
values.comment:
Upstream `handleUpdateDisplayedValue`'s live-sync half: the `onChange`
payload a typed `raw` produces, when `updateValueOnInput` is on and no
`precision` is set (upstream also gates on the absent custom `parse` /
`format`, which this API does not carry). `Nothing` — no update.

values.name: isWipValue
values.comment:
Upstream `isWipValue`: true while the user may still be typing a decimal
(`"0."`, `"1.20"`, `"-0"`, `"-"`), so the raw text must not be replaced by its
parsed value. A faithful port of

    (value.includes('.')
      && (/^(-)?\d+.*(\.|0)$/.test(value) || /^-?\d*$/.test(value)))
    || value === '-'
    || value === '-0'

(The second alternative can never fire for a string that contains `'.'`, but
it is ported anyway; JS regex `.` excludes line terminators, which a
single-line input value cannot contain.)

values.name: minusUpdate
values.comment: Upstream `doMinus`, the `−step` twin of `addUpdate`.

values.name: minusable
values.comment: Upstream `minusableRef`, the `−step` twin of `addable`.

values.name: parse
values.comment:
Upstream `parse`: `null` for empty / whitespace-only input, else JS
`Number(value)`. The NaN case is kept as `Just (0/0)` — upstream's `null`
clears the value while its `NaN` is merely invalid, and
`deriveValueFromDisplayedValue` tells them apart.

values.name: parseNumber
values.comment:
Upstream `parseNumber` — the string arm (`number` inputs are the identity,
`null` is `Nothing`): JS `Number(string)` with `NaN` collapsed to `Nothing`.
Note `parseNumber "" == Just 0` (JS `Number("")`) while `parse "" == Nothing`.

values.name: toFixedJs
values.comment:
JavaScript `Number.prototype.toFixed`, from the exact decimal expansion of
the double: `2.675 → "2.67"` (its binary value is below the tie), `0.125 →
"0.13"` (an exact tie rounds away from zero — as does `-0.125 → "-0.13"`),
`|x| ≥ 1e21` falls back to `String(x)` (`"1e+21"`), NaN / Infinity render as
`"NaN"` / `"Infinity"`. Precision is clamped into JS's 0–100 range (JS throws
`RangeError` outside it).

values.name: validator
values.comment:
Upstream `validator`: `null` passes (an empty input is valid), `NaN` does
not.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-input-number` root: one div wrapping the inner `n-input` with the
buttons threaded through its prefix / suffix slots. Children: element 0 is
the `prefix` slot, element 1 the `suffix` slot (both optional, both wrapped
in `n-input-number-prefix` / `-suffix` spans while `showButton` is on).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.InputNumber.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.InputOtp
comment:
Naive UI's `InputOtp`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Gap, Options, Size, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

    import NUI.InputOtp exposing (defaults)

    NUI.InputOtp.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = model.otp
            , onUpdateValue = Just GotOtp
        }
        []

    NUI.InputOtp.view theme
        { defaults
            | mask = True
            , size = NUI.InputOtp.Small
            , length = 4
            , gap = Just (NUI.InputOtp.Px 16)
        }
        []

(`defaults` must be bound to a local name first — see `NUI.Input`.)

The element carries the `.n-input-otp` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*`
custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. Each slot is an
`NUI.Input.view` (an `n-input`), exactly like upstream's default slot fallback.

**Runtime.** Upstream owns the per-slot value (`useMergedState`) and justifies
it to `length` entries; this library is pure, so the caller owns `value` (the
view re-justifies it to `length` slots for rendering). `onUpdateValue` receives
the value Naive UI reports: the single-character input rule, the multi-character
(paste / autofill) distribution across slots and the `allowInput` filter are
ported from upstream's `handleInput`. What stays with the caller: slot focus
movement (`focusOnChar`, arrow keys, the auto-advance after input — DOM
focus, i.e. `Browser.Dom.focus`), upstream's `onFinish` (derive it
from `onUpdateValue`: every slot non-empty) and the paste / keydown handlers
(`NUI.Input` exposes no such hooks). On rejection by `allowInput` the browser
fires no `input` event, so no message is emitted (matching upstream); a no-op
`onUpdateValue` is only emitted when an already-empty slot is re-input, which
upstream fires and then swallows via a shallow-equality check.

The `slotInputAttributes` seam carries raw attributes onto each built-in
slot's inner `<input>` (upstream's typed default slot lets a caller reach
the inner `NInput` — there is no `inputProps` on `n-input-otp` itself): pass
per-index ids (`\i -> [ HA.id ("otp-" ++ String.fromInt i) ]`) so
`Browser.Dom.focus` can move between slots — the demo app's auto-advance
recipe (examples/src/Sections/Controls.elm) focuses the first empty slot
after every `onUpdateValue`.

The children argument models upstream's typed default slot: element _i_
replaces the built-in input of slot _i_ (pass `[]` for the built-in inputs).
Upstream zeroes each inner input's padding through `builtinThemeOverrides`;
the built-in slots pass that to `NUI.Input.varOverrides`
(`--n-padding-left/right: 0`) — children replacing a slot must do their own
zeroing if they want the same 24–36px-cell geometry.

unions.name: Gap
unions.comment:
A CSS length for the `gap` prop — a pixel count (upstream's `pxfy` number)
or a raw CSS length string.

unions.name: Size
unions.comment: The slot size — Naive UI's `size` prop (`small | medium | large`).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-input-otp` props. `value` is the caller-owned per-slot list (the
view re-justifies it to `length` entries for rendering); `allowInput` is
upstream's same-named filter (character, slot index, current value);
`slotInputAttributes` lands on each built-in slot's inner `<input>`.
aliases.type: { value : List.List String.String, length : Basics.Int, onUpdateValue : Maybe.Maybe (List.List String.String -> msg), allowInput : Maybe.Maybe (String.String -> Basics.Int -> List.List String.String -> Basics.Bool), size : NUI.InputOtp.Size, gap : Maybe.Maybe NUI.InputOtp.Gap, block : Basics.Bool, mask : Basics.Bool, disabled : Basics.Bool, readonly : Basics.Bool, status : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Input.Status, placeholder : Maybe.Maybe String.String, rtl : Basics.Bool, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg), slotInputAttributes : Basics.Int -> List.List (Html.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The raw `--n-*` custom properties an input-otp with these options attaches
(before `NUI.Internal.renderVars` drops `initial`/empty values). Exposed so the
`--n-*` output can be asserted directly; `view` uses exactly this.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.InputOtp.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Six empty medium slots, no gap override (the theme's medium gap), no
mask, no filter, no per-slot attributes.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-input-otp` root: `length` slot elements in a row, children
replacing built-ins per index (upstream's typed default slot), the two
`--n-*` vars from `cssVarsFor` on the root.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.InputOtp.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Internal
comment:
Small shared helpers used by every component.

Naive UI styles every component from two inputs:

1.  BEM class names on the element (`.n-button.n-button--primary`), which carry the
    static structure rules from `css/naive-ui.css`.
2.  `--n-*` CSS custom properties, which carry the themed values. Naive UI emits
    these as an inline `style` attribute; so do we.

Both are attached to elm-ui elements via `Element.htmlAttribute`.

@docs TransitionPhase, transitionClass, isLeavePhase, classIf, classes, cssVars, renderVars, applyVarOverrides

unions.name: TransitionPhase
unions.comment:
A Vue `<Transition>` phase. Naive UI's transitions are runtime state
(`fade-in-scale-up-transition`, `fade-in-transition`, …); this library is pure,
so the caller owns the timing and tells the view which phase to render. The
matching CSS rules ship in the stylesheet. `enter` phases animate an element in,
`leave` phases animate it out (the element must stay mounted until the leave
finishes — see `isLeavePhase`).

values.name: applyVarOverrides
values.comment:
Naive UI's per-instance `builtinThemeOverrides` as a key/value patch over a
component's resolved `--n-*` vars: an override whose key is already a var is
swapped IN PLACE (position/order kept); an unknown key is appended at the END.
`[]` leaves the variable list untouched.
values.type: List.List ( String.String, String.String ) -> List.List ( String.String, String.String ) -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: classIf
values.comment:
`classIf True "x" == [ "x" ]`, `classIf False "x" == []`. Compose a class list
with `List.concat`.

values.name: classes
values.comment:
Join class names into one `class` attribute —
`classes ["n-tag", "n-tag--round"]`.

values.name: cssVars
values.comment:
Attach an inline `style` attribute from a list of declarations —
`--n-*` custom properties in the common case. Naive UI sometimes merges the
themed vars with literal declarations into one `style` attribute on the same
element (Icon's `font-size`/`color`, IconWrapper's `height`/`width`/…); pass them
in the same list rather than adding a second `style` attribute, which the DOM
clobbers. `initial` values (Naive UI's "unset" marker) and empties are dropped.

values.name: isLeavePhase
values.comment:
Whether the phase is a leave — the element is on its way out and must stay
mounted until the animation ends.

values.name: renderVars
values.comment:
Render a var list to the `style` attribute's value (the `k:v;k:v` string
behind `cssVars`) — drops `initial` and empty values the same way, then joins
with `;`. Exposed because several components pre-render the string to share
one literal `style` attribute between element kinds (Card, Code,
ColorPicker, DataTable, DatePicker …).

values.name: transitionClass
values.comment:
The class a phase adds to the transitioning element, e.g.
`transitionClass "fade-in-transition" EnterActive == "fade-in-transition-enter-active"`.

name: NUI.Layout
comment:
Naive UI's `Layout` (and `LayoutContent`), rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Options, Position, content, cssVarsFor, defaults, positionClass, view

    import NUI.Layout exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Layout.view theme
        { defaults | hasSider = True }
        [ NUI.LayoutSider.view theme NUI.LayoutSider.defaults [ Element.text "Sider" ]
        , NUI.Layout.content theme defaults [ Element.text "Content" ]
        ]

`view` renders `n-layout`; `content` renders Naive UI's `LayoutContent` — the
exact same component (upstream literally calls `createLayoutComponent True`)
with one extra `n-layout-content` class. The element carries the `.n-layout`
BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships
Naive UI's exact CSS.

With `hasSider` the scroll container gets Naive UI's inline
`display:flex; flex-wrap:nowrap; width:100%; flex-direction:row` so siders and
content line up in a row.

**Documented gaps** (runtime concerns this pure library leaves to the caller):

  - `scrollTo` — imperative instance method, not modelled.
  - `nativeScrollbar = False` — upstream swaps the scroll container for an
    `NScrollbar`, which is not ported; only the native path is supported and
    `False` currently renders it too.
  - `onScroll` / `scrollbarProps` / `contentClass` — omitted; `contentStyle`
    covers the styling need (extra attributes can go on the children).
  - `siderPlacement` — upstream siders read it from their parent layout; here
    the placement is a direct `NUI.LayoutSider.placement` option.
  - `useReactivated` scroll restore — the caller owns scroll state.

The root is an elm-ui element where upstream uses a plain block `div`; Naive
UI's rules declare every load-bearing property, so the result renders the same
— except for width: an elm-ui `el` defaults to `width shrink` (the `wc` class
pins `align-self: flex-start`), which would shrink-wrap the shell inside a
flex parent, so `view` / `content` explicitly set `width fill` (the block-div
`n-layout` fills its mount).

**Divergence (content padding):** upstream's docs demos pass
`content-style="padding: 24px;"` to every `n-layout-content` / sider; callers
that copy those demos verbatim get an unpadded wall of text otherwise. This
port merges a default `padding: 12px 24px` into `content`'s scroll container
(`view` stays untouched) — a caller's own `contentStyle` pairs land later in
the same declaration block and win.

unions.name: Position
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `position` prop, shared by the whole layout family: `static`
flows in the document, `absolute` pins the element (Naive UI's
`--absolute-positioned` modifier).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-layout` props: positioning, the sider-row flag, the embedded
colour variant, and the scroll container's inline style pairs (`contentStyle`
merges after the template's own pairs — a caller's later pair wins).
aliases.type: { position : NUI.Layout.Position, hasSider : Basics.Bool, embedded : Basics.Bool, nativeScrollbar : Basics.Bool, contentStyle : List.List ( String.String, String.String ), attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: content
values.comment:
Naive UI's `LayoutContent` (`n-layout-content`): the same component as
`view` with the additional `n-layout-content` class. Naive UI's CSS has no rule
for that class — it is a semantic marker — so `view` and `content` render
identically; emit it anyway for parity with upstream's DOM.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Layout.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The raw `--n-*` custom properties a layout with these options attaches.
Exposed so the `--n-*` output can be asserted directly; `view` and `content`
use exactly this.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Layout.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
A static, scrollable, non-embedded layout with no inline styles — the
plain shell Naive UI's docs demos build on.

values.name: positionClass
values.comment:
The `position` suffix upstream's layout family appends to its modifier
classes (`static` / `absolute`) — shared by `NUI.LayoutHeader` /
`NUI.LayoutFooter` / `NUI.LayoutSider` through their `Position` option.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-layout` root (no content class) — `width fill` on the elm-ui root
(see the module docs), the scroll container as its only child.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Layout.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.LayoutFooter
comment:
Naive UI's `LayoutFooter`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Options, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

    import NUI.LayoutFooter exposing (defaults)

    NUI.LayoutFooter.view theme
        { defaults | bordered = True }
        [ Element.text "Footer" ]

The element carries the `.n-layout-footer` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*`
custom properties (`footerColor` / `footerColorInverted` etc. from
`NUI.Theme.Layout`); `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Divergence (visibility chrome):** like `NUI.LayoutHeader`, the non-inverted
footer additionally carries an inline light background (`#f7f7fa`) + padding so
the region reads as part of the app shell on white surfaces (upstream's light
`footerColor` is `rgb(250, 250, 252)`, visually indistinguishable there).
Inverted footers keep the pure `--n-*` theming.

**Divergence (width):** the root sets `width fill`. Upstream's `.n-layout-footer`
is a block `div` (implicitly full width) — unlike `.n-layout-header` it declares
no `width`, so an elm-ui `column` (which defaults to `width shrink`) would
shrink-wrap the strip to its content and leave it narrower than the header it
sits under.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-layout-footer` props: positioning, the bottom border, and the
inverted colour variant (which also opts out of the visibility chrome —
see the module docs).
aliases.type: { position : NUI.Layout.Position, bordered : Basics.Bool, inverted : Basics.Bool, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment: The raw `--n-*` custom properties a footer with these options attaches.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutFooter.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment: A static, borderless, non-inverted footer with no extra attributes.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-layout-footer` element — `width fill` (see the module docs for
why the strip must not shrink-wrap), the footer's `--n-*` vars, and the
non-inverted region chrome merged after them.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutFooter.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.LayoutHeader
comment:
Naive UI's `LayoutHeader`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Options, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

    import NUI.LayoutHeader exposing (defaults)

    NUI.LayoutHeader.view theme
        { defaults | bordered = True }
        [ Element.text "Header" ]

The element carries the `.n-layout-header` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*`
custom properties (`headerColor` / `headerColorInverted` etc. from
`NUI.Theme.Layout`); `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Divergence (visibility chrome):** upstream's light theme paints a header
`#fff` (cardColor) — invisible on the white surfaces the layout demo sits on
(upstream's own docs demos paper over this with a demo `<style>` block). This
port instead emits a light region background (`#f7f7fa`) plus padding inline
on the non-inverted header, so the app-shell structure is self-evident without
caller CSS. Inverted headers keep the pure `--n-*` theming.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-layout-header` props: positioning, the bottom border, and the
inverted colour variant (which also opts out of the visibility chrome —
see the module docs).
aliases.type: { position : NUI.Layout.Position, bordered : Basics.Bool, inverted : Basics.Bool, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment: The raw `--n-*` custom properties a header with these options attaches.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutHeader.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment: A static, borderless, non-inverted header with no extra attributes.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-layout-header` element: the header's `--n-*` vars with the
non-inverted region chrome merged after them, children in a column. Unlike
the footer the header needs no explicit width — upstream's CSS declares
`width: 100%` for it.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutHeader.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.LayoutSider
comment:
Naive UI's `LayoutSider`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs CollapseMode, Options, Placement, Trigger, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

    import NUI.LayoutSider exposing (defaults)

    NUI.LayoutSider.view theme
        { defaults
            | showTrigger = NUI.LayoutSider.ArrowCircle
            , onToggleCollapsed = Just ClickedSiderToggle
        }
        [ Element.text "Sider content" ]

The element carries the `.n-layout-sider` BEM classes, the optional
`.n-layout-toggle-button` / `.n-layout-toggle-bar` trigger and the
`.n-layout-sider__border` bar, plus Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties;
`NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS (including the chevron rotation rules for
`--collapsed` / `--right-placement`).

**`collapsed` is caller-owned.** Upstream keeps an uncontrolled state and
flips it when the trigger is clicked; this library is pure, so the caller owns
the flag and the trigger click reports through
`onToggleCollapsed (not collapsed)`. The `max-width` transition Naive UI runs
between the two states is pure CSS and works once the caller updates the flag.

**Documented gaps** (runtime concerns this pure library leaves to the caller):

  - `scrollTo` — imperative instance method, not modelled.
  - `onAfterEnter` / `onAfterLeave` — upstream fires them from the
    `transitionend` of `max-width`; the caller can listen for that transition
    on the root element.
  - `nativeScrollbar = False` — upstream swaps the scroll container for an
    `NScrollbar`, which is not ported; only the native path is supported and
    `False` currently renders it too. That also means the theme's internal
    `invertScrollbar` flag (upstream `__invertScrollbar`, a non-`--n-*` key
    used only to recolour that scrollbar in inverted siders) is not emitted.
  - `defaultCollapsed` — subsumed by the caller-owned `collapsed`.
  - `onScroll`, `scrollbarProps`, `triggerClass` / `triggerStyle` /
    `collapsedTriggerClass` / `collapsedTriggerStyle` — omitted.
  - `placement` is a direct option; upstream siders instead read the parent
    layout's `siderPlacement` prop (Vue provide/inject).

Length props are strings that must carry their own unit (`"272px"`, `"20%"`);
upstream's `formatLength` turns bare numbers into `px`, so write `272` as
`"272px"`.

**Divergences (visibility chrome + collapsed clipping):**

  - The non-inverted sider carries an inline light background (`#fafafc`) plus
    a default scroll-container padding, so the region reads as part of the app
    shell on white surfaces (upstream's light `siderColor` is `#fff`; its docs
    demos paper over that with demo CSS). Inverted siders keep the pure
    `--n-*` theming.
  - In `ByTransform` collapse mode upstream keeps `min-width: width` on the
    scroll container while the root collapses to `collapsedWidth` — and since
    nothing clips (the sider root has no `overflow: hidden`; the toggle bar
    deliberately lives at `right: -28px`), the still-full-width content paints
    past the collapsed sider over the neighbouring content. This port clamps
    the container's `min-width` to `collapsedWidth` once collapsed, so the
    content clips at the sider boundary instead. (The pure port renders end
    states, so the transition-reflow the `min-width` existed for does not
    apply.)

unions.name: CollapseMode
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `collapseMode`: `width` animates the sider's own width,
`transform` keeps the content at full `width` (a `min-width` on the scroll
container) and lets the `max-width` clip it.

unions.name: Placement
unions.comment:
Which side of the content the sider sits on (upstream reads the parent
layout's `siderPlacement`; here it is a direct option). `Right` flips the
border, the trigger and the chevron via `--right-placement` rules.

unions.name: Trigger
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `showTrigger`: no trigger, the arrow-circle button
(`.n-layout-toggle-button`, upstream's `true` / `'arrow-circle'`) or the
inset bar (`.n-layout-toggle-bar`, `'bar'`).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-layout-sider` props. `collapsed` is caller-owned (see the module
docs); the length props (`width` / `collapsedWidth`) are CSS length strings
that carry their own unit; `contentStyle` merges into the scroll container's
inline style after the template's own pairs.
aliases.type: { position : NUI.Layout.Position, placement : NUI.LayoutSider.Placement, bordered : Basics.Bool, collapsed : Basics.Bool, onToggleCollapsed : Maybe.Maybe (Basics.Bool -> msg), collapsedWidth : String.String, width : String.String, collapseMode : NUI.LayoutSider.CollapseMode, showCollapsedContent : Basics.Bool, showTrigger : NUI.LayoutSider.Trigger, inverted : Basics.Bool, nativeScrollbar : Basics.Bool, contentClass : String.String, contentStyle : List.List ( String.String, String.String ), attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The raw `--n-*` custom properties a sider with these options attaches
(plus the `max-width` / `width` inline styles `view` merges into the same
declaration). Exposed so the `--n-*` output can be asserted directly.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutSider.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
A left-placed, expanded, borderless, non-inverted sider: `272px` wide,
collapsing to `48px` by transform with its content shown, no trigger, native
scrollbar, no inline styles.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-layout-sider` root: the classes, the `--n-*` vars plus the
`max-width` / `width` inline pair (and the non-inverted region chrome),
the scroll container, then the optional trigger and border elements.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LayoutSider.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.List
comment:
Naive UI's `List` and `ListItem`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Item, Options, cssVarsFor, defaults, item, view

    import NUI.List exposing (item)

    NUI.List.view theme
        NUI.List.defaults
        [ { item | content = [ Element.text "First" ] }
        , { item
            | prefix = Just (Element.text "•")
            , content = [ Element.text "Second" ]
            , suffix = Just (Element.text "→")
          }
        ]

The element carries the `.n-list` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

markup or the variables, so it is not modelled).

name: NUI.LoadingBar
comment:
Naive UI's `LoadingBar` — the bar itself, rebuilt on elm-ui.

@docs Options, State, Status, cssVarsFor, defaults, error, finish, init
@docs kick, start, startFromTo, view

    import NUI.Internal as I
    import NUI.LoadingBar as LoadingBar


    -- a full run, driven from the caller's update (phase + transition
    -- together; `kick` one animation frame after `start`):
    --
    --   StartLoading  -> LoadingBar.start { model | phase = Just I.EnterFrom }
    --   Kick          -> LoadingBar.kick                    -- next frame
    --   FinishLoading -> LoadingBar.finish { model | phase = Just I.LeaveFrom }
    --
    --   view: LoadingBar.view theme LoadingBar.defaults model

The element is Naive UI's own DOM: one `div.n-loading-bar-container` (fixed to
the top of the viewport) wrapping one `div.n-loading-bar
.n-loading-bar--{status}` whose inline `max-width` is the progress. The
`--n-*` custom properties come from `NUI.Theme.LoadingBar` and `NUI.Css`
ships Naive UI's exact CSS — including the `max-width 4s linear` tween for
`--starting` and the `.2s` ones for `--finishing` / `--error`.

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream mounts the bar inside a `LoadingBarProvider`
and drives it imperatively (`useLoadingBar()` → `start` / `finish` / `error`),
mutating the live DOM node across `nextTick`s — `el.className = …`,
`el.style.maxWidth = …`, `el.style.transition = 'none'` … `''`, with forced
reflashes (`void el.offsetWidth`, LoadingBar.tsx:70-77). The provider, the
teleport (`to`), and the composable are not ported; the component is a pure
state machine the caller steps (the `NUI.Countdown` precedent), and `view`
renders exactly the DOM those mutations would have produced:

  - `start` / `startFromTo` — upstream `start()` (LoadingBar.tsx:58-77;
    defaults `0 → 80`): a fresh run whose `runId` change remounts the bar
    (keyed), so it reappears at `from` instead of tweening from the previous
    run's width, with an inline `transition: none` so the first frame paints
    `from` without animating.
  - `kick` — invoke one frame after `start` (e.g. from
    `Browser.Events.onAnimationFrame`); it moves the bar to `toProgress` and
    drops the inline `transition: none`, letting the CSS tween `max-width`
    take over. This replaces upstream's forced-reflow dance
    (LoadingBar.tsx:73-76).
  - `finish` — upstream `finish()` (LoadingBar.tsx:79-92): `--finishing`
    (the CSS retargets `max-width` to `100%` in `.2s`) and hides the bar.
    No-op unless a run is loading — upstream's live `finishing || erroring`
    guard (LoadingBar.tsx:80-81).
  - `error` — upstream `error()` (LoadingBar.tsx:94-117): mid-run it switches
    to `--error` and tweens to `100%` (the `.2s` retarget); from idle it
    starts an already-finished error run (upstream's `start(100, 100,
    'error')`, LoadingBar.tsx:99-107). No-op while a finish/error is still
    fading out (see the guard divergence below).
  - `init` — `started = False`; the view renders `Element.none` (upstream:
    `if (!this.started) return null`, LoadingBar.tsx:171-172).

**Visibility.** Upstream shows the container via `v-show` on `loading ||
(!loading && entering)` — i.e. `loading || entering` — inside a
`<Transition name="fade-in-transition" appear>` (LoadingBar.tsx:176-209); a
hiding element only collapses once the `.8s` leave fade has finished, and
`handleAfterLeave` then resets the flags (LoadingBar.tsx:125-127). The port
keeps the bar painted for EVERY status a started run can hold — `--starting`
tweens, and `--finishing` / `--error` settle at `100%` (red for `--error`)
— so a finished/errored run is visible at its final width; an enter/leave
fade phase (upstream's `entering`, plus the leave hold) additionally keeps
the container mounted mid-fade. `display: none` is emitted only for a
not-started run, which `view` already renders as `Element.none`. The fade
phases themselves are caller-driven (the `NUI.BackTop` / `NUI.Spin`
precedent) — no timers live here:

  - on `start` (or an idle `error`), set `phase = Just I.EnterFrom` in the
    same update (upstream's `appear` / v-show enter), advance to
    `I.EnterActive` next frame and clear to `Nothing` after the `.3s` fade;
  - on `finish` / `error`, set `phase = Just I.LeaveFrom` in the same update,
    advance to `I.LeaveActive` and clear after the `.8s` fade — that clear is
    the port's `handleAfterLeave`: it releases the finish/error no-op guard
    (the container itself stays painted at `100%` — see Visibility). Leave
    phases keep the container mounted and visible mid-fade
    (`I.isLeavePhase`, the `NUI.Spin` hold).

**Divergences from upstream** (everything else is a faithful port):

  - **Provider skipped.** No `LoadingBarProvider` / `useLoadingBar` /
    teleport (`to`): the caller owns one `State`, renders the bar where it
    wants it, and passes the provider's props (`containerClass`,
    `containerStyle`, `loadingBarStyle`) as `Options` instead.
  - **The reflow dance is data.** Upstream juggles `className` / `maxWidth` /
    `transition` imperatively across `nextTick`s; the port encodes the same
    frames declaratively (`kicked`, the `runId` keyed remount). One transient
    upstream frame disappears: the just-mounted bar with the bare
    `n-loading-bar` class (no modifier, no `max-width`, transparent) before
    `start`'s callback lands — here `start` sets the status atomically, with
    the same (invisible) rendering.
  - **A settled `--finishing` / `--error` run stays painted.** Upstream's
    `v-show` retargets to `false` the moment `loading` clears (on
    `finish` / `error`), so the bar survives only the `.8s` leave fade before
    `handleAfterLeave` collapses it. The port has no collapse signal once the
    caller clears the phase, so `isDisplayed` keeps a finished/errored run
    visible at its final width — the frozen static demos (which call
    `finish` / `error` with no phase) rely on it.
  - **`transitionDisabled` / `css=false`** — upstream's flag that keeps
    Vue's transition engine from fighting those imperative style writes
    (LoadingBar.tsx:34, 52-53, 183) — has no equivalent; the pure port has no
    such race.
  - **Guard window.** Upstream holds the `finishing || erroring` no-op guard
    from `finish`/`error` until the leave fade ends
    (`handleAfterLeave` → `init()`); the port holds it while a `Leave` phase
    is set. A second `error` in the very same update as the first
    `error`/`finish` — before the caller has attached the `Leave` phase —
    restarts the run instead of no-oping. Unreachable when the recipe above
    is followed (set the `Leave` phase together with `finish`/`error`).
  - **`loadingBarStyle`** — upstream accepts `string | CSSProperties` per
    variant (LoadingBar.tsx:43-48); the port takes raw CSS strings, merged
    verbatim after the themed vars and `max-width` (so the fragment wins on
    conflicts), the `error` variant picked while erroring. Same for
    `containerStyle` (a raw fragment on the container, after the view's own
    `display: none`).
  - **`inlineThemeDisabled` / `themeClass`** mode is not ported — the port
    always emits the inline `--n-*` vars on the bar (upstream's default
    mode, LoadingBar.tsx:200-206).
  - **`attributes` exists for record parity only** — the root is raw HTML
    (`Element.html`, the `NUI.Highlight` / `NUI.Heatmap` precedent: an
    `Element.Attribute` cannot attach to a raw node), so it is unused.

unions.name: Status
unions.comment:
The bar's status — upstream's `createClassName` argument
(LoadingBar.tsx:14-19): `--starting` (loading tween), `--finishing`
(completing), `--error` (failed).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The provider-side props upstream threads from `LoadingBarProvider`:
the container's extra class / style, and the per-variant raw style fragment
for the bar (the `error` one picked while erroring). `attributes` exists for
record parity only (the root is raw `Html`; see the module docs).
aliases.type: { containerClass : Maybe.Maybe String.String, containerStyle : Maybe.Maybe String.String, loadingBarStyle : Maybe.Maybe { loading : String.String, error : String.String }, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

aliases.name: State
aliases.comment:
One run of the bar. `started` mounts the container; `status` drives the
bar's modifier class (and doubles as upstream's `loading` flag —
`Starting` ⇔ loading); `progress` is the rendered `max-width` percentage and
`toProgress` where `kick` tweens to; `runId` keys the bar element so a new
run remounts instead of tweening from the old width; `kicked` is upstream's
post-reflow frame (the inline `transition: none` is emitted until it is set);
`phase` is the container's `fade-in-transition` phase (caller-driven — see
the module docs).
aliases.type: { started : Basics.Bool, status : NUI.LoadingBar.Status, progress : Basics.Float, toProgress : Basics.Float, runId : Basics.Int, kicked : Basics.Bool, phase : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The raw `--n-*` custom properties the bar attaches — upstream's
`cssVarsRef` (LoadingBar.tsx:136-144). Exposed so the `--n-*` output can be
asserted directly; `view` uses exactly this.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
No container class / style, no bar style overrides — upstream's bare
provider defaults.

values.name: error
values.comment:
Upstream's `error()` (LoadingBar.tsx:94-117). Mid-run: `--error` and a
`.2s` tween to `100%`. From idle (never started, or a previous run whose
leave fade has ended — upstream resets its flags in `handleAfterLeave`, the
clear of the `Leave` phase here): the `start(100, 100, 'error')` run
(LoadingBar.tsx:99-107), which shows a finished red bar; drive it like a
`start` (an `EnterFrom` phase for the appear, then the leave). No-op while a
finish/error is still fading out (a `Leave` phase is held).

values.name: finish
values.comment:
Upstream's `finish()` (LoadingBar.tsx:79-92). No-op unless a run is
loading — upstream's `finishing || erroring` guard (which for `finish` is
observably a no-op in every other state too: a settled bar is hidden either
way).

values.name: init
values.comment:
Upstream's idle state: not started (the view renders `Element.none`),
`Starting`, progress 0 staging 80, run 0, not kicked, no phase.

values.name: kick
values.comment:
Upstream's reflow frame (LoadingBar.tsx:73-76): the caller invokes this
one animation frame after `start`, which re-enables the CSS transition and
moves the bar to `toProgress`.

values.name: start
values.comment: Upstream's `start()` with its defaults — `start(0, 80, 'starting')`.

values.name: startFromTo
values.comment:
Upstream's `start(fromProgress, toProgress, 'starting')`
(LoadingBar.tsx:58-77): mounts the container, resets the bar to `from` with
the transition disabled (the `runId` remount + inline `transition: none`),
and stages `to` for `kick`.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The container element — `Element.none` for a not-started run (upstream's
`if (!this.started) return null`), else the fixed `n-loading-bar-container`
holding the `runId`-keyed bar. Mount it wherever the caller wants the bar
(upstream's teleport target).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.LoadingBar.Options msg -> NUI.LoadingBar.State -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Log
comment:
Naive UI's `Log` (`n-log`), rebuilt as a pure pane composing `NUI.Code` and
`NUI.Scrollbar`.

@docs LogEvent, Options, Panel, SpinOverrides, defaults, mergedLines
@docs scrollEvents, styleHeight, view, wheelEvents

    import NUI.Log as Log

    Log.view theme
        { Log.defaults
            | lines = [ "first line", "second line" ]
            , rows = 5
        }

The DOM is Naive UI's own: `div.n-log` (line-height + height + the 6 `--n-*`
vars) wraps an `n-scrollbar` whose content is an `n-code` (with a default slot,
so Code emits no `.__code__`) holding one `pre` per line, plus a
`div.n-log-loader` (an `n-base-loading` spinner + a content span) shown while
`loading`. `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream measures the scroll container and throttles
`wheel` (`Log.tsx:115-174`); this library is pure, so the port exposes the
render surface, the pure event algebra (`scrollEvents` / `wheelEvents` returning
`LogEvent`s), and `styleHeight`. The caller owns the scrolling, throttling and
`scrollTo` silent flag (the service/caller pattern of `NUI.Upload` /
`NUI.Carousel`); `attributes` land on the root `div.n-log`.

**Highlight.** `language = Just _` (even `""`) means "highlight"; each line is
run through `NUI.Code.codeHtml` with the SAME gates (`LogLine.tsx:35-46`), and
falls back to the trimmed/raw text when there is no hljs or the language is
unknown. `trim` is applied PER LINE and defaults to `False` here (⚠ `NUI.Code`'s
default is `True`).

**Divergences (`[D]`):**

  - `[D]` `wheel` is throttled 300 ms upstream (lodash); the port is pure, so
    `wheelEvents` is the unthrottled body — the caller throttles.
  - `[D]` `scrollTo` / `silentRef` and the deprecated `scrollToTop` /
    `scrollToBottom` are imperative (`NUI.Scrollbar` has no instance method);
    they are the caller's, and the silent-scroll suppression is too.
  - `[D]` `loadingText` is a port convenience (`Maybe String`); upstream always
    reads the `Log.loading` locale (`locales/common/enUS.ts:91-93`, `'Loading'`).
    `Nothing` (or `Just ""`) yields `"Loading"` via `Maybe.withDefault` — this
    port adds the field, so there is no upstream JS-truthiness to mirror.
  - `[D]` `LogLine` sets the per-line highlight with `innerHTML`
    (`LogLine.tsx:35-46`); elm/html blocks that path (see `NUI.Code`), so each
    line's resolved string is parsed by `NUI.Internal.RawHtml` — the highlight
    renders as real elements, and its recovery semantics are docstringed.
  - `[D]` The `NBaseLoading` `NIconSwitchTransition` wrapper adds no node and
    `show` is always `true` here, so the `.__placeholder` branch never renders.
  - `[D]` Log passes the single global `Theme` to the embedded Code/Scrollbar;
    upstream threads a peer theme (extract-theme only reads `self`, so peers
    never reach the generated Elm theme).
  - `[oracle R4]` the root and the loader are `Element.column`s (elm-ui flex
    columns) where upstream mounts bare `div`s — layout-neutral here EXCEPT
    width: the cssr declares every load-bearing property of `.n-log` /
    `.n-log-loader` (`position`, `height`, absolute placement), but upstream's
    block-div width (fill the container) must be re-asserted via
    `Element.width Element.fill` because elm-ui's column default is
    width-content (see `view`); the loader is the last child either way.

unions.name: LogEvent
unions.comment:
The scroll/wheel outcomes as messages (`LogEvents`): `RequireMoreFrom panel`
is upstream's `onRequireMore(from)`, plus `onReachTop` / `onReachBottom`.

unions.name: Panel
unions.comment: Which end of the log a `RequireMoreFrom` refers to.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `n-log` options (`logProps`, `Log.tsx:46-81`), with Elm message channels
in place of Vue listeners. `attributes` land on the root `div.n-log` (wire the
scroll/wheel handlers there).
aliases.type: { loading : Basics.Bool, trim : Basics.Bool, log : Maybe.Maybe String.String, lines : List.List String.String, fontSize : Basics.Int, lineHeight : Basics.Float, language : Maybe.Maybe String.String, rows : Basics.Int, offsetTop : Basics.Int, offsetBottom : Basics.Int, hljs : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Code.Hljs, spinProps : NUI.Log.SpinOverrides, loadingText : Maybe.Maybe String.String, loaderTransition : Maybe.Maybe NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

aliases.name: SpinOverrides
aliases.comment:
The `NBaseLoading` overrides `LogSpinProps` re-exports (`SharedSpinProps`);
each field falls through to the `LogLoader` call site / `NBaseLoading` default.
aliases.type: { strokeWidth : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int, stroke : Maybe.Maybe String.String, scale : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Float, radius : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int }

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Upstream defaults, byte-for-byte: `trim = False` (⚠ `Code`'s is `True`),
`fontSize = 14`, `lineHeight = 1.25`, `rows = 15`, offsets `0`, `lines = []`.

values.name: mergedLines
values.comment:
`mergedLines` (`Log.tsx:99-105`): a TRUTHY `log` string is split on `"\n"`;
`Nothing` (or `Just ""`) falls through to `lines`. (`log = ""` is falsy in JS.)

values.name: scrollEvents
values.comment:
`handleScroll` (`Log.tsx:115-142`): `<=` on both ends; `RequireMoreFrom`
precedes `ReachX` within a block; both blocks CAN fire in one event.
values.type: { scrollTop : Basics.Int, containerHeight : Basics.Int, contentHeight : Basics.Int, offsetTop : Basics.Int, offsetBottom : Basics.Int } -> List.List NUI.Log.LogEvent

values.name: styleHeight
values.comment:
`styleHeight` (`Log.tsx:94-98`): `calc(${Math.round(rows * lineHeight *
fontSize)}px)`. Elm's `round` is `Math.round` (ties toward +∞), so `262.5` ->
`263`.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The `n-log` element. The root is an elm-ui flex column so the absolutely
positioned loader resolves against it (`.n-log { position: relative }`).

values.name: wheelEvents
values.comment:
`_handleWheel` (`Log.tsx:162-171`): top uses STRICT `scrollTop === 0` (and
`deltaY < 0`); bottom uses `scrollBottom <= 0` (and `deltaY > 0`). `offsetTop` /
`offsetBottom` are NOT consulted.
values.type: { scrollTop : Basics.Int, containerHeight : Basics.Int, contentHeight : Basics.Int, deltaY : Basics.Float } -> List.List NUI.Log.LogEvent

name: NUI.Marquee
comment:
Naive UI's `Marquee`, rebuilt on elm-ui — the infinitely scrolling strip
(announcement tickers, one-line news crawls, status runs) built from two
copies of the same content sliding side by side.

    import NUI.Marquee exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Marquee.view theme
        { defaults | duration = 12 }
        [ Element.text "Scrolling text" ]

The element carries the `.n-marquee` BEM classes and the animation `--n-*`
custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS (including the
`n-marquee` keyframes).

**Runtime.** Upstream measures the content and container widths with a
`ResizeObserver` and derives the duration (and, with `auto-fill`, the repeat
count). This library is pure, so the caller owns those numbers: pass the scroll
`duration` in seconds directly, and — for `autoFill` — the `repeat` count
(`repeatCountInOneGroup`). The rendered DOM (two `__group`s, one item repeated)
is exactly upstream's.

@docs Options, defaults, view, cssVarsFor

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The marquee options. Three fields are the caller-owned replacement for
upstream's measured runtime (see the module docs): `duration` is the scroll
span — upstream computes `contentWidth * repeatCount / speed` (its `speed`
prop defaults to `48`) and this port takes the seconds directly, so the
upstream default `duration = 0` renders a _stationary_ strip exactly as an
unmeasured upstream marquee does (its `contentWidth` starts at `-1`);
`play` maps `--n-play` (`False` pauses the animation); and with `autoFill`
on, `repeat` is the `repeatCountInOneGroup` upstream derives as
`ceil(containerWidth / contentWidth)` — the item count per group (group one
keeps one original plus `repeat - 1` mirrors; group two repeats `repeat`
mirrors). `attributes` land on the root `n-marquee` element.
aliases.type: { duration : Basics.Float, play : Basics.Bool, autoFill : Basics.Bool, repeat : Basics.Int, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The animation custom properties upstream computes from its measurements —
here supplied directly by the caller (see the module note).

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Upstream's implicit state before any measurement: running, not
auto-filling, one copy per group, a `0s` duration (the animation is a no-op
until the caller supplies one).

values.name: view
values.comment:
The scrolling strip: the root `n-marquee` element (plus `--auto-fill`
when `options.autoFill`) carrying the animation vars and the caller's
`attributes`, wrapping the two `n-marquee__group` rows — the first holds the
original item plus the auto-fill mirrors, the second the mirror run. The
children are the slot content, rendered once per item (both the original and
every mirror get the same list).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Marquee.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

name: NUI.Mention
comment:
Naive UI's `Mention` — an `NUI.Input` trigger plus a caller-mounted
`NUI.SelectMenu` body. Upstream (`Mention.tsx`) mounts `NInput` in a
VBinder target and `NInternalSelectMenu` in the follower — Mention is
NOT an `NInternalSelection` consumer (same family as AutoComplete, but
NOT a verbatim copy: three load-bearing divergences, frozen below).

    import NUI.Mention as Mention
    import NUI.SelectMenu

    Mention.view theme
        { Mention.defaults | onInput = Just Typed }
    Mention.menu theme Mention.menuDefaults
        [ SelectMenu.Option
            { value = "710mechgy"
            , label = "710mechgy"
            , disabled = False
            , attributes = []
            }
        ]

Trigger (`view`) DOM — the `.n-mention` wrapper is bare (no vars, no
state classes; all styling lives on the `.n-input` and the menu), and
its cssr is NOT the auto-complete twin: `width: 100%; z-index: auto;
position: relative` — no `display: inline-flex`:

    div.n
        - mention
        └─ NUI.Input.view (see its docstring for the full tree)

`view` maps per-field: `value` / `onInput` (typing; there is no clear
icon — Mention passes no `clearable`), `placeholder` (default `""` —
upstream `Mention.tsx` default is the empty string, NOT AutoComplete's
baked `"Please Input"`), `size` (small / medium / large — no `tiny`;
keys the INPUT only), `type_` (text / textarea — NO `password`,
upstream's union is two-valued), `autosize` (the `NUI.Input` seam:
emits `n-input--autosize`, suppresses `n-input--resizable`; the height
measurement is caller-owned), `status` (re-bound to `NUI.Input.Status`),
`disabled`, `bordered`, `rtl` (the input's `--rtl`; upstream's own cssr
has no rtl block), and `attributes` (wrapper). Mention exercises NO
other input feature — no `clearable`, no `loading` on the trigger, no
prefix / suffix slots (upstream's `prefix` PROP is the trigger
character(s), not a slot), no `inputProps` (hence no `inputAttributes`
field here).

Menu (`menu`) DOM — the `NUI.SelectMenu` body carrying Mention's own
class and vars:

    div.n-base-select-menu .n-base-select-menu--medium-size
        [--rtl] .n-mention-menu [fade-in-scale-up-transition-*]
      tabindex = -1   (NOT focusable — upstream omits the prop,
                       InternalSelectMenu defaults it false → -1)
      style = 23 menu vars at Medium → --n-menu-box-shadow
              (24 declarations; the port emits --n-bezier once)
      └─ NUI.SelectMenu rows — value stays `Single Nothing`: no row is
         ever `--selected` and no checkmark NODE renders
         (`--show-checkmark` still lands on rows); `multiple = False`;
         `loading` = the MENU's `__loading` row when `MenuOptions.loading`
         is True

The menu is hardcoded Medium (upstream passes no `size`, the menu
defaults it) — the trigger's `size` never keys it, and the follower
gets NO `width` upstream (AutoComplete passes `width="target"`; the
Mention menu is content-sized — do not stretch it to the input's
width). `--rtl` rides the menu through `MenuOptions.rtl`.

**The three divergences from AutoComplete (do not copy-paste past
them):**

1.  `loading` lands on the MENU (`n-base-select-menu__loading` row),
    never the input suffix — the exact opposite of AutoComplete, whose
    loading is the input spinner. `MenuOptions.loading` wires it.
2.  Upstream Mention FILTERS internally (`filter` prop, live default;
    `filteredOptionsRef`). AutoComplete renders everything it is given.
    The port drops the engine — the caller pre-filters and passes the
    already-filtered list. The frozen default predicate:
    `!pattern → True`; else `label` string → `String.startsWith pattern
    label`; else `value` string → `String.startsWith pattern value`;
    else `False`.
3.  The wrapper CSS differs (see above) and `placeholder` defaults to
    `""`.

Options are `NUI.SelectMenu.Option` verbatim: upstream's
`MentionOption = SelectBaseOption<string>` (value string, label
string / render, disabled, class, style) — there are NO bare-string
options upstream (unlike AutoComplete), hence no `fromString`. Groups
map 1:1 through `SelectMenu.Group`; `renderLabel` becomes label
strings / `Custom` rows.

Caller-owned runtime (the port-wide convention): the whole show gate —
the menu is open iff the input is `document.activeElement` AND the
caret (`selectionEnd`) sits in a `prefix`-introduced run with no
`separator` / `\n` / `\r` between the prefix character and the caret
(scan backward from `selectionEnd - 1` down to 0; a separator or
newline ends any pattern; the first char found in `prefix` — default
`@`, string or list of single-char strings — opens the menu); close on
blur, on a separator / newline crossing, on Enter-with-no-pending.
There is NO clickoutside directive upstream — closing is blur +
re-scan driven. `onSearch(pattern, prefix)` fires each time a prefix is
detected, with `pattern = String.slice (prefixIndex + 1)
selectionEnd inputValue`. The select commit (upstream
`handleSelect`): with the cached prefix and pattern boundaries,
`rest = String.slice end inputValue`; `alreadySeparated =
String.startsWith separator rest`; `middle = option.value ++
(alreadySeparated ? "" : separator)`; the new value is
`String.slice 0 start inputValue ++ middle ++ rest`; the caret moves
to `start + String.length middle + (alreadySeparated ? 1 : 0)`; then
re-derive the show gate. `separator` defaults to `" "` (length 1).
Keyboard: the input owns every key — ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Enter with
the menu open preventDefault and drive the menu (prev / next / select
the pending option; Enter with no pending closes); ArrowLeft /
ArrowRight re-scan; IME-composing keys are ignored; there is NO Escape
or Tab handling. Pending: `autoPending` inits to the first available
option on every open (value is never set, so no row is ever pending by
selection). Positioning: upstream anchors the follower to a 0-width
caret div positioned by mirror-div measurement (`utils.ts`, vendored
`textarea-caret-ts`) — un-portable; the caller positions the menu
(`placement` default `bottom-start`). Focus / blur inst methods; IME.

Dropped: the `filter` prop (caller pre-filters — the default predicate
is frozen above); `to` / `zIndex` / `placement` (caller positioning);
`internalDebug`; the `default` slot (upstream forwards it as the menu's
children — render `Custom` rows instead); `renderLabel` (label strings
/ `Custom` rows); the object `autosize` (caller sets `rows`).
`scrollbarProps` has no `NUI.SelectMenu` seam (the plain option-wrapper
path is the port's render) — the field stays for the caller, the
`NUI.Select` precedent. Values are `String` (upstream `string | null`;
null ≡ "").

values.comment:
The bare `.n-mention` wrapper + the `NUI.Input` trigger, mapped per
the module docstring (no `display: inline-flex` — the wrapper cssr is
`width: 100%; z-index: auto; position: relative`).

**Explicit-width seam.** The wrapper's cssr is `.nui-root.nui-root
.n-mention { width: 100% }` (specificity 0,3,0), which beats elm-ui's
own `Element.width (px n)` class on the same node (`.we.width-px-n`,
0,1,0) — so an explicit trigger width `Element.width`ed onto `attributes`
was silently dropped. The port therefore lands the caller's `attributes`
on an OUTER elm-ui node and keeps the `n-mention` wrapper on the inner
one: a caller width then sizes the outer node (no competing rule) and the
inner `.n-mention` still fills it via its `width: 100%` rule, while the
default (no caller width) fills the available width (`Element.width
Element.fill` prepended — elm-ui reverses the attribute list and keeps the
FIRST `Width` attribute it reaches, so a caller `Element.width` in
`attributes` still wins over the default fill).

name: NUI.Menu
comment:
Naive UI's `Menu` — the vertical/horizontal navigation tree. Upstream is
one public component (`NMenu`) over a treemate options tree (the Cascader
shape); `NSubmenu` / `NMenuOption` / `NMenuOptionGroup` / `MenuDivider` are
internal and render here as one recursive walk (upstream `itemRenderer`).

    import NUI.Menu as Menu
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Menu.view Theme.default
        { menuD
            | value = Just "pos-1"
            , expandedKeys = [ "sub-1" ]
            , onSelect = Just Selected
            , onExpandedKeysChange = Just ExpandedKeys
        }
        [ Menu.Option
            { key = "sub-1"
            , label = "Submenu"
            , extra = Nothing
            , icon = Nothing
            , disabled = False
            , children =
                Just
                    [ Menu.Option
                        { key = "pos-1", label = "Option", extra = Nothing, icon = Nothing, disabled = False, children = Nothing, attributes = [] }
                    ]
            , attributes = []
            }
        , Menu.Divider { attributes = [] }
        ]

**DOM** (vertical; leaf, submenu, group, divider):

    div.n-menu.n-menu--vertical [style: 43 --n-* vars; role=menu]
    ├─ div.n-menu-item [role=menuitem]
    │   └─ div.n-menu-item-content(--selected) [padding-left]
    │       ├─ div.n-menu-item-content__icon [w/h/font-size/margin-right]
    │       └─ div.n-menu-item-content-header > (text | span.__extra)
    ├─ div.n-submenu [role=menu; aria-expanded]
    │   ├─ div.n-menu-item > div.n-menu-item-content(--child-active) (+__arrow)
    │   └─ div.n-submenu-children [role=menu] > …
    ├─ div.n-menu-item-group [role=group]
    │   ├─ div.n-menu-item-group-title [padding-left] > (text | text extra)
    │   └─ div > …
    └─ div.n-menu-divider

Horizontal swaps `--vertical`/`role=menu` for `--horizontal`/`role=menubar`,
drops arrows, indent and inline submenu children, and nulls dividers;
`--collapsed` (menu-collapsed, vertical) renders icon-only rows with
upstream's centering arithmetic (`padding-left = collapsedWidth/2 −
maxIconSize/2`, `icon-margin-right` compensation).

**The state contract.** `value` and `expandedKeys` are caller state (upstream's
controlled props); the view emits `onSelect` (leaf click → key; upstream
`on-update:value` without the raw option) and `onExpandedKeysChange` (submenu
toggle → the whole new list, accordion applied — upstream `toggleExpand`).
Pure helpers mirror upstream's imperative/uncontrolled seams:
`initialExpandedKeys` (`defaultExpandAll` / the value's ancestor path —
upstream's uncontrolled init), `toggleExpanded` (accordion: expanding a
level-1 submenu closes the first open level-1 sibling), `expandTo`
(`MenuInst.showOption`, accordion-aware), `keyPathTo` (treemate
`getPath().keyPath`).

**The popover seam.** Everything in `NUI.Popover`'s docstring about the
caller-owned runtime applies: upstream horizontal submenus, menu-collapsed
submenus (`NDropdown`) and menu-collapsed leaf labels (`NTooltip`) are
teleported popovers. The port renders the full inline DOM — the trigger rows
included — and exports `submenuDropdownOptions`, the pure `rawNodes →
NDropdown options` mapping upstream hands its popovers, so a caller mounting
`NUI.Dropdown.view` bodies (upstream config: size `Large`,
`fontSizeLarge 14px`, `optionIconSizeLarge 18px`, `dropdownPlacement`,
`inverted`, hover trigger, `placementAttribute` on the wrapper) reproduces
the popover layer.

**Divergences from upstream (documented):**

  - No popover body mounts (above); the `--hover` content modifier (upstream:
    popover-open state) is never emitted.
  - Submenu expand animation: upstream `NFadeInExpandTransition` measures
    heights at runtime; the cssr `fade-in-height-expand-*` rules are
    extracted and `transition` carries the phase classes — the caller owns
    the clock (cf. `NUI.Modal` / `NUI.Dropdown` `transition` fields).
  - `responsive` (VOverflow measurement, the `__ellpisisGroup__` counter,
    `deriveResponsiveState`) and `watchProps` (Vue controlled/uncontrolled
    re-sync) are not ported; `collapsed` is explicit (upstream can inherit it
    from `NLayoutSider`).
  - `label`/`icon`/`extra` replace the `label|title`/`titleExtra` aliases and
    the `render*` hooks; the `*Field` overrides are not modelled (typed
    records); `nodeProps` becomes per-option `attributes` (leaf/submenu: the
    `n-menu-item` wrapper; group: the title div — upstream puts them there);
    `expandIcon` is the inlined filled chevron (house style, cf.
    `NUI.BaseSelection`); `dropdownProps`/`domId` ride the caller's popover;
    `dropdownPlacement` is carried for that seam (upstream default `bottom` —
    the docs' `top` is wrong; code wins).
  - `show === false` options are omitted by the caller (cf. `NUI.Dropdown`);
    `type: 'render'` options are not modelled — upstream drops them silently
    (their `render` field is never called).
  - Upstream quirk kept: menu-level `disabled` flows into submenus (it is
    checked in `NSubmenu` only), never into root-level options or groups.
    Group `disabled` is likewise an injection its LEAF children read — a
    submenu (or nested group) under a disabled group stays alive, and a leaf
    under `submenu > group` reads the submenu's merged state and ignores the
    group's (upstream's `NSubmenu ? … : …` ternary).
  - Upstream's leading-space text nodes before `extra` are kept (`" extra"`).
  - Derived colours (`itemColorActive*` = `changeColor(primary, α)`) are
    pinned literals in `NUI.Theme.Menu` (toolchain convention, cf. Tag).

**Not ported:** `MenuInst` imperatives (`showOption` → `expandTo`,
`deriveResponsiveState` → meaningless without `responsive`), the deprecated
aliases (`items`, `title`, `titleExtra`, `expandedNames`,
`onOpenNamesChange`, `onExpandedNamesChange`; the port's `onSelect` IS the
new `on-update:value`), and keyboard navigation (upstream has none — only
`:focus-within` CSS parity, which the extracted rules carry).

(Record updates bind `defaults` to a local first — see `NUI.Button`.)
