name: NUI.Message
comment:
Naive UI's `Message` service (provider + environments), rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Internal as I
    import NUI.Message as Message


    -- in `update` (the caller owns the queue and the hide clock):
    --
    --   ShowMessage  -> ( Message.create "hi" { Message.defaults | content = "Saved" } model.messages
    --                   , ...schedule a `Hide` msg via `Message.effectiveDuration` ...
    --                   )
    --   Hide         -> ( Message.destroy "hi" model.messages, ... )          -- stamp LeaveFrom
    --   AfterLeave   -> ( Message.remove "hi" model.messages, ... )           -- splice when the leave ends
    --
    --   view: Message.view theme model.messages

Upstream is a `MessageProvider` holding a queue of `MessageEnvironment`s. Each
environment renders `<NFadeInExpandTransition appear>` around a `div
.n-message-wrapper` (whose inline `align-items` and `--n-*` vars the message
carries) and owns a `setTimeout(hide, duration)` clock. This library is pure —
no ports, no `update` — so the provider's props and the queue live in one
caller-owned `State`, the transforms here are the provider API, and `view`
renders exactly the DOM the environments would show:

  - `create` — upstream `create()` (MessageProvider.tsx): appends to `items` in
    DOM order. It stamps `phase = Just I.EnterFrom` (upstream mounts with
    `appear`, so the first paint already carries the
    `fade-in-height-expand-transition-enter-from` class). When the provider is
    at `max`, the OLDEST item is dropped from the state instantly — no leave
    phase, none of its callbacks fire (upstream `shift()` unmounts it
    untransitioned). `max` follows JS truthiness: `Just 0` and `Nothing` are
    UNLIMITED (a negative `Just` would be truthy upstream — evicting on every
    create — while the port never evicts for `n <= 0`; the same pathological
    divergence noted on `NUI.Notification`), and
    the count includes items already leaving. Exactly one drop per create.
  - `info` / `success` / `warning` / `error` / `loading` — upstream's typed
    API: `create` with the kind stamped (`{ type: 'info', ...options }`).
  - `destroy` — upstream `destroy()` → the environment's `hide()`:
    `phase := Just I.LeaveFrom`. NO-OP when the item is already in a leave
    phase — upstream's `showRef` is already `false`, and resetting the ladder
    would restart the collapse (a byte-visible divergence); an unknown key is a
    no-op too. Note the ladder resets to `LeaveFrom` even mid-enter (upstream
    starts the leave from whatever state it is in).
  - `destroyAll` — upstream `destroyAll()`: the same rule for every item.
  - `remove` — upstream `onInternalAfterLeave` → `splice`: drops the item once
    its leave has ended (caller-owned clock: fire your after-leave msg one
    leave-duration after `destroy`, then `remove`). This is what empties the
    container — `view` renders `Element.none` while `items` is empty. Removing
    mid-leave makes the container vanish before the animation ends.
  - `effectiveDuration` — the resolved hide timeout: the item's `duration`
    when set, otherwise the provider default (`State.duration`). Upstream's
    `setHideTimeout` guards `if (duration)`, so `Just 0` means NEVER (no
    fallback to the provider default — the falsy check wins).

**Service-template rule.** Config upstream READS while transforming lives in
`State` (`max`, `duration`, `keepAliveOnHover`, `closable`, `rtl` — the
provider props), view-only config lives in `Options`. The three mergeable
props merge per-item-then-provider exactly as the provider's JSX does
(`message.duration === undefined ? this.duration : message.duration`), at
transform/view time.

**Callback matrix** (upstream MessageEnvironment.tsx):

  - close-icon click → `onClose` only — fire-and-forget; a message's close is
    never vetoed (upstream ignores `onClose`'s return and `hide()`s
    unconditionally). The port emits `onClose`; completing the close is the
    caller's `destroy` in the same update.
  - timer expiry / `destroy` / `destroyAll` → hide WITHOUT `onClose`.
  - `onLeave` / `onAfterLeave` fire on every transition leave — timer expiry
    included — but NOT on max-eviction (the evictee is unmounted without a
    transition and fires nothing at all). A pure view cannot fire messages on
    its own; the caller fires them from the clock it owns (onLeave when
    stamping the leave, onAfterLeave when the leave has run its 300ms).

**Icon wrapper.** Upstream renders `div.n-message__icon` iff
`showIcon && (icon /= Nothing || kind /= Default)` — a `Default` message
without a custom icon has NO icon wrapper even at `showIcon = True`, and
`render /= Nothing` replaces the whole body (icon, content and close included)
so it never renders one. The `NIconSwitchTransition` around the icon (an
animation for live TYPE changes) is dropped: items are immutable here — edit
the item's `options` instead.

**Divergences from upstream** (everything else is a faithful port):

  - **Provider / teleport skipped.** No `MessageProvider`, no `to` teleport:
    the caller owns one `State` and mounts the container where it wants it
    (the `NUI.LoadingBar` precedent).
  - **The hide clock is data.** Upstream arms `setTimeout` on mount, clears it
    on hover and re-arms it on leave (`keepAliveOnHover`); the caller owns the
    timer and steps the phases. The wrapper's internal mouseenter/mouseleave
    listeners are still emitted — but only when the MERGED `keepAliveOnHover`
    is on, and attached to a decoder that can never produce a message (the
    options expose no public mouse handlers — upstream's API has none either;
    pausing the clock on hover is the caller's job).
  - **`max-height` pinning of `fade-in-height-expand`** (upstream measures the
    element at runtime) is not reproduced — the phase classes and the caller
    clock drive the CSS transition, the `NUI.Menu` precedent.
  - **`MessageReactive` mutability** — upstream lets `create`'s return value
    mutate `content` / `type` live; here an item's `options` are plain data —
    rebuild the state with the edited options.
  - **`spinProps`** — the loading icon's bytes are fixed (strokeWidth 24,
    scale 0.85, upstream's defaults at the message call site). The deprecated
    `hide` / `deactivate` / `onHide` / `onAfterHide` aliases are not ported.
  - **`onClose` return value** — ignored (upstream ignores it too).
  - **`themeClass` / `inlineThemeDisabled`** — not ported; the inline
    `--n-*` vars are always emitted (upstream's default mode).

name: NUI.Modal
comment:
Naive UI's `Modal` — the mount-body family: unlike `NUI.Popover`/
`NUI.Dropdown` (a follower anchored to a trigger), Modal renders its own fixed
full-viewport tree and centres the content with flex (`align-self: center;
margin: auto` inside the scroll content). Upstream `Modal.tsx` is orchestration
around `BodyWrapper.tsx` (the `ModalBody` component):

    div.n-modal-container (role=none, the 4 css vars [+ z-index])
      div.n-modal-mask (aria-hidden)                       — iff showMask
      div.n-modal-body-wrapper [--mask-hidden] (role=none)
        NUI.Scrollbar (contentClass n-modal-scroll-content)
          the content root, always classed `n-modal`

    import NUI.Modal as Modal
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Modal.view Theme.default
        Modal.defaults
        (Modal.Custom []
            [ Element.text "Content" ])

    -- the card preset: upstream spreads dialog props last, so the card is
    -- UNBORDERED by default — start from Modal.cardDefaults
    Modal.view Theme.default
        { Modal.defaults | show = True }
        (Modal.Card
            { Modal.cardDefaults
                | title = Just (Element.text "Title")
                , closable = True
            }
            [ Element.text "Card content" ])

**Everything runtime is caller-owned** (the popover family precedent, applied
to the inverse architecture — upstream provides
`popoverBodyInjectionKey = null`, it consumes nothing):

  - **Mounting and `show`.** The caller decides where the tree lives (upstream
    teleports to `to`; mount `view` wherever you want it) and owns the show
    state. `show = False` with no leave phase renders a bare container —
    unmount the view when fully closed (`displayDirective: 'if'` semantics;
    the keep-mounted `display: none` variant is not modelled).
  - **Transitions.** Both the mask (`fade-in-transition`) and the content
    (`fade-in-scale-up-transition`, enter scale `.5`) run `.25s` on the same
    clock: pass the phase through `maskTransition`/`bodyTransition` and keep
    the view mounted while either is a leave phase (`I.isLeavePhase`). The
    mask node and the body-wrapper tree are only rendered while
    `show || isLeavePhase …`.
  - **Outside-click closing.** Upstream's mask never receives clicks (the
    fixed body-wrapper overlays it; `maskClosable` closes via the
    `clickoutside` directive on the content node). The port's mask is inert
    and `aria-hidden`; wire your own outside-click handling.
  - **Keyboard.** `closeOnEsc`/`onEsc`, `trapFocus`/`autoFocus` (VFocusTrap
    tab cycling) are caller runtime.
  - **`blockScroll`.** Upstream locks `document.body`; not reachable from a
    pure view.
  - **Drag and mouse `transformOrigin`.** Global mousemove/mousedown runtime
    (upstream `useDragModal` + the modal provider's mouse tracking); the port
    is effectively `transformOrigin: 'center'`. The `.n-modal .n-draggable`
    CSS rule ships unused.
  - **z-index.** No `zindexable` auto-increment: pass `zIndex` and allocate
    stacking yourself (rendered as `z-index` appended after the vars).

**Presets.** `Custom` wraps your content in a port-owned `div.n-modal`
(upstream clones the caller's root vnode and merges the class onto it — Elm
elements cannot be cloned; the extra wrapper is visually identical because the
`.n-modal` rules land on it). The Custom wrapper is TWO nodes: the port-owned
`.n-modal` shell — which also inlines `flex-shrink: 1; min-width: 0`, since
elm-ui nodes carry `flex-shrink: 0` and would hold an auto-width custom body
at its max-content size, spilling past the scroll content's box (upstream's
plain div keeps the flex default) — and an inner carrier column receiving
the caller's `attributes`: a caller `style` attribute on the shell itself
would clobber the port's geometry declarations (duplicate `style`
attributes, last one wins). `Card` composes `NUI.Card.view` with the
`n-modal` class, `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` merged onto the card
root (via Card's `extraClasses`/`attributes` seams) — start from
`cardDefaults`: upstream spreads `{...cardBaseProps, ...dialogProps}` so the
card is unbordered by default inside a modal. **Both presets wrap each child in
`Element.paragraph`** — a bare elm-ui `Element.text` carries `white-space: pre`
and a content-width box, so it never wraps and overflows the card/mask on one
line; upstream's `n-modal` body is normal block flow (the `pre` belongs only to
a `content-in-pre` variant). Either way the body phase class
(`fade-in-scale-up-transition-*`) is forced **last** in the root class list
(the house invariant, cf. `NUI.Dropdown`), after any caller-supplied
`extraClasses`. `dialog`/`confirm` presets compose `NUI.Dialog` (see the
**The dialog presets** paragraph below).

`showMask = False` adds `n-modal-body-wrapper--mask-hidden` (pointer-events
pass-through except the content) exactly as upstream's `maskHidden = !showMask`.

**The dialog presets** compose `NUI.Dialog.view`: the body root keeps its own
`.n-dialog` classes and vars, gains `n-modal` (prepended to the dialog's
`extraClasses`, before the phase classes — phase LAST stays) and
`aria-modal="true"` (upstream `BodyWrapper` adds exactly that; `role=dialog`
is the dialog's own). Upstream's `.n-modal .n-dialog` rule (width `446px`,
`max-width: calc(100vw - 32px)`) ships with dialog's cssr, so the composed
body is sized for free. The env-level runtime (`useDialog` queue, the
return-`false`-blocks-close gate, mask/esc/drag) is caller-owned — see
`NUI.Dialog`'s contract.

(upstream `preset: 'card'`), or the dialog pair `Dialog`/`Confirm` (upstream
`preset: 'dialog' | 'confirm'` — `confirm` is a deprecated alias of `dialog`;
both render the identical `NUI.Dialog` body, only the constructor differs).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The container options. `show` gates the mask and the body-wrapper tree
(each ALSO renders while its own transition phase is a leave phase — see
`maskTransition` / `bodyTransition`; `show = False` with no leave phase
renders a bare container, i.e. unmount the view when fully closed).
`showMask` (`True` upstream) drops the mask node and adds
`n-modal-body-wrapper--mask-hidden` — upstream's mask is inert either way,
so outside-click closing is always caller wiring. `zIndex` (`Just n` →
`z-index: n` appended after the vars; `Nothing` omits it — upstream's
z-index pooling is not modelled). `attributes` land on the container div.

values.comment:
The mount-body modal: the fixed full-viewport container (vars, optional

name: NUI.Notification
comment:
Naive UI's `Notification` service (provider + environments), rebuilt on
elm-ui. The `NUI.Message` twin: same `State` contract, a few byte-visible
deltas called out below.

    import NUI.Internal as I
    import NUI.Notification as Notification


    -- in `update` (the caller owns the queue and the hide clock):
    --
    --   Notify   -> ( Notification.create "n1" { Notification.defaults | title = Just "Hi" } model.notes
    --              , ...schedule a `Hide` msg via `Notification.effectiveDuration`...
    --              )
    --   Hide     -> ( Notification.destroy "n1" model.notes, ... )      -- stamp LeaveFrom
    --   AfterLeave -> ( Notification.remove "n1" model.notes, ... )     -- splice when the leave ends
    --
    --   view: Notification.view theme model.notes

Upstream is a `NotificationProvider` holding a queue of
`NotificationEnvironment`s. Each environment wraps a `div
.n-notification-wrapper` in `<Transition name="notification-transition"
appear>` and owns a `setTimeout(hide, duration)` clock. This library is pure —
no ports, no `update` — so the provider's props and the queue live in one
caller-owned `State`, the transforms here are the provider API, and `view`
renders exactly the DOM the environments would show:

  - `create` — upstream `create()` (NotificationProvider.tsx): appends to
    `items` in DOM order. It stamps `phase = Just I.EnterFrom` (upstream
    mounts with `appear`). When the provider is at `max` — counted as
    `list.length - leavingCount`, i.e. items already in a leave phase do NOT
    count (upstream's `leavingKeySet`) — the OLDEST still-live item is
    destroyed instead of dropped: it enters its leave ladder animated, exactly
    like a `destroy` (upstream's one instant-splice path is a Vue mount race
    for not-yet-mounted refs; the pure port always animates — documented
    divergence). `max` follows JS truthiness: `Just 0` and `Nothing` are
    UNLIMITED (upstream would also treat a negative `Just` as truthy and evict
    on every create — the port never evicts for `n <= 0`, the one documented
    divergence on that pathological input). Exactly
    one eviction per create.
  - `info` / `success` / `warning` / `error` — upstream's typed API: `create`
    with the kind stamped (there is no `loading` kind here, unlike message).
  - `destroy` — upstream `destroy()` → the environment's `hide()`:
    `phase := Just I.LeaveFrom`. NO-OP when the item is already in a leave
    phase (upstream's `showRef` is already `false`; resetting the ladder would
    restart the slide — a byte-visible divergence). Unknown keys are no-ops.
  - `destroyAll` — upstream `destroyAll()`: the same rule for every item.
  - `remove` — upstream `onInternalAfterLeave` → splice: drops the item once
    its leave has ended. This is what empties the container — `view` renders
    `Element.none` while `items` is empty.
  - `effectiveDuration` — the resolved hide timeout: the item's own `duration`
    and NOTHING else. Upstream's notification provider has NO `duration` prop
    (unlike message): `Nothing` means never auto-close, `Just 0` is falsy and
    also means never. The `State` argument exists to keep the service-template
    signature parallel to `NUI.Message` and is deliberately unused.

**Deltas from `NUI.Message`** (each upstream-byte-checked):

  - **Vars on TWO nodes.** Both `n-notification-wrapper` and
    `n-notification` carry the full `--n-*` set (upstream `Notification.tsx`
    puts `cssVars` on both). `--n-icon-color` is emitted only when `kind /=
    Default`: upstream reads `self[createKey('iconColor', type)]` and there is
    no `iconColorDefault` key, so the default type drops the var (Vue skips
    undefined styles).
  - **`transitioning` container class.** Upstream toggles a bare
    `transitioning` class on the container while a transition count is > 0
    (before-enter→after-enter, before-leave→after-leave). The pure derivation:
    any item whose `phase /= Nothing` — VALID ONLY IF the caller holds the
    phase `Just` across the whole window (walk the ladder, then `Nothing` on
    after-enter; `remove` on after-leave). Clearing early diverges silently.
    Mixed enter+leave items still yield the one bare class.
  - **`content` renders in a `<pre>`** (upstream keeps a literal `pre` element
    — whitespace bytes are significant there).
  - **Close can be vetoed.** Upstream's env `handleClose` resolves the user
    `onClose` and hides only when the feedback is not `false` (a rejected
    promise also prevents the hide). In Elm the veto is data, not a return
    value: the port emits `onClose` on close-icon click and the CALLER decides
    whether to `destroy`. Timer expiry / `destroy` / `destroyAll` still hide
    WITHOUT firing `onClose`.
  - **Hover-pause gate is `duration && keepAliveOnHover`** (env bytes): the
    internal mouseenter/mouseleave listeners exist only for a notification
    that has BOTH a duration and the merged keep-alive flag. The public
    `onMouseenter` / `onMouseleave` options are always attached (upstream
    merges them via `mergeEventHandlers`).
  - **Scrollable.** Upstream defaults `scrollable: true` and renders an
    `NScrollbar` (contentStyle `overflow: hidden`) around the wrappers —
    unless the placement is `top` / `bottom`, where scrollable is forced off
    (byte-visible: no scrollbar tree). The scrollbar bars themselves are
    hidden at rest (runtime-measured, `NUI.Scrollbar`'s documented contract).
  - **Falsy text fields.** `title` / `description` / `content` / `meta` skip
    their element when `Nothing` OR an empty string (upstream `this.title ?`
    — `''` is falsy there too).

**Divergences from upstream** (everything else is a faithful port):

  - **Provider / teleport skipped.** No `NotificationProvider`, no `to`
    teleport: the caller owns one `State` and mounts the container where it
    wants it (the `NUI.LoadingBar` precedent).
  - **The hide clock is data.** The caller arms the timer from
    `effectiveDuration`, clears/re-arms on hover (a FULL restart on
    mouseleave — upstream `setHideTimeout`, not a remaining-time resume), and
    steps the phase ladder.
  - **`max-height` pinning of the enter/leave windows** (upstream's manual
    `handleBefore*` height juggling) is not reproduced — the phase classes and
    the caller clock drive the CSS transition (the `NUI.Menu` precedent).
  - **`NotificationReactive` mutability** — edit the item's `options` and
    rebuild the state instead. The deprecated `hide` / `deactivate` /
    `onHide` / `onAfterShow` / `onAfterHide` aliases are not ported.
  - **`themeClass` / `inlineThemeDisabled`** — not ported; the inline
    `--n-*` vars are always emitted (upstream's default mode).
  - **`onAfterEnter`** — notification-only (message has none); fires from the
    caller's clock when the enter ladder settles.

name: NUI.NumberAnimation
comment:
Naive UI's `NumberAnimation`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.NumberAnimation exposing (defaults)

    NUI.NumberAnimation.view theme
        { defaults | to = 110, from = 10, duration = 3000, elapsed = 1500 }
        []

Upstream's `formattedValueRef`, directly assertable:

    import NUI.NumberAnimation exposing (defaults)

    NUI.NumberAnimation.format
        { defaults
            | to = 1234567.5
            , precision = 1
            , showSeparator = True
            , elapsed = 2000
        }
    -- { integer = "1,234,567", decimal = Just "5", decimalSeparator = "." }

**Runtime.** Upstream owns a `requestAnimationFrame` tween (`utils.ts`'s
`tween`, plus the `play` / `active` / `onFinish` props) and derives the
displayed value from `performance.now()`. This library is pure, so the caller
owns the clock — the same contract as `NUI.Countdown` — and passes `elapsed`,
the milliseconds since the animation started. `tweenValue` maps that onto
upstream's exact expression, including the
`elapsedTime = Math.min(current - startTime, duration)` clamp and the exact
`to` that upstream's `onFinish` assigns once that clamp bites: `elapsed = 0`
displays `from`, any `elapsed >= duration` displays `to` (and a `duration`
of `0` finishes immediately, as upstream's `elapsedTime === duration` does).

`elapsed` was chosen over an already-resolved `value` so that `from` / `to` /
`duration` stay live inside the options — the record remains the single
source of truth and the caller supplies only what a clock actually knows.
Upstream's `active` and `play()` collapse into when the caller starts
advancing `elapsed`, and `onFinish` into noticing `elapsed >= duration`.

Elm has no `Intl`, so the locale-derived strings are inputs too:
`decimalSeparator` and `groupSeparator` default to `"."` / `","` — en-US,
Naive UI's fallback locale, and zh-CN agree on both. Grouping is fixed
3-digit thousands; locales that group differently (hi-IN's `12,34,567`) have
no equivalent.

NumberAnimation carries no classes and no `--n-*` variables of its own
(like `NUI.Countdown`).

values.comment:
Upstream's prop defaults (`duration: 2000`, `precision: 0`, no
separator, `%`-style unit semantics — `to` / `from` both `0`), plus the
port's runtime inputs at rest: `elapsed = 0` (nothing has ticked) and the
en-US separators `"."` / `","`.

values.name: easeOut
values.comment:
Upstream's easing, `1 - (1 - t) ** 5` (easeOutQuint). `easeOut 0 == 0`,
`easeOut 1 == 1`.

values.name: format
values.comment:
The displayed value as upstream's `formattedValueRef` computes it:
`round(displayedValue, precision).toFixed(precision)`, split at the decimal
point, with the integer part optionally grouped. Exposed so the formatter is
directly assertable without rendering:

    NUI.NumberAnimation.format
        { defaults | to = 16.5, precision = 2, elapsed = 2000 }
    -- { integer = "16", decimal = Just "50", decimalSeparator = "." }

values.name: formatToFixed
values.comment:
Upstream's `round(displayedValue, precision).toFixed(precision)`:

    formatToFixed 0 1234.5678 == "1235"

    formatToFixed 2 1234.5678 == "1234.57"

    formatToFixed 2 0 == "0.00"

    formatToFixed 3 0.0005 == "0.001"

JS `toFixed` never uses exponent notation and always emits exactly
`precision` fractional digits — unlike `String.fromFloat`, which produces
`"1e-7"` below `1e-7`. (The one divergence kept: JS `toFixed` switches to
`"1e+21"` at `1e21` and beyond, where this still writes the digits out —
upstream never animates that high.) The sign is that of the _rounded_ value,
so `-0.0004` at precision 2 is `"0.00"`, not `"-0.00"` — upstream's round
trip already loses the negative zero there.

values.name: groupDigits
values.comment:
Upstream's `showSeparator` branch:
`new Intl.NumberFormat(locale).format(Number(integer))` — default-options
`Intl` grouping, which for the locales at hand is plain thousands. The
separator is caller-owned here; the digits are grouped in threes from the
right and a leading `-` stays put:

    groupDigits "," "1234567" == "1,234,567"

    groupDigits "," "-1234567" == "-1,234,567"

Locales with other group sizes (hi-IN's `12,34,567`) are out of scope — see
the module docs.

values.name: roundTo
values.comment:
lodash's `round(value, precision)` — what upstream formats the displayed
value with. The decimal point is shifted through the number's _string_ form
(`"1.005e2"`, round, `"101e-2"` back), lodash's exponent trick, so binary
representation error never enters:

    roundTo 2 1.005 == 1.01

where the naive `roundTo p v = toFloat (round (v * 10 ^ p)) / 10 ^ p` yields
`1` (`1.005 * 100 == 100.49999…` as a Float).

Ties go up, JS `Math.round`-style — half towards `+Infinity`, not away from
zero. That is exactly what elm/core's `round` _implements_ (its kernel is
`Math.round`, so `round -1.5 == -1` — run it), even though the elm/core
_docs_ claim ".5 away from zero", which would give `-2`; `roundTo` follows
the implementation, matching lodash (`roundTo 0 -1.5 == -1`,
`roundTo 2 -1.005 == -1`). Negative precision works as in lodash
(`roundTo -2 1234 == 1200`), and as in lodash the precision is capped at
`292`. Precision `0` skips the shift and rounds directly, mirroring
lodash's `if (precision && …)` guard.

values.name: tweenValue
values.comment:
Upstream's `tween` value: the tweened number `elapsed` milliseconds in,
where upstream's loop computes
`from + (to - from) * easeOut(Math.min(current - startTime, duration) / duration)`
and its `onFinish` then assigns `to` exactly. So `elapsed >= duration`
returns `to` outright (no `from + (to - from) * easeOut 1`, which can sit one
ulp off `to` in Float), and `duration = 0` finishes immediately. Negative
`elapsed` flows through the formula unclamped — upstream's monotonic clock
can never produce it, and this port changes no upstream expression.
values.type: { from : Basics.Float, to : Basics.Float, duration : Basics.Float, elapsed : Basics.Float } -> Basics.Float

name: NUI.Pagination
comment:
Naive UI's `Pagination`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Pagination exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Pagination.view theme
        { defaults
            | itemCount = Just 153
            , currentPage = model.page
            , onUpdatePage = Just GotPage
        }
        []

The element carries the `.n-pagination` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*`
custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. The page-window
algorithm is pure and exposed: `pageItems` (upstream `createPageItemsInfo`),
`pageCount` and `getDefaultPageSize` are behaviour-for-behaviour ports of
`src/pagination/src/utils.ts` and `mergedPageCountRef`.

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream keeps the page, the page size and the quick
jumper's text in refs; here all of them are options and every state change is
a message you wire yourself:

  - `currentPage` / `onUpdatePage` — page clicks, the prev / next buttons and
    the fast-backward / fast-forward ellipses all emit the **target** page
    (upstream's `doUpdatePage` fires only when the component is not disabled
    and the target differs from the current page, so a click that would
    change nothing gets no handler here either).
  - `jumperValue` / `onJumperInput` — the quick jumper input's text. Upstream
    syncs it to `String(page)` on every page change (and clears it after a
    non-simple jump); reproduce that in your update.
  - `pageSize` — `Nothing` falls back to `getDefaultPageSize` (the first
    `pageSizes` entry, 10 by default), exactly like upstream's uncontrolled
    state.
  - `itemCount` has priority over `pageCount`, like upstream (which warns
    when both are set).

The children argument is upstream's `prefix` slot (rendered in
`.n-pagination-prefix` only when non-empty); the `suffix` option covers the
`suffix` slot.

**Documented gaps** (runtime or unported dependencies — do not try to close
them here):

  - **Size picker.** Upstream's `pageSizes` selector is an `NSelect`, which
    this library has not ported — the element is omitted entirely (upstream's
    `displayOrder` slot `size-picker`). `onUpdatePageSize` exists for the day
    it is.
  - **Quick-jump dropdown.** The ellipsis items' `NPopselect` hover menu is
    not ported. Hover state is caller-side runtime, so
    `n-pagination-item--hover` is never emitted and the fast items always
    show the `More` ellipsis icon (upstream swaps in the fast-backward /
    fast-forward icon while hovered); `showQuickJumpDropdown` only controls
    whether `pageItems` attaches the jump option lists.
  - **Quick-jump commit.** Upstream jumps on the jumper input's `change`
    (Enter / blur); `NUI.Input` has no change event, so typing is wired
    (`onJumperInput` filters non-digits, like upstream's `handleJumperInput`)
    but committing the jump is the caller's concern.
  - **Focus, transitions, hover.** Upstream's focus management, the
    `transition-disabled` reflow trick and all hover-state tracking are
    runtime concerns of the original and intentionally absent.
  - **Locale / render slots.** "Goto" is upstream's `enUS` `goto` label; the
    `prev` / `next` / `label` / `goto` render props are not ported (the arrow
    buttons always render `NBaseIcon` chevrons, page items their number).
  - **Sizes.** Naive UI's pagination has no `tiny` size; `Tiny` clamps to
    `Small` for the item metrics (the jumper input still gets upstream's
    `smallerSize` of the clamped size).

name: NUI.Popconfirm
comment:
Naive UI's `Popconfirm` — the popover body plus the confirm panel
(upstream renders `NPopover` on its default body path with
`internalExtraClass={['popconfirm']}` and the panel in the default slot; the
`NUI.Tooltip` lane):

    import NUI.Popconfirm as Popconfirm

    Popconfirm.view theme
        { Popconfirm.defaults
            | popover = { NUI.Popover.defaults | width = Just "220px" }
            , onPositiveClick = Just Confirmed
        }
        [ Element.text "Delete it?" ]

DOM (everything in `NUI.Popover`'s docstring applies — the caller-owned show
state / trigger / `v-placement` wrapper, the header/footer/scrollable
structure, `overlap` suppressing the arrow, the transition phases):

    div.n-popover.n-popover-shared [.rtl] .n-popconfirm [+popover modifiers]
      style = [width?] + 15 popover vars
      ├─ div.n-popover__content
      │    └─ div.n-popconfirm__panel  style = 4 panel vars
      │        ├─ div.n-popconfirm__body                 — iff showIcon || content
      │        │    ├─ div.n-popconfirm__icon > i.n-base-icon > svg(warning)
      │        │    └─ content…
      │        └─ div.n-popconfirm__action               — ALWAYS (upstream quirk)
      │             action slot | negative? positive? (NUI.Buttons, small)
      └─ arrow pair (mergedShowArrow; default True)

**Actions are composed `NUI.Button`s** — negative first (plain `small`,
Default kind — NOT ghost, unlike Dialog's), then positive (`small`,
Primary). `positiveProps`/`negativeProps` model upstream's `{...buttonProps}`
spread as update functions on the derived base (caller wins, exactly the
spread). Each button renders iff its text is not `Hidden`; `DefaultText`
labels are upstream's baked `enUS` locale (`Confirm`/`Cancel` — the
`NUI.Pagination` "Goto" convention). The `__action` div ALWAYS renders —
upstream's fallback returns `[]` (truthy) when both texts are null, so even
`Hidden` texts leave an empty action row (the Dialog `action = Just []` hole
shape; pinned).

**Runtime is caller-owned**: upstream's default `trigger` is `'click'`; the
return-`false`-blocks-close gate (`onPositiveClick` resolving false keeps the
popover open) is the caller's update deciding whether to unmount; the arrow /
placement / width ride the `popover` options untouched.

name: NUI.Popover
comment:
Naive UI's `Popover` body (`n-popover`), rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Popover exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Popover.view theme
        { defaults | header = Just (Element.text "Title") }
        [ Element.text "Content" ]

The element carries the `.n-popover` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**What this module is.** Upstream `n-popover` is two things: a trigger runtime
(hover/click/focus state machine with `delay`/`duration` timers, clickoutside,
z-index pooling, `VBinder`/`VTarget` measurement of the trigger, `VFollower`
positioning and flip) and the body it shows. This library is pure, so only the
**body** is ported (the `NUI.BackTop` / `NUI.Affix` / `NUI.Scrollbar`
caller-owned-runtime precedent): the caller owns the show state (mount/unmount
this element), the trigger (their element, their handlers), and the positioned
wrapper the body must sit in (below).

**The wrapper contract.** Every placement rule in Naive UI's CSS is
`[v-placement="…"] > .n-popover-shared` (margin, arrow position) reading
`--v-offset-left/top` and `--v-target-width/height` runtime variables. Put the
body inside a wrapper that carries the `v-placement` attribute —
`placementAttribute` emits it — and position it yourself (upstream's follower
applies `transform: translateX(…) translateY(…)`, z-index, and the `--v-*`
variables; see vueuc's `v-binder-follower-content`). The wrapper must live
inside `nui-root` (this port's CSS is doubly scoped; upstream teleports to
`body` instead). Set `--v-offset-left: 0` and `--v-offset-top: 0` on the
wrapper as vueuc does — the arrow `-start`/`-end` rules read them **without**
fallbacks, so an unset var degrades the arrow position to `auto` (the
`--v-target-*` vars carry their own `, 0px` fallbacks and matter only for
`arrowPointToCenter`).

**Documented gaps:**

  - `trigger` (`'hover' | 'click' | 'focus' | 'manual'`), `delay`, `duration`,
    `keepAliveOnHover`, `disabled`, `flip`, `zIndex`, `to`, `x`/`y` and the
    events (`on-update:show`, `on-clickoutside`) are runtime — not modelled.
    Bind the trigger's DOM events with your own handlers.
  - `show` is modelled by mounting / unmounting this element (upstream's
    `displayDirective: 'if'`, the default). `'show'`-style keep-mounted hiding
    is the caller's (`attributes` can carry `display: none`), and the
    enter/leave animation is driven through `transition` phases below.
  - `placement` has no `Options` field: it affects only the wrapper attribute
    (`placementAttribute`), never the body node.
  - `width: 'trigger'` (match-trigger-width) is runtime measurement — set the
    px yourself. A numeric `width` upstream becomes `"<n>px"`; the port takes
    raw CSS.
  - `minWidth` / `maxWidth` are deprecated upstream (and upstream pushes
    `minWidth` as `maxWidth` — an upstream bug) — not modelled.
  - `internalRenderBody` and the other `internal*` props (the dropdown /
    tooltip reuse lane) are not modelled; those components will compose this
    module directly.
  - `n-popover--show-header-or-footer` and the header / footer nodes exist only
    while `header` / `footer` are `Just` (upstream renders each wrapper only
    when its slot is non-empty).
  - `extraClasses` is upstream's `internalExtraClass` slot — extra classes
    after `n-popover-shared` (and `--rtl`), before the conditional modifiers.
    `NUI.Tooltip` uses it to add its `n-tooltip` marker.

name: NUI.Popselect
comment:
Naive UI's `Popselect` — the popover-family body whose **select-menu root
is the popover-shared body** (upstream swaps the body via
`internalRenderBody`; the `NUI.Dropdown` lane — this is NOT a
`NUI.Popover.view` wrapper):

    import NUI.Popselect as Popselect
    import NUI.SelectMenu

    Popselect.view theme
        { Popselect.defaults | onUpdateValue = Just Selected }
        [ NUI.SelectMenu.Option
            { value = "drive", label = "Drive My Car", disabled = False, attributes = [] }
        ]

DOM (everything in `NUI.Popover`'s docstring about the runtime applies — the
caller owns show/trigger (`'hover'` default)/positioning and mounts the body
in a `placementAttribute` wrapper, default placement **bottom**):

    div.n-base-select-menu .n-base-select-menu--{size}-size
        [--rtl] [--multiple] .n-popselect-menu .n-popover-shared
        [rtl] [overlap] .n-popover-shared--show-arrow [center-arrow]
        [popover-transition-*]
      tabindex = 0 (focusable)
      style = 23 menu vars → --n-menu-box-shadow → [width?] → 15 popover vars
              (--n-padding = 0, upstream builtinThemeOverrides)
      └─ NUI.SelectMenu rows (header / options-or-empty / action) — see there

There is **no `n-popover` class, no `n-popover__content` wrapper, no arrow
node** — the internalRenderBody path (identical to Dropdown). The
`--show-arrow` modifier follows the popover's `mergedShowArrow =
!overlap && showArrow` (popselect omits the prop, so the default `true`
survives — present unless `overlap`, even though no arrow node renders on
this path; a margin-only cosmetic quirk; pinned).

**Selection** is pure: `value` (`SelectMenu.Value`) drives `--selected` +
the checkmark per option; clicking a non-disabled leaf fires
`onUpdateValue` with the NEXT value computed by `toggleValue` (upstream's
panel `toggle`: multiple toggles list membership preserving order; single
selects — or deselects to `Single Nothing` when `cancelable` and the value
was current). Upstream then auto-closes on single select — the caller's
update does that here. Sizes: upstream `PopselectSize` has no `tiny` — the
four constructors map onto `NUI.SelectMenu.Size` internally.

caller-owned.

The merged 39 `--n-*` custom properties on the root, in order: the 23

single mode selects the key — or deselects to `Single Nothing` when
`cancelable` and the key was already current.

The `n-popselect-menu` body — the select-menu root carrying the
popover-shared classes and the 39 merged vars. Mount it inside a wrapper
that carries `placementAttribute`.

name: NUI.Progress
comment:
Naive UI's `Progress`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Progress exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Progress.view theme NUI.Progress.defaults []

    NUI.Progress.view theme
        { defaults
            | type_ = NUI.Progress.Circle
            , percentage = 80
            , status = NUI.Progress.Success
        }
        []

    NUI.Progress.view theme
        { defaults
            | percentage = 66
            , processing = True
            , height = Just 12
        }
        []

    NUI.Progress.view theme
        { defaults
            | type_ = NUI.Progress.MultipleCircle
            , percentages = [ 80, 60 ]
            , colors = [ NUI.Progress.Solid "#2080f0", NUI.Progress.Solid "#18a058" ]
            , railColors = [ "#2080f0", "#18a058" ]
            , strokeWidth = 6
            , circleGap = 0.5
        }
        [ Element.text "Circle racing!" ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-progress`
BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships
Naive UI's exact CSS. The children are the default slot: custom indicator
content, replacing the percentage text / status icon.

`Dashboard` is the circle graph with `gapDegree` defaulting to 75.
`MultipleCircle` draws concentric rings — one per entry in `percentages`, each
with its own fill colour (`colors`) and rail colour (`railColors`) — and turns
the default slot into the centre indicator when a child is given.

A fill colour may be a solid colour (`Solid "#2080f0"`) or a linear gradient
(`Gradient [ "white", "#18a058" ]`), Naive UI's `string | { stops }`. Rails are
solid colours only, as upstream. The gradient's `id` is byte-identical to
Naive UI's (`gradient-` + css-render's murmur2 hash for circles, the ring index
for multiple-circle).

`railStyle` (`Line`) and `railStyles` (`MultipleCircle`) are Naive UI's
`rail-style` prop: inline style overriding the built-in rail style, merged in
Vue's array order (a colliding key wins in place, new keys append). Only the
`CSSProperties` form is modelled as a `( "prop", "value" )` list; upstream's
raw-string alternative is not. `Circle` / `Dashboard` accept `railStyle` but
ignore it, exactly as upstream (`Circle.tsx` declares the prop and never
applies it). `railStyles` is indexed per ring, paired with `railColors`.

**Why the inline `width: 100%` on the graph wrappers.** Upstream's graph
divs are plain blocks — the rail fills its parent and the circle svg fills
the 120px `--circle` root by the svg default `width: 100%` + viewBox aspect
ratio. Here every wrapper is an elm-ui element: `flex-basis: auto` items in a
`display: flex` parent size to their content (0 for the empty rail / a
viewBox-only svg), and `.s > .wc { align-self: flex-start }` stops the
cross-axis stretch. The inline widths restore the upstream block chain
(graph → graph-line → rail, graph → graph-circle → svg) so the rail spans
full width and the ring renders at the root's size.

@docs ProgressType, Status, FillColor, IndicatorPlacement, Options, defaults, view, cssVarsFor

unions.name: FillColor
unions.comment:
A fill colour: a solid CSS colour, or Naive UI's `{ stops }` gradient — a
list of colour stops whose first two are the gradient's ends (`stops[0]` /
`stops[1]`). Rails are always `Solid`; only fills may be `Gradient`.

unions.name: IndicatorPlacement
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `indicator-placement` (line only): the indicator sits inside
the fill or after the graph.

unions.name: ProgressType
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `type` prop: `line`, `circle`, `dashboard` (a circle whose gap
defaults to 75°) or `multiple-circle`.

unions.name: Status
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `status` prop. `Default` shows the percentage text; the other
statuses swap it for the status icon and pick the themed fill / icon colours.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The progress options. Graph kind: `type_` picks line / circle /
dashboard / multiple-circle. Values: `percentage` is the single graph's
value (line / circle / dashboard), `percentages` the per-ring values
(`multipleCircle` — one ring per entry, paired by index with `colors` /
`railColors` / `railStyles`). Look: `status` drives the themed fill / icon
colours and swaps the indicator for the status icon; `showIndicator` hides
the whole indicator (`indicatorPlacement` = inside / outside, line only);
`processing` adds the line fill's animated processing state; `unit` is the
indicator's suffix (`%`). Colours: `color` (a `FillColor` — solid or
gradient) overrides the theme fill for the single graph, `colors` the
per-ring fills, `railColor` / `railColors` the rails (solid CSS strings),
and `railStyle` / `railStyles` inline style overrides merged after the
built-ins (Vue array-order; circle / dashboard declare but ignore
`railStyle`, upstream's own dead prop). Line geometry: `height` (px) fixes
the rail height, `borderRadius` / `fillBorderRadius` the corner radii
(defaulting to half the height). Circle geometry: `strokeWidth`,
`viewBoxWidth` (both defaults from upstream), `gapDegree` (defaults to 75
for dashboard, else 0), `gapOffsetDegree`, `offsetDegree` (rotate the arc),
and `circleGap` (the multiple-circle ring spacing, default 1).
`attributes` land on the root.

Upstream's prop defaults: a `0%` default-status line with its indicator

name: NUI.QrCode
comment:
Naive UI's `QrCode`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.QrCode exposing (defaults)

    NUI.QrCode.view theme
        { defaults | value = "https://www.naiveui.com/" }

    NUI.QrCode.view theme
        { defaults
            | value = "https://www.naiveui.com/"
            , color = "#18a058"
            , backgroundColor = "#F5F5F5"
            , errorCorrectionLevel = NUI.QrCode.H
        }

The symbol is encoded by the ported Nayuki library (`NUI.Qrcodegen`) and drawn
as an inline `<svg>`; `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS (`.n-qr-code` plus
the `--n-border-radius` variable).

**Rendering backend.** Upstream defaults to a `<canvas>` and can also emit an
inline `<svg>` (`type="svg"`). This library is pure, so it always renders the
`<svg>` form — the same modules, the same pixels, without imperative canvas
drawing or image preloading. Because of that, upstream's canvas-only
`icon-background-color` / `icon-border-radius` props are not modelled.

**Runtime.** The `iconSrc` image is referenced directly (`<image href=…>`), so
the caller owns loading it. A `value` that does not fit yields an empty
container (upstream throws); the default `value` is `"-"`, mirroring upstream's
`value ?? '-'` fallback.

@docs ErrorCorrectionLevel, Options, Padding, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

unions.name: ErrorCorrectionLevel
unions.comment:
The QR error correction level, mirroring upstream's
`error-correction-level` prop (`'L' | 'M' | 'Q' | 'H'`).

unions.name: Padding
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `string | number` `padding` prop. `Px 12` renders `12px`;
`Custom "5%"` passes an arbitrary CSS length through unchanged.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The `qr-code` options — Naive UI's props one-to-one: `value` (text),
`color` / `backgroundColor` (the dark modules / the quiet-zone ground),
`iconSrc` + `iconSize` (the centered logo `<image>`; `0` means 10% of
`size`, upstream's `0.1 * size` fallback), `size` (the square's pixel
edge), `padding` (the quiet zone), `errorCorrectionLevel`, and the
caller's `attributes` (upstream's fallthrough attrs).
aliases.type: { value : String.String, color : String.String, backgroundColor : String.String, iconSrc : Maybe.Maybe String.String, iconSize : Basics.Int, size : Basics.Int, padding : NUI.QrCode.Padding, errorCorrectionLevel : NUI.QrCode.ErrorCorrectionLevel, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: cssVarsFor
values.comment:
The entries of the container's inline `style` attribute, in upstream order:
the plain properties from `QrCode.tsx` (`padding`, `background-color`, `width`,
`height`) followed by the `--n-*` custom properties.

`box-sizing: content-box` pins the box model upstream relies on: `QrCode.tsx`
sets `padding` + `width`/`height` on a plain `div`, where the `content-box`
default makes the symbol (`size × size`) fit inside the padding. Elm-ui
wrappers force `border-box`, which would shrink the content area to
`size - 2 * padding` and squeeze/clip the svg — pinning `content-box` keeps
the box at `size + 2 * padding` with the svg centered, exactly upstream.
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.QrCode.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults, value-for-value: a `"-"` value (upstream's
`value ?? '-'` fallback), black on white, a 100px symbol, a 12px quiet
zone, no icon (and a 40px icon size when one is set), `M`edium error
correction, no attributes.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The QR container: `div.n-qr-code` sized by `size` and padded by `padding`,
holding Naive UI's inline `<svg>` symbol.

name: NUI.Radio
comment:
Naive UI's `Radio` and `RadioGroup`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Radio exposing (defaults, groupDefaults)

    NUI.Radio.view theme
        { defaults | checked = True }
        [ Element.text "歌单" ]

    NUI.Radio.group theme
        { groupDefaults
            | value = Just model.city
            , onChange = Just SetCity
        }
        [ NUI.Radio.choice "Beijing" "北京"
        , NUI.Radio.choice "Shanghai" "上海"
        , NUI.Radio.choice "Guangzhou" "广州"
        ]

    -- button group (Naive UI's `n-radio-button` children)
    NUI.Radio.group theme
        { groupDefaults | value = Just model.size, onChange = Just SetSize }
        [ NUI.Radio.button "small" "小"
        , NUI.Radio.button "medium" "中"
        , NUI.Radio.button "large" "大"
        ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: elements carry the `.n-radio` /
`.n-radio-group` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and
`NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

Notes on the port:

  - Radio is check-only, like the original: activating an already-checked
    radio fires nothing, and a radio cannot be unchecked by clicking it.
  - A group disables a choice when either the group or the choice is disabled.
  - `Tiny` clamps to `Small` — Naive UI's radio scale has no tiny step.
  - String labels render pixel-identical to Naive UI. Custom `Element` label
    content is aligned but renders at elm-ui's `line-height: 1` (elm-ui forces
    it on text wrappers; see `NUI.Internal` and `tools/bridge.css`).
  - Naive UI's `--focus` ring is driven by native input focus events and is
    not reproduced (stateless view).

`choice` renders Naive UI's `n-radio`, `button` its `n-radio-button`.

`attributes` (the fallthrough seam).

aliases.comment:
The standalone-radio options — Naive UI's radio props: `size`,
`checked`, `disabled`, the `label` string (the slot children `view`
takes win, like upstream), `onChange` (fires only when an unchecked
radio is activated — check-only), and `rtl`. A group's `value` +
`onChange` derive all of these per choice.

A `n-radio-button` choice — enabled, button markup (the group then also
renders its `__splitor` separators and the `--button-group` class).

Naive UI's defaults (`medium`, unchecked, enabled, no label, no
handler, LTR).

The `n-radio-group` element: each choice rendered per `child` (plain

Naive UI's defaults (everything empty / medium / off). `attributes`

the parent's fallthrough `class` onto the group root after its own; the

values.comment:
The standalone `n-radio` element: the ` `-sized dot wrapper and the
label (slot children, else the `label` string), with the state classes,
vars, and ARIA/click wiring of `interactive`. Usually reached through
`group`.

name: NUI.Rate
comment:
Naive UI's `Rate`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Rate exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Rate.view theme { defaults | value = Just 4 }

    NUI.Rate.view theme
        { defaults | allowHalf = True, value = Just 3.5 }

The element carries the `.n-rate` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Runtime.** Upstream tracks the hovered value internally (and derives a half
value from the pointer's `offsetX`); this library is pure, so the caller owns
the hovered value (`hoverValue`) and the selected value. Upstream's default slot
(one custom icon per index, receiving `{ index }`) is not modelled — the default
star icon is always rendered. `readonly` drops the item click handler, and
`onSelect` receives the derived value Naive UI reports (`index + 1`; the `+ 0.5`
half step depends on pointer geometry the caller owns). Naive UI's `clearable`
click-to-clear is the caller's decision inside `onSelect`.

@docs Options, Size, cssVarsFor, defaults, view

unions.comment:
The item size — Naive UI's `size` prop (`small | medium | large`, or a number
of pixels).

aliases.comment:
The rate options — Naive UI's props plus the caller-owned hover state:
`count` stars, the selected `value`, the `hoverValue` (upstream's internal
`hoverIndex`; drives `--active` while hovering), `allowHalf`, `readonly`
(no click handlers), `size`, the `color` override for the active star,
`onSelect` (receiving `index + 1`), and `attributes`.

The rate's `--n-*` custom properties (`--n-item-color-active` is the `color`
option when given).

values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults: 5 stars, nothing selected or hovered, whole-star
steps, interactive `medium` stars, the theme's active color, no handler.

values.comment:
The `n-rate` element — `count` star items (`.n-rate__item`, with an
overlaid `__half` star per item under `allowHalf`), each `--active` per

`onSelect (index + 1)`.

name: NUI.Result
comment:
Naive UI's `Result`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Result exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Result.view theme NUI.Result.defaults []

    NUI.Result.view theme
        { defaults
            | status = NUI.Result.Code404
            , size = NUI.Result.Huge
            , title = Just "404"
            , description = Just "Page not found"
        }
        [ Element.text "You can put some content here." ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-result` BEM classes
and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.
The children of `view` are the default slot (`.n-result-content`); `footer` renders
the footer slot.

unions.comment:
Naive UI's result sizes (`ResultSize` — unlike most components it has no
`tiny`, but adds `huge`).

unions.name: Status
unions.comment:
Naive UI's `status` prop. `Info`/`Success`/`Warning`/`Error` render the
monochrome status icons (they inherit `--n-icon-color`); the HTTP codes render
Naive UI's colorful preset illustrations.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The result options — Naive UI's props: `status`, `size`, the `title` /
`description` strings, `icon` (the icon slot; `Nothing` renders the status
preset), and `footer` (the footer slot). No `attributes` — upstream takes
no fallthrough attrs here.

The raw `--n-*` custom properties a result with these options attaches (before

name: NUI.Scrollbar
comment:
Naive UI's `Scrollbar` (`n-scrollbar`), rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Scrollbar exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Scrollbar.view theme
        { defaults | showYBar = True, yBarStyle = Just "height:40px;top:0" }
        [ Element.el [ Element.height (Element.px 400) ] (Element.text "Long content") ]

The element carries the `.n-scrollbar` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Runtime.** Upstream measures the container/content, decides whether a rail
overflows (`needXBar` / `needYBar`), reads the bar geometry, and shows the bar on
hover (`trigger`) or always (`trigger === 'none'`). This library is pure, so the
caller owns that state: `showYBar` / `showXBar` decide whether a bar element is
rendered (upstream's `needBar && isShowBar && !isIos`) and `yBarStyle` / `xBarStyle`
carry the measured geometry as raw CSS (the `NUI.BackTop` / `NUI.Affix`
caller-owned-runtime precedent). The rails themselves always render.

Upstream also drives the scroll from a bar drag (`handleYScrollMouseDown` /
`handleXScrollMouseDown`: mousedown on the bar memoizes the scroll offset +
pointer, the window mousemove scales the pointer delta by
`(content - container) / (container - bar)` into `container.scrollTop/Left`,
window mouseup releases). The seams are the same story: `containerAttributes`
addresses the scrolling div (`Browser.Dom.setViewportOf`) and
`yBarAttributes` / `xBarAttributes` put the press decoder on the bar div
itself (upstream binds `onMousedown` exactly there).

**Composition seams.** `extraClasses` (appended after `n-scrollbar`, like a Vue
fallthrough class) and `attributes` let wrapper components merge themselves onto
the scrollbar root — `NUI.DrawerContent`'s non-native body uses it for the
`n-drawer-body` class (the `NUI.Card` seam precedent).

**Documented gaps:**

  - The root is an elm-ui element (the `NUI.Progress` / `NUI.Badge` precedent, so the
    caller's `attributes` land on it), which means elm-ui's own structure classes also
    sit alongside `n-scrollbar`, and the root is a flex column where upstream is a
    block. Both are harmless here: Naive UI's doubly-scoped rules declare every
    load-bearing property of `.n-scrollbar` (`overflow`, `position`, `height`,
    `width`), the bridge restores `flex-basis`, and every child is `height`/`width:
    100%` or absolutely positioned, so it does not depend on the root's display mode.
    The container and rails remain the root's direct children (`>` selectors hold).
  - `vueuc`'s `VResizeObserver` (content/container resize tracking) is omitted.
  - `trigger` (public `'none' | 'hover'`) is not modelled: it only selects between a
    no-op `Wrapper` and a `Transition`, so it has no static DOM effect. Hover-driven
    show/hide is the caller's (`attributes` can bind `mouseenter` / `mouseleave`).
  - `onScroll` is not modelled; attach it with `attributes` (the `NUI.Layout`
    precedent for a native scroll container).
  - `n-scrollbar-rail--disabled` (added by a `watchEffect` when a rail does not
    overflow) is not modelled — runtime.
  - The `fade-in-transition` on the bar is not driven (caller-owned; cf. LoadingBar).
  - The horizontal bar's RTL offset (`right` vs `left`) is caller-owned via `xBarStyle`.
  - Upstream's own root merge puts the fallthrough attrs FIRST: `NScrollbar`
    declares `inheritAttrs: false` and renders its root as
    `mergeProps(this.$attrs, { class: 'n-scrollbar…', style: cssVars })`
    (Scrollbar.tsx:868), so a consumer's fallthrough `class` lands BEFORE
    `n-scrollbar` and its fallthrough style before the `--n-*` vars — the
    reverse of Vue's template fallthrough. The port keeps the library-wide
    own-first convention (`extraClasses` / `rootStyle` appended after, the
    drawer seam's pinned `n-scrollbar n-drawer-body`); the order difference
    is inert (class order never affects the cascade, and the two style
    declaration sets are disjoint).
  - The `scrollable` / `duration` / `container*` / `useUnifiedContainer`
    / `triggerDisplayManually` / `internal*` props and the `scrollTo` / `scrollBy` /
    `sync` instance methods are internal-only or imperative — not modelled
    (`scrollable = false` renders the slot bare upstream; wrapper
    components branch before calling `view`). The
    `container` prop (a caller-owned scroll element) is not reproduced: the built-in
    `n-scrollbar-container` / `n-scrollbar-content` are always rendered. When the caller
    needs to drive the container's scroll imperatively (upstream's `scrollTo` instance
    method — e.g. `NUI.TimePicker`'s scroll-to-active), `containerAttributes` puts
    attributes (an `id`) on the scrolling `n-scrollbar-container` div so
    `Browser.Dom.setViewportOf` can address it; the container's own classes and
    structure stay upstream's.

name: NUI.Select
comment:
Naive UI's `Select` — a thin composition over `NUI.BaseSelection` (the
trigger) and `NUI.SelectMenu` (the body). NOT a popover-family body-swap:
upstream mounts the menu in its own `VFollower` (positioning/clickoutside/
show/keyboard all runtime), so the port renders the trigger and offers the
menu as a separate caller-mounted body (the `NUI.Dropdown` lane minus the
popover entirely).

    import NUI.Select as Select
    import NUI.SelectMenu

    Select.view theme
        { Select.defaults | onUpdateValue = Just Changed }
        [ NUI.SelectMenu.Option
            { value = "drive", label = "Drive My Car", disabled = False, attributes = [] }
        ]

Trigger (`view`) DOM — the `.n-select` wrapper is bare (no vars, no extra
classes; all styling lives on the `.n-base-selection` trigger and the menu):

    div.n-select
      └─ NUI.BaseSelection.view (see its docstring for the full tree;
         `view` derives the display state from `value` + `options`)

`view` derives, per upstream: single `selectedLabel` = the value's option's
label, else the fallback (`fallbackOption` default true → the value itself
as its label; false → no selection shown); multiple `tags` = the value list
order mapped onto options (same fallback rules; unknown values drop when
`fallbackOption = False`); numeric `maxTagCount` slices the tags and sets
`ellipsisTag = Just rest` when `rest > 0`; `showClear = clearable &&
!disabled && (hover || active) && selected` (upstream `mergedClearable &&
selected` — hover is the one truly-runtime input, hence a field here).

Menu (`menu`) DOM — the select-menu root carrying Select's own additions
(the `NUI.Popselect` composition precedent, minus the popover classes):

    div.n-base-select-menu .n-base-select-menu--{size}-size
        [--rtl] [--multiple] .n-select-menu [fade-in-scale-up-transition-*]
      tabindex = 0 (focusable, upstream hardcodes true)
      style = 23 menu vars → --n-menu-box-shadow
      └─ NUI.SelectMenu rows incl. the __loading row (loading) — see there

`menuVars` = the 23 `NUI.SelectMenu` vars + `--n-menu-box-shadow` (Select's
single own var). The transition class is the follower's
`fade-in-scale-up-transition` phase (upstream wraps the menu in that
`Transition`).

Caller-owned runtime (the port-wide convention): show state, positioning
and mounting, keyboard navigation and pending (`--pending` via per-option
`attributes`), `virtualScroll`, filtering state (`pattern` +
`onPatternInput` flow through; `filterOptions` is the pure default filter),
`remote`/`loading` orchestration, tag creation (`tag` mode — prepend a
being-created option to the list you pass), the responsive `maxTagCount`
overflow and its preview popover (slice + `BaseSelection.ellipsisTag` is
the static seam), `clearFilterAfterSelect`, form-item size/disabled/status
merging, `consistentMenuWidth` (width follows the trigger's wrapper),
`onSearch`/`onScroll`/`onFocus`/`onBlur`, IME. `widthMode` is dead upstream
(declared, never read) — not ported; `items`/`onChange` deprecated; the
`default` slot upstream never renders. Values are `String` keys
(upstream allows numbers; the documented `NUI.SelectMenu` limitation).

name: NUI.SelectMenu
comment:
Naive UI's internal select-menu body (upstream `NInternalSelectMenu`,
`_internal/select-menu/`), rebuilt on elm-ui — the support module
`NUI.Popselect` renders (the `NUI.DrawerContent` / `NUI.Scrollbar` precedent;
the future `Select` batch extends it).

    div.n-base-select-menu .n-base-select-menu--{size}-size
        [--rtl] [--multiple] [+ caller extraClasses]
      tabindex = focusable ? 0 : -1
      style = 23 css vars
      ├─ div.n-base-select-menu__header [data-header]          — iff header
      ├─ div.n-base-select-menu__loading                       — iff loading
      │    > NBaseLoading (strokeWidth 20)                     — replaces the
      │      scrollbar/empty middle entirely
      ├─ NUI.Scrollbar
      │    > div.n-base-select-menu-option-wrapper             — padding from size
      │        > div.n-base-select-group-header {label}        — group header
      │        > div.n-base-select-option [--disabled] [--selected]
      │            [--grouped] [--pending] [--show-checkmark]
      │          > div.__content {label, [i.n-base-icon.__check > svg]}
      │                                                        — check iff selected && showCheckmark
      │          (a Custom row builds the same shell around its node;
      │           `renderOption` then swaps the whole row for the callback's
      │           return — upstream hands the built node to the callback,
      │           so the shell — its click, hover, selection — survives a wrap)
      │    (empty list → div.__empty [data-empty] {empty | NUI.Empty})
      └─ div.n-base-select-menu__action [data-action]          — iff action
          + div[width:0;height:0][tabindex=0]                  — NFocusDetector, inert

`data-header` / `data-empty` / `data-action` serialize `"true"` (upstream's
bare JSX attrs compile to `{true}` — the `NUI.Transfer` close-icon /
`NUI.TreeSelect` slot rule).

Everything runtime is caller-owned (the popover-family precedent): keyboard
navigation and `--pending` (caller-injected per-option `attributes`),
`virtualScroll` (the virtual list — the plain option-wrapper path only),
focus handlers, `onTabOut`. `loading` (upstream `Select`'s remote state)
replaces the middle with the `__loading` row — header and action still
mount. `--grouped` is computed from the tree;
`--show-checkmark` lands on EVERY option while `showCheckmark` (upstream
default true — the padding rule needs it). Options carry `value : String`
keys (upstream allows numbers); `Custom` renders its node inside the option
shell — `__content` carries the node, `onToggle` fires with its `key` (a
render lane row has no `value`, so it never marks `--selected`, matching
upstream's `isSelected` on a valueless rawNode). When `renderOption` is set,
every row — custom rows included — is swapped for the callback's return
(upstream `SelectOption.tsx`'s render tail: `renderOption({ node, … })`). Empty = zero flattened rows, group headers included — a
childless group renders its header, never the empty fallback.

comment:
Naive UI's `Skeleton`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    NUI.Skeleton.view theme NUI.Skeleton.defaults []

    -- three shimmering text lines
    NUI.Skeleton.view theme
        { opts
            | text = True
            , width = Just (NUI.Skeleton.Px 120)
            , repeat = 3
        }
        []

    -- a round avatar placeholder
    NUI.Skeleton.view theme
        { opts | circle = True, width = Just (NUI.Skeleton.Px 40) }
        []

(`defaults` must be bound to a local first — Elm's record update syntax does
not accept a qualified `NUI.Skeleton.defaults` there.)

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-skeleton`
class and one inline `style` attribute holding both the plain properties

`width`, `height`, `animation`) and the `--n-*` custom properties. `NUI.Css`
ships Naive UI's exact CSS, including the `skeleton-loading` keyframes.

Naive UI's `Skeleton` renders an empty placeholder div and has no slot, so
the `List (Element msg)` parameter exists only to keep the uniform NUI
component API — children are not rendered.

name: NUI.Slider
comment:
Naive UI's `Slider` — the rail/fill/handles navigation for numeric
values, single or range. Upstream is one component over an arrified value
list (single = `[value]`; `range` switches scalar↔array semantics).

    import NUI.Slider as Slider
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Slider.view Theme.default
        { sliderD
            | value = [ 40 ]
            , marks = [ { value = 34, label = "34" } ]
        }

**DOM** (horizontal, marks set):

    div.n-slider(--disabled|--active|--with-mark|--vertical|--reverse)
    │         [style: 25 --n-* vars; mousedown/touchstart]
    └─ div.n-slider-rail
        ├─ div.n-slider-rail__fill [style: left|bottom %, width|height %]
        ├─ div.n-slider-dots(--transition-disabled)
        │   └─ div.n-slider-dot(--active) [style: left|… %]
        ├─ div.n-slider-handles
        │   └─ div.n-slider-handle-wrapper [tabindex, role=slider, aria-*,
        │           style: left|… %, z-index] > (thumb | div.n-slider-handle)
        │       └─ div.n-slider-handle-indicator--<placement> [5 vars]  (tooltip)
        └─ div.n-slider-marks
            └─ div.n-slider-mark [style: left|… %]

**The state contract.** Upstream's drag runtime (document mousemove/up,
rect measurement, focus management) is caller-owned (the `NUI.Split` /
`NUI.Rate` precedent): `value`, `activeIndex`, `hoverIndex`, `dragging`
and `dotTransitionDisabled` are caller state. The view emits the discrete
handle events (`onHandleFocus`/`onHandleBlur`/`onHandleMouseEnter`/
`onHandleMouseLeave`, index-tagged) and a bare root `onMousedown`
(upstream binds the same handler to mousedown + touchstart); the
pointer→value→snap math is exported pure (`pointerToValue`,
`sanitizeValue`, `stepValue`, `closestMark`). `preventDefault` (upstream
only when a handle is picked) and arrow-key stepping are the caller's
`attributes` seam (`stepValue` carries the math).

**The popover seam.** Upstream teleports the value indicator through
`VBinder/VFollower` (`fade-in-scale-up` transition). The port anchors the
indicator to the handle wrapper itself — absolutely positioned against the
handle (the placement's side + centring transform, one margin offset from the
CSS `--{placement}` rule) — the positioned/teleported wrapper remains the
caller's (`NUI.Popover` conventions). `tooltip` gates the indicator;
`showTooltip` is the persistent non-range override (upstream's
`enabled = showTooltip && !range` is the follower seam).

**The rail anchor.** Upstream's fill/dots/handles/marks are absolutely
positioned DIRECT children of `.n-slider-rail` (its `position: relative`
makes it the containing block). The port renders them exactly so — any
intermediate wrapper would become the offset parent itself (elm-ui's
`.s { position: relative }`) at zero content width and collapse every
percentage offset inside it.

**Divergences from upstream (documented):**

  - `marks` is a `List Mark` in caller order (upstream's
    `Record<string,…>` insertion order); an empty list stands for absent
    marks (upstream's truthy-empty-object edge is a Vue-ism not modelled).
  - The `keyboard` prop and the `to`/teleport plumbing are not ported
    (above); `onUpdate:value`'s emission rides the caller's drag runtime,
    so the view carries no value-change handler — `onDragstart`/
    `onDragend` likewise (the root `onMousedown` signal covers the start).
  - `formatTooltip` formats the indicator text only (upstream default is
    the raw number — `String.fromFloat` is byte-identical to JS
    `String(number)`).
  - Upstream's `handleCountExceeds2` (more than two values: the fill
    renders unstyled — a bare node is kept — and all dots go inactive) is
    kept; `aria-disabled` reads the RAW `disabled` prop (upstream quirk —
    the attribute is emitted only when disabled; never the form-item
    merge, which the port has none of).
  - Accepted edges: `stepPrecision` counts the decimals segment of the
    step's string (upstream counts every char after the dot, exponent
    included — only reachable for degenerate exponent-form steps); the
    sanitize buffer is always `±1` (upstream treats a falsy `0` as unset
    and substitutes the direction default — the port's call sites never
    pass anything but `±1`).

(Record updates bind `defaults` to a local first — see `NUI.Button`.)

name: NUI.Space
comment:
Naive UI's `Space`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    NUI.Space.view theme
        NUI.Space.defaults
        [ NUI.Button.view theme NUI.Button.defaults [ Element.text "Ok" ] ]

Naive UI's Space ships no CSS — it is a plain flex container styled inline
(`display`, `flex-direction`, `justify-content`, `align-items`, `flex-wrap`,
`gap`). This module reproduces exactly those declarations as inline styles on an
elm-ui `row`/`column`, so the rendered layout matches Naive UI's
flex-gap-supported output (every modern browser).

**Wrapper divergence.** Upstream defaults to `wrapItem: true`, wrapping every
child in a `div[role=none]` (the `itemClass` / `itemStyle` carriers, and the
pre-flex-gap margin layout). This port renders the children straight into the
flex container — equivalent to upstream's `wrapItem: false` +
`internalUseGap` shape (the one modern browsers take anyway through the
`ensureSupportFlexGap` probe), so `wrapItem` / `itemClass` / `itemStyle` are
not modelled. An empty child list renders `Element.none`, like upstream's
`!children.length → null`.

name: NUI.Spin
comment:
Naive UI's `Spin`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Spin exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Spin.view theme NUI.Spin.defaults []

    NUI.Spin.view theme
        { defaults
            | description = Just (Element.text "Loading")
        }
        []

    -- wrapping content: the spinner overlays it while spinning
    NUI.Spin.view theme NUI.Spin.defaults [ Element.text "Content" ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the elements carry the `.n-spin` /
`.n-base-loading` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and
`NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Two shapes.** With children, `.n-spin-container` holds the content
(`.n-spin-content`, dimmed via `.n-spin-content--spinning` while `show`) plus an
absolutely-positioned `.n-spin-body`; without children, `.n-spin-body` is the
root and renders a standalone spinner. Without a custom `icon` the spinner is
Naive UI's internal `n-base-loading` SVG — the CSS `rotator` keyframe already
spins `__container`, and the SMIL `<animate>`/`<animateTransform>` children are
kept so real browsers animate the dash arc too.

**Data-driven runtime.** The caller owns the state: `delay` and the
deprecated `spinning` alias are just `show` applied late (no debouncing timer
here). `transition` (a `NUI.Internal.TransitionPhase`) adds the
`fade-in-transition-*` class around `.n-spin-body` and holds a leave mounted —
but only in the **wrapped** shape; the standalone shape renders the spinner
directly with no `Transition` (matching upstream's `Spin.tsx`, where the
`<Transition>` wraps `icon` only under a default slot), so `transition` is
ignored there. `content-class` / `content-style` are not ported (use
`attributes`).

**Why `scale`/`radius` are plain while `Button`/`Switch` spin\* are `Maybe`.**
Upstream `Spin` re-exports `NBaseLoading`'s `scale`/`radius` as its own props
(`exposedLoadingProps`, defaults `1`/`100`), and Vue materializes prop
defaults before render — `Spin.tsx` always passes a concrete
`radius={this.radius}` / `scale={this.scale}`. The value is therefore always
present, and this record bakes the defaults in (`strokeWidth` stays a `Maybe`
because Spin drops the prop default and computes one from `size`).
`Button`/`Switch`, by contrast, port upstream's `spinProps` — a spread over an
explicit `<NBaseLoading strokeWidth={20}/>` call site — where an absent key
falls through to that baseline, hence their `Maybe` fields. The asymmetry is
upstream-faithful, not an oversight.

`NUI.Types.Size` (which adds `tiny` and cannot be a number), so — like `Card` —
this module defines its own enum.

`radius` (the `NBaseLoading` re-exports; see the module docstring for

name: NUI.Split
comment:
Naive UI's `Split`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Split exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Split.view theme
        { defaults
            | size = NUI.Split.Ratio 0.4
            , pane1 = [ Element.text "Left" ]
            , pane2 = [ Element.text "Right" ]
        }

The element carries the `.n-split` BEM classes and Naive UI's `--n-*` custom
properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Runtime.** Upstream turns drag gestures into a new `size` (`px` or a ratio)
and flips the resize trigger's hover class while dragging. This library is pure,
so the caller owns `size` and `dragging`; the rendered markup (panes, trigger
wrapper, trigger) and the computed `flex` / trigger-size styles match upstream.

**Theme.** Naive UI's split theme is two common-variable lookups
(`resizableTriggerColor` = `borderColor`, `resizableTriggerColorHover` =
`primaryColorHover`) and its dark theme omits `self`, so this module reads them
from `theme.common` directly rather than from a generated theme module.

**Divergences (visibility chrome):** the panes carry a default light border
(`1px solid #efeff5`, overridable through `pane1Style` / `pane2Style`), and the
default `resizeTriggerSize` is `6` (upstream: `3`) — upstream's docs demos sit
on white surfaces where a 3px light-grey bar reads as missing; 6px keeps the
drag seam visible while staying a hairline.

**Upstream props not modelled** (all runtime or uncontrolled):
`defaultSize` (the uncontrolled mirror of `size` — state lives with the
caller), the pane clamp `min` / `max` (defaults 0 / 1; fold them into the
`size` you pass), and the drag events `onDragStart` / `onDragMove` /
`onDragEnd` (the caller owns the gesture; wire the wrapper through
`resizeTrigger` or `attributes` if you need the seam).

The split options — Naive UI's props plus the caller-owned drag state:

(omits the trigger wrapper entirely), `dragging` (upstream's
`isDragging` — drives `--hover` on the default trigger), the two panes'

The `n-split` element — pane 1 (its `flex` computed from `size`), the

name: NUI.Table
comment:
Naive UI's `Table` (`n-table`), the static table — real `<table>` DOM,
rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Table exposing (cellDefaults, defaults, rowDefaults)

    NUI.Table.view theme
        NUI.Table.defaults
        { head = [ { rowDefaults | cells = [ { cellDefaults | content = [ Element.text "Name" ] } ] } ]
        , body = [ { rowDefaults | cells = [ { cellDefaults | content = [ Element.text "Naive" ] } ] } ]
        }

(Record updates bind `defaults` to a local first — see `NUI.Button`.)

Upstream is five components: `Table` renders the `<table class="n-table">`
root (modifier classes + the 21 `--n-*` vars) and `Th` / `Td` / `Tr` /
`Thead` / `Tbody` are BARE tag wrappers the caller composes by hand. The
port keeps the root faithful and types the tag tree: `Table.head` rows
render as `<thead><tr><th>…` (omitted entirely when empty), `Table.body`
as `<tbody><tr><td>…`. Cell content is `Element msg`, embedded through
`Element.layoutWith` (`display: contents`, the `NUI.Descriptions`
precedent — there is no public `Element` → `Html`).

DOM (`Table.tsx` render + the five wrappers):

    table.n-table [--rtl] [--bottom-bordered] [--bordered] [--single-line]
                  [--single-column] [--striped]
      style = 21 vars
      ├─ thead > tr > th{colspan?, rowspan?}          — iff head non-empty
      └─ tbody > tr > td{colspan?, rowspan?}          — iff body non-empty

Divergences from upstream (documented): the root sits inside a bare
elm-ui wrapper `div` (the `NUI.Descriptions` root shape — caller
`attributes` need an elm-ui element to land on; Naive UI's own root IS
the `table` tag, and every `.n-table` rule resolves identically through
the wrapper), and `thead` / `tbody` take no caller attributes (upstream
reaches them only through Vue fallthrough on the hand-composed wrappers;
row and cell attributes are modelled, section attributes are not).

Not ported: nothing — the component is fully static (no runtime state, no
slots beyond the rows themselves). `--n-merged-border-color` is derived on
the ROOT RULE in the stylesheet (not an inline var), and the modal /
popover color variants ride the `insideModal` / `insidePopover` container
selectors automatically.
