name: NUI.Tabs
comment:
Naive UI's `Tabs` (`n-tabs` + `n-tab-pane`), rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Tabs as Tabs

    Tabs.view theme
        { Tabs.defaults | value = model.tab }
        [ { name = "a", label = Element.text "A", disabled = False, closable = Nothing
          , content = [ Element.text "Pane A" ] }
        , { name = "b", label = Element.text "B", disabled = False, closable = Nothing
          , content = [ Element.text "Pane B" ] }
        ]

The visual result is Naive UI's own: the element carries the `.n-tabs` BEM classes and
Naive UI's `--n-*` custom properties, and `NUI.Css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS. The caller
owns the active `value` (like `NUI.Form` / `NUI.Descriptions`).

**Divergences from upstream (documented):**

  - The nav/rail/tab/pane markup is built as raw `Html` (the port needs `data-*`
    attributes and a `<button>` close), and the caller's `label` / `content` `Element`s are
    embedded through `Element.layoutWith` (the `NUI.Form` precedent) with
    `Element.noStaticStyleSheet` — so each label/content carries one `display:contents`
    wrapper `div` and no duplicate elm-ui stylesheet.
  - `vueuc`'s `VXScroll` (top/bottom scroll) and `VResizeObserver` are omitted: for
    `Top`/`Bottom` the port renders `n-tabs-nav-scroll-wrapper > n-tabs-nav-scroll-content`
    directly; for `Left`/`Right` it keeps naive-ui's own `n-tabs-nav-y-scroll` wrapper.
  - The scroll buttons (`TabsButton` / `n-tabs-scroll-button`) are omitted (JS overflow).
  - `.n-tabs-bar` and the segment `.n-tabs-capsule` are positioned by upstream
    JS (`updateBarStyle` / `updateSegmentPosition` measure the active tab at
    runtime). The port inlines a pure-CSS equivalent: the bar rides inside the
    active tab (`position: relative` + `left/top: 0; width/height: 100%` —
    exactly the box upstream measures), and the capsule gets
    `width/height: calc(…)/count` + `translate(calc(3px + i * 100%), 3px)`
    (segment wrappers are equal-width `flex-grow` items). No transition of
    either between tabs (upstream animates `left`/`transform`).
  - `animated` only toggles the `n-tabs-pane-wrapper` markup; the enter/leave transition
    is not driven (the caller-driven-transition precedent, cf. Form's fade-down).
  - `displayDirective`: `'show:lazy'` is not ported — `ShowIf` (only the active pane) and
    `Show` (all panes, inactive ones `display:none`) are.
  - A close click does **not** `stopPropagation` (Elm has no such hook), so when a card tab
    is both activatable and closable both messages fire.
  - The add tab inherits `tabClass` / `tabStyle` (upstream's separate `addTabClass` /
    `addTabStyle` props are not ported, and the add tab is not a first-class element).
  - Not ported: draggable tabs, keyboard nav, `tabProps` passthrough,
    `paneWrapperClass`/`Style`, `addTabClass`/`Style`, `tabsPadding` > 0, `labelSize`,
    `onBeforeLeave`, `addable` as an object, `showScrollButton`.
  - `name` is `String` (upstream `string | number`).
  - `[oracle D]` **D1 — add tab ignores `trigger`.** `onAdd` is always
    click-wired (`:1072-1080`); upstream's add tab is a `Tab`, so a hover
    trigger adds on mouseenter (`Tab.tsx:124`).
  - `[oracle D]` **D2 — close `aria-disabled`.** The port omits it when enabled;
    `NBaseClose` always emits it (`Close.tsx:40` renders `"false"` when
    enabled).
  - `[oracle D]` **D3 — icon SVG byte drift.** `closePath` drops the trailing
    zero-area path segment + outer `<g>`; the add icon drops `width="512"
    height="512"` — visually identical (the shipped `_internal/icon` rule sizes
    the svg to `1em`).
  - `[oracle D]` **D4 — placement `start`/`end` not ported.** Upstream resolves
    them via RTL (`Tabs.tsx:171-180`); callers pre-resolve to Left/Right.
  - `[oracle D]` **D5 — `addTabFixed` not modeled.** The port always renders the
    add tab inside the scroll wrapper; upstream pins it outside once measured
    (`Tabs.tsx:666-704`, `:1244`).
  - `[oracle D]` **D9 — uncontrolled seeding.** Upstream seeds the first pane's
    name when uncontrolled (`Tabs.tsx:215-223`); the port is fully caller-owned
    (`value` required).

name: NUI.Theme
comment:
The **runtime theme** — the record every `NUI.*` component view takes as
its first argument.

It is the Elm counterpart of Naive UI's theme as handed to `ConfigProvider`:
`common` carries the shared variable palette (upstream `theme.common`, i.e.
`commonLight` / `commonDark` — see `NUI.Theme.Common`), and `mode` selects
which per-component variable set the `NUI.Theme.*` resolvers derive from,
exactly like upstream's `self(vars)` plumbing where each component theme
reads the common palette.

Typical use:

    import NUI.Theme as Theme


    -- the default light theme
    theme =
        Theme.default

    -- dark mode
    theme =
        Theme.withMode Theme.Dark Theme.default

    -- dark mode with a brand colour (hover/pressed derived like Naive UI)
    theme =
        Theme.default
            |> Theme.withMode Theme.Dark
            |> Theme.setPrimary "#18a058"

Nothing is global or mutated: components derive their `--n-*` custom
properties from whatever record you pass, so keep the theme in your model
(the examples app does) and thread it through `view`.

name: NUI.Theme.Color
comment:
Minimal colour maths ported from [`seemly`](https://github.com/07akiron/seemly) — the
library Naive UI itself uses for colour derivation — so that this port's runtime hover/
pressed/composite colours match Naive UI's byte-for-byte.

Every `NUI.Theme.*` resolver leans on this module: `createHoverColor` and
`createPressedColor` reproduce upstream's `createHoverColor`/`createPressedColor`
helpers that most component themes call on the shared palette, and `changeColor`
mirrors `seemly.changeColor` for alpha swaps.

@docs Rgba, parse, toCss, composite, changeColor, createHoverColor, createPressedColor

aliases.name: Rgba
aliases.comment:
An RGBA colour. Channels `r`/`g`/`b` are 0–255, alpha `a` is 0–1 — same ranges
`seemly` uses, so ports of its arithmetic stay exact.
aliases.type: { r : Basics.Float, g : Basics.Float, b : Basics.Float, a : Basics.Float }

values.name: changeColor
values.comment:
`seemly.changeColor(color, { alpha })` — keep a colour's RGB channels and swap
its alpha, as a `String -> Float -> String` convenience. Unparseable input is
returned unchanged.

values.name: composite
values.comment:
Alpha-composite `top` over `bottom` (seemly's `composite`, source-over blend).
Used to derive hover/pressed tints and to flatten translucent colours the way
Naive UI does when mixing surfaces.

values.name: createHoverColor
values.comment:
Composite 16% white over the input — upstream's `createHoverColor`, used by
most component themes to derive a hover tint from a palette colour. Unparseable
input is returned unchanged.

values.name: createPressedColor
values.comment:
Composite 12% black over the input — upstream's `createPressedColor`, the
pressed-state counterpart of `createHoverColor`. Unparseable input is returned
unchanged.

values.name: parse
values.comment:
Parse `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `rgb(r, g, b)` and `rgba(r, g, b, a)` into an `Rgba`.
Whitespace and letter case are tolerated; anything else yields `Nothing` (callers
fall back to the input string, so an unparseable value never breaks rendering).

values.name: toCss
values.comment:
Render an `Rgba` back to a CSS `rgba(r, g, b, a)` string (alpha rounded to 3
decimals) — the exact string form Naive UI emits, e.g. `rgba(56, 137, 197, 0.25)`.

name: NUI.TimePicker
comment:
Naive UI's `TimePicker` — an `NUI.Input` trigger plus a caller-mounted
columns panel (upstream mounts the panel in its own `VFollower`; the port
renders the trigger and offers the body separately, the `NUI.TreeSelect` /
`NUI.AutoComplete` composition precedent — show state, positioning,
clickoutside and keyboard are caller-owned runtime).

    import NUI.TimePicker as TimePicker

    TimePicker.view theme
        { TimePicker.defaultOptions
            | value = Just model.time
            , onUpdateValue = Just SetTime
        }

    -- the panel is a separate element — mount it yourself when `show`
    TimePicker.panel theme
        { TimePicker.defaultOptions
            | value = Just model.time
            , onUpdateValue = Just SetTime
        }

Trigger (`view`) DOM:

    div.n-time-picker
      style = 3 trigger vars → --n-icon-color-disabled-override, --n-bezier
      └─ NUI.Input.view (see its docstring) with the picker seams on:
         `passivelyActivated`, `attrSize = format.length + 4`,
         `internalForceFocus = show`, `textDecoration = 'line-through'` while
         the value is invalid, `readonly = inputReadonly || disabled`, and the
         clock icon riding `suffix` (not clearable) or `clear-icon-placeholder`
         (clearable — swaps to the clear icon over a value) inside
         `i.n-base-icon.n-time-picker-icon`.

Panel (`panel`) DOM — the body carrying the 14 time-picker vars:

    div.n-time-picker-panel [fade-in-scale-up-transition-*]
      tabindex = 0
      style = 14 vars → --n-item-border-radius
      ├─ div.n-time-picker-cols
      │   └─ per visible unit: div.n-time-picker-col
      │        [.n-time-picker-col--invalid] [.n-time-picker-col--transition-disabled]
      │        └─ NUI.Scrollbar.view > item divs + div.n-time-picker-col__padding
      ├─ div.n-time-picker-actions        — iff actions non-empty
      │    └─ NUI.Button size=tiny each (confirm: type primary + class
      │       .n-time-picker-actions__confirm + disabled iff invalid)
      └─ div[width:0;height:0][tabindex 0]  — NBaseFocusDetector

Visible units follow the format string exactly as upstream
(`hourInFormat = /H|h|K|k/.test(format)`, `format.includes('m')`,
`format.includes('s')`), plus the AM/PM column whenever `use12Hours`.

**Punts (caller-owned runtime, the port-wide convention).**

  - The scroll-to-active `scrollTimer` (`TimePicker.tsx:657-676`) measures the
    active item's `offsetTop` and scrolls each column — DOM geometry, no
    static effect. `data-active` rides the active item (`NUI.Scrollbar`'s
    position is caller-owned via `yBarStyle`), and the `colContainerIds` seam
    puts inert `id`s on the visible columns' `n-scrollbar-container` divs so
    the caller can drive that scroll with `Browser.Dom.setViewportOf`.
  - The IANA `timeZone` prop is replaced by `zone : Time.Zone` (caller
    supplied; `Time.utc` by default). `formatValue` / `parseInput` take it
    explicitly.
  - The `memorizedValue` auto-restore (`watch(mergedShow)` re-emits the
    memorized value when the current one is invalid, `:801-805`) is
    caller-owned data.
  - The panel's Tab handling (`handleMenuKeydown`) is caller-owned; the inert
    focus-detector sentinel at the panel's tail is what the runtime watches.
  - Enter / Escape activation (`handleWrapperKeydownEnter` / `...Esc`),
    programmatic focus / blur, the `onActivate` / `onDeactivate` emissions,
    clickoutside and the follower placement are caller-owned (no ports in
    house style — flip `show` yourself).
  - `onUpdate:value` fires with `(value, formattedValue)` upstream; a single
    Elm message cannot carry both — use `onUpdateValue` (format with
    `formatValue` when you need the string) and `onUpdateFormattedValue`
    separately.
  - `[oracle D]` **actions order.** The port renders `opts.actions` in the
    caller's list order; upstream renders a fixed `clear, now, confirm` gated by
    membership (`Panel.tsx:328-360`). Identical for the default
    `[Now, Confirm]`; only a non-canonical caller list reorders.

`formatValue` implements the date-fns token subset `H HH h hh K k m mm s ss a`
plus `'...'` literals (`''` → `'`); everything else passes through verbatim.
`parseInput` is `strictParse` (`date-picker/src/utils.ts:480-495`): parse then
re-`format` and require string equality, else `Nothing`. Parsed fields fill from
1970-01-01 (upstream's backup is `new Date()`; the time-of-day is what the
trigger compares) and are placed in `zone` via its offset at that instant.

comment:
Naive UI's `Tooltip` — upstream calls it "popover wearing waistcoat": the
`n-popover` body driven by the tooltip theme.

    import NUI.Theme as Theme
    import NUI.Tooltip exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Tooltip.view Theme.default
        defaults
        [ Element.text "A tooltip" ]

The element is the popover body (`.n-popover …` classes, Naive UI's exact CSS)
plus the `n-tooltip` marker class, with five of the popover vars overridden by
the tooltip theme: in light mode a dark bubble (`--n-color` black-ish,
`--n-text-color` the base colour); dark mode matches the popover's own colours.

**Everything in `NUI.Popover`'s docstring applies** — the caller-owned show
state / trigger / positioning, the `v-placement` wrapper contract (use
`placementAttribute`), the `--v-offset-*` note, the header/footer/scrollable
structure, `overlap` suppressing the arrow, and the transition phases. This
module only swaps the theme; see `NUI.Popover` for the full contract.

**Documented gaps** (beyond the popover's):

  - `NUI.Theme.Tooltip`'s light `color` is a pinned literal
    (`rgba(38, 38, 38, 1)`, upstream `composite(baseColor, 'rgba(0, 0, .85)')`
    computed at the default theme) — overriding `common.baseColor` does not
    re-derive it (the toolchain convention for derived values; cf. Tag).

name: NUI.Transfer
comment:
Naive UI's `Transfer`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Transfer as Transfer
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Transfer.view Theme.default
        { Transfer.defaults
            | options =
                [ { label = "Option 1", value = "1", disabled = False }
                , { label = "Option 2", value = "2", disabled = False }
                ]
            , value = [ "2" ]
            , sourceTitle = Just "Source"
            , targetTitle = Just "Target"
        }

Two scroll-synced lists (`n-transfer-list--source` / `--target`) with a
header (title + select/clear button + count `__extra`), an optional filter
input, and the item list (`__background` / `__checkbox` / `__label` /
`__close`), exactly Naive UI's DOM.

**Fidelity notes (read before diverging):**

  - **State is caller-owned.** Upstream keeps `value` and the two filter
    patterns in refs; the port takes them as inputs and reports every
    mutation through one channel, `onCheck : Maybe (List String -> msg)`
    (upstream's single `doUpdateValue` — item toggles, source check/uncheck
    all and target clear all all collapse into it). The filter inputs wire
    `onSourceFilterInput` / `onTargetFilterInput`; feed the text back as
    `sourcePattern` / `targetPattern`.
  - **Sizes.** `size` drives the five size-keyed theme vars and the header
    button size (`Large` → small buttons, anything else → tiny — upstream
    `size === 'large' ? 'small' : 'tiny'`). Upstream has no `tiny` transfer;
    the port's wider `Size` clamps `Tiny` to the small var set.
  - **Titles.** An empty-string title renders NO `__title` div (upstream's
    `title &&` guard — `''` is falsy). Function-valued titles
    (`[String, Function]` upstream) are not modelled — `Maybe String`
    only; a custom node is the caller's `renderSourceLabel`.
  - **Locale bytes are the defaults.** The header button labels default to
    the enUS `'Select all'` / `'Unselect all'` / `'Clear'` and `__extra` to
    `'Total {n} items'` / `'{n} items selected'` (upstream injects locale
    data; caller-supplied precedent, cf. DataTable's filter labels).
    `selectAllText` / `clearText` override the first two.
  - **`sourceFilterable` is already merged.** Upstream's deprecated
    `filterable` ORs into it; the port takes the merged value.
  - **The target filter reuses `sourceFilterPlaceholder`.** Upstream
    Transfer.tsx :374 wires `this.sourceFilterPlaceholder` into the target
    filter too — a faithful mirror, not a copy-paste bug of ours.
  - **`virtualScroll` is not modelled** — the plain (non-windowed) list
    path is the only renderer (Cascader/Select precedent).
  - **`renderEmpty` (config channel) is not modelled** — an empty list
    always renders the default `NUI.Empty` (no `NConfigProvider`).
  - **The default filter** matches upstream's: an empty pattern passes
    everything; otherwise a lowercase `contains` over the label. A custom
    `filter` receives the side (`Source` / `Target`).
  - **Duplicate option values** resolve last-wins (upstream's forEach +
    `Map.set` overwrite); `value` entries without an option are dropped
    from the target list, exactly upstream's `optionMap.get(v)` miss.
    Duplicate `value` ENTRIES are not deduped (upstream's three header ops
    start from `new Set(value)`; the port's list ops keep the raw order —
    degenerate-input divergence, same observable for duplicate-free input).
  - **`headerColor`** is generated in `NUI.Theme.Transfer` (the extractor
    executes upstream's `composite(cardColor, tableHeaderColor)`) but no
    css var consumes it — unused upstream too.
  - **Icon bytes.** The close icon is the generic `CloseIcon` `d` verbatim;
    the search icon's `d` is whitespace-normalized (upstream wraps the path
    data across lines — SVG-path-grammar identical, not byte-identical).
    The close button omits `NBaseClose`'s `onMousedown` preventDefault
    (a focus-steal guard for `focusable=false` — no serialized-DOM
    difference; `addEventListener` only).

name: NUI.Tree
comment:
Naive UI's `Tree`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Tree exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Tree.view theme { defaults | data = data, expandedKeys = [ "a" ] } []

Upstream renders a flat node list (`getFlattenedNodes` over the expanded
keys) as `div.n-tree-node-wrapper` rows inside the `div.n-tree` root; each
row is an indent chain (guide lines under `showLine`), a switcher (arrow
svg, or the loading spinner while the key is in `loadingKeys`), an optional
checkbox, and the content (prefix / label / suffix). All interaction state —
expanded / checked / selected / pending / loading keys — is caller-owned
data, exactly as upstream's controlled props; the view emits the DOM for it.

Upstream: `src/tree/src/Tree.tsx` (render + cssVars), `TreeNode.tsx`,
`TreeNodeSwitcher.tsx`, `TreeNodeCheckbox.tsx`, `TreeNodeContent.tsx`,
`utils.ts` (`filterTree`), and treemate (`getCheckedKeys`, flatten, check /
uncheck cascade math).

Not ported (runtime, caller-owned): the virtual-list branch (plain wrapper
path only, as in Select/Cascader), the expand/collapse `MotionWrapper`
transition, drag-drop event wiring (the drop mark itself is data:
`dropMark`), keyboard navigation (`pendingKey` is data), and the async
`onLoad` dance (`loadingKeys` is data). `--n-drop-mark-color` /
`--n-loading-color` stay live through those data fields.

values.comment:
Upstream `filterTree` (`utils.ts:78-146`) with the default
case-insensitive label-contains matcher (`Tree.tsx:397-411`): the pruned
tree keeps every match and the branch above it (a matched branch deep in a
collapsed subtree keeps its whole subtree — the visited-tail rule), the
highlight set is the matched keys in document order, and the expanded set
is the cloned-branch keys that reveal the matches. An empty pattern
echoes the tree untouched.

children join only while their parent's key sits in `expandedKeys`, each

and the ancestors' last-child chain (nearest-first) for the `showLine`
indent.

`cascade`, each key extends to its whole enabled subtree and the parents

`checkStrategy` then collapses the result (`All` keeps every level,
`Parent` the topmost checked ancestor, `Child` leaf levels only). An
unloaded node (`isLeaf = False`, `children = Nothing`) keeps its own key
and skips only the subtree extension under `allowCheckingNotLoaded` —
without it, upstream throws `SubtreeNotLoadedError` (from this
normalization too, `lib/check.js` `getExtendedCheckedKeySet`); the pure
port stays total by keeping the same set the `allowNotLoaded` path would
produce.

The tree — the `div.n-tree` root (`--rtl` / `--checkable` / `--block-node`

match set. Checked / indeterminate normalize against the FULL data tree
with the default `All` strategy (upstream passes no `checkStrategy` to
`getCheckedKeys` — the configured one applies only to `check` / `uncheck`);
`indeterminateKeys` overrides the computed set wholesale.

name: NUI.TreeSelect
comment:
Naive UI's `TreeSelect` — a `NUI.BaseSelection` trigger plus a
caller-mounted tree menu (the `NUI.Select` / `NUI.Cascader` composition
precedent: upstream mounts the menu in its own `VFollower`, so the port
renders the trigger and offers the body separately; show state,
positioning, clickoutside and keyboard are caller-owned runtime).

    import NUI.SelectMenu exposing (Value(..))
    import NUI.TreeSelect as TreeSelect

    TreeSelect.view theme
        { TreeSelect.defaults
            , value = Single (Just "outfield")
            , options = data
            , onUpdateValue = Just Changed
        }

Trigger (`view`) DOM — the `.n-tree-select` wrapper is bare (no vars, no
extra classes; `z-index / outline / width / position` come from the
stylesheet):

    div.n-tree-select
      └─ NUI.BaseSelection.view (see its docstring for the full tree;
         `view` derives the display state from `value` + `options` — a
         value whose node is MISSING drops entirely, no fallback label)

Menu (`menu`) DOM — the body carrying the 11 tree-select vars:

    div.n-tree-select-menu [fade-in-scale-up-transition-*]
      tabindex = 0 (upstream hardcodes it)
      style = 11 vars → --n-header-divider-color
      ├─ div.n-tree-select-menu__header [data-header]     — iff header
      ├─ NUI.Tree.view (internalScrollable — see below)   — iff nodes visible
      ├─ div.n-tree-select-menu__empty                    — iff NO visible
      │    > {empty slot | NUI.Empty}                     nodes (replaces the
      ├─ div.n-tree-select-menu__action [data-action]     whole tree — iff action
      └─ div[width:0;height:0][tabindex 0]                — NFocusDetector

The embedded tree (`NUI.Tree` with `internalScrollable`): the whole
`.n-tree` root — classes, 18 vars — rides ON the scrollbar's root via
fallthrough, the content carries `padding:4px` (the theme's `menuPadding`),
and the node rows wrap in one attribute-less `div`:

    div.n-scrollbar.n-tree.n-tree--block-node.n-tree--block-line
         [.n-tree--checkable iff checkable] [.n-tree--rtl iff rtl]
      style = scrollbar's own 23 vars ; tree's 18 vars (fallthrough last)
      └─ .n-scrollbar-container > .n-scrollbar-content[padding:4px]
         > div > .n-tree-node-wrapper*   (checkboxes inert + not focusable)

`data-header` / `data-action` serialize `"true"` (upstream's bare JSX
attrs compile to `{true}` — the `NUI.Transfer` close-icon aria-hidden
precedent).

Value algebra — pure helpers (the `NUI.Transfer` derive precedent).
Upstream passes `internalUnifySelectCheck` UNCONDITIONALLY, so line
clicks, label clicks and checkbox clicks all converge:

  - `handleNodeClick opts value key` — single: `Single (Just key)` whatever
    was clicked (checkbox included — cancelable is off upstream; a disabled
    or missing node is a no-op). multiple + checkable: flips the node
    through the tree's cascade check / uncheck under the MERGED cascade
    (`multiple && cascade && checkable`) and MERGED strategy
    (`checkStrategyOf` — `leafOnly` folds to `child`), checked-status base
    normalized with the default `All` strategy exactly as upstream's
    `displayedCheckedKeysRef`. multiple + plain: `Tree.toggleSelect` (rows
    toggle in and out — the checkbox renders states only; a wired checkbox
    would double-fire with the row click, the `NUI.Cascader` note).
    A NON-leaf is dead under the merged `child` strategy without the
    cascade multiple mode (`TreeNode.tsx:111-121` under
    `internalTreeSelect` — no `--selectable`, the click never selects);
    leaves and every non-`child` node click through.
  - `deleteOption opts value key` — the tag close: base =
    `Tree.getCheckedKeys` with cascade + allowNotLoaded but NO strategy
    (upstream `TreeSelect.tsx:623-629` — treemate's default `all`); a key
    outside the base is a no-op; checkable runs `Tree.uncheck` under the
    RAW `checkStrategy` (upstream `:643` passes `props.checkStrategy`
    unmerged — the deprecated `leafOnly` folds everywhere EXCEPT this
    delete path, upstream's own inconsistency), plain splices the single
    index.
  - `clearValue value` — `Multiple []` / `Single Nothing`.
  - `initialPendingKey opts` — the `--pending` seed: `Nothing` under
    `checkable`, else the LAST key of an initial list value (a single value
    seeds nothing). The caller feeds it (and every later click — upstream's
    `pendingNodeKeyRef`) through `pendingKey`.

Caller-owned runtime (the port-wide convention): show state and follower
positioning (`placement` / `to` / `consistentMenuWidth` — mount `menu` in
your own positioned wrapper), the `fade-in-scale-up-transition` phases
(`transition` carries the class), clickoutside + the keyboard ladder
(Enter / Escape / ArrowDown through the tree), `onLoad` async
(`loadingKeys` data), `watchProps`, IME, focus return, the filter's
expand-to-reveal (a non-empty `pattern` fires `onUpdateExpandedKeys` with
`Tree.filterTree`'s reveal keys upstream — merge them yourself), and
`clearFilterAfterSelect` (reset `pattern` after a multiple check).

Not ported: `getChildren` (fixed record fields — the `NUI.Cascader`
note), `renderTag` + `ellipsisTagPopoverProps` + the responsive
`maxTagCount` overflow (numeric slicing is the static seam, as in
`NUI.Select`), `defaultExpandAll` / `defaultExpandedKeys` (seed
`expandedKeys` — `Tree.getNonLeafKeys` expands everything),
`overrideDefaultNodeClickBehavior` (behaviour-only), `menuProps`'s raw
`style` (use `attributes`; the class rides it too),
`leafOnly` is deprecated (folds into `checkStrategyOf`), `virtualScroll`'s
windowing (punted like the `--virtual` columns — the port pins the
`internalScrollable`-branch bytes, upstream's
`consistentMenuWidth=false` configuration), numeric option keys
(`String` keys — the `NUI.SelectMenu` limitation).

Upstream `useMergedCheckStrategy` — the deprecated `leafOnly` is

The clear button (`handleClear`, :604-616): an empty list in multiple

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults (`checkStrategy: 'all'`, `separator: ' / '`,
`indent: 24`, `placeholder` = the en-US locale `'Please Select'`, single
`null` value; everything else false / empty).

values.name: deleteOption
values.comment:
The tag close (`handleDeleteOption`, :617-661; multiple mode only).
The base normalizes with cascade + `allowCheckingNotLoaded` but NO
check strategy — treemate's default `all` — then the checkable path
unchecks under the RAW `checkStrategy` (upstream `:643` passes
`props.checkStrategy` unmerged — `leafOnly` does NOT fold on the delete
path) while the plain path splices exactly the found index. A key
outside the base leaves the value untouched.

values.name: handleNodeClick
values.comment:
One node click — every mode converges (upstream
`internalUnifySelectCheck` is always on: a checkbox click in single mode
REDIRECTS to select; a row click in checkable multiple mode becomes the
cascade check / uncheck flip). Disabled or missing nodes are no-ops
(`Tree.tsx:1032-1035`; the per-node gate), and so is a non-leaf under the
merged `child` strategy without the cascade multiple mode — upstream's
per-node selectable gate under `internalTreeSelect` (`TreeNode.tsx
:111-121`: the row renders without `--selectable` and `_handleClick`
returns before `handleSelect` — with `expandOnClick` / `checkOnClick` off,
the tree-select default, the click does nothing at all).

values.name: initialPendingKey
values.comment:
The `--pending` seed (upstream `pendingNodeKeyRef` init, :274-281):
nothing under `checkable`, else the LAST key of an initial list value — a
single value seeds nothing.

name: NUI.Types
comment:
The two enums every `NUI.*` component takes — `Size` is Naive UI's `size`
prop and `Kind` its `type` prop, ported as Elm custom types with the
component-class suffix each constructor maps to (`sizeClass` /
`kindClass`).

    -- `NUI.Button.view theme { defaults | kind = NUI.Button.Primary } …`
    -- is rendered with the class `n-button--primary-type` (kindClass)
    kindClass Primary --> "primary"

Both scales are driven per component through its `Options` record
(`{ defaults | size = Small }`); the returned class suffix combines with the
component's BEM block for the final `n-{block}--{suffix}-type` form.

@docs Size, Kind, sizeClass, kindClass

unions.name: Kind
unions.comment: Naive UI status / colour scale (its `type` prop).

unions.name: Size
unions.comment:
Naive UI size scale (`size` prop) — `sizeClass` maps it to the class
suffix: `Tiny → "tiny"`, `Small → "small"`, `Medium → "medium"`,
`Large → "large"`.

values.name: kindClass
values.comment:
The class suffix for a kind — `kindClass Primary == "primary"`; components
emit it as `"n-{block}--" ++ kindClass kind ++ "-type"`, the class behind
Naive UI's coloured variants (`.n-button--primary-type` …).

values.name: sizeClass
values.comment:
The class suffix for a size — `sizeClass Small == "small"`; components
emit it as `"n-{block}--" ++ sizeClass size ++ "-type"`.

name: NUI.Typography
comment:
Naive UI's `Typography` component set, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Typography exposing (defaults)

Every element carries the same BEM classes and the same `--n-*` custom properties
Naive UI emits, so with `NUI.Css` in scope it renders using Naive UI's own CSS.

    NUI.Typography.h1 theme
        NUI.Typography.defaults
        [ Element.text "Wonderful" ]

    NUI.Typography.text theme
        { defaults | kind = T.Primary, strong = True }
        [ Element.text "primary and strong" ]

    NUI.Typography.ul theme
        NUI.Typography.defaults
        [ NUI.Typography.li [ Element.text "First" ]
        , NUI.Typography.li [ Element.text "Second" ]
        ]

One `Options` record covers the whole set (Naive UI threads the same theme props
through every typography component); each element only honours the fields its
Naive UI counterpart has, plus a few elm-side conveniences that Naive UI leaves to
its users (`size`, `align`, `fontWeight`, `href`).

Block-level elements (`h1`-`h6`, `p`, `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `hr`) are
elm-ui paragraphs — block flow with wrapping inline children. `text` and `a` flow
inline when placed inside a paragraph.

name: NUI.Upload
comment:
Naive UI's `Upload`, rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import NUI.Upload as Upload
    import NUI.Theme as Theme

    Upload.view Theme.default
        { Upload.defaults
            | fileList =
                [ { id = "a"
                  , batchId = Nothing
                  , name = "a.png"
                  , percentage = Just 42
                  , status = Upload.Uploading
                  , url = Nothing
                  , thumbnailUrl = Nothing
                  , type_ = Nothing
                  , fullPath = Nothing
                  }
                ]
        }

The DOM is Naive UI's own: the root `div.n-upload` (the 16 `--n-*` vars), the
`input.n-upload-file-input`, the `div.n-upload-trigger` (with its image-card
dragger), the `div.n-upload-file-list` and the `div.n-upload-file` rows
(`__info` / `__thumbnail` / `__name` / `__action`), plus the line progress bar
while a file is uploading. `css/naive-ui.css` ships Naive UI's exact CSS.

**Caller-owned runtime.** Upstream's `Upload` is an imperative component: it
opens the file dialog, drives XHR (or a `customRequest`), reads `File` objects
into a `FileList`, resolves thumbnails asynchronously and serialises
`doChange` through `nextTick`. This library is pure, so the port exposes the
render surface and the **pure state machine**, and the host app owns the
effects:

  - `fileList` is the caller's list. Every open/close/append/replace is a
    caller update; the module's `settle` / `pendingFile` / `updateFileList` /
    `appendFile` / `removeFileById` / `mark*` helpers are the ports of
    upstream's `createSettledFileInfo` / `handleFileAddition` / `doChange` /
    the XHR-handler transitions — the caller applies them in its `Msg` handlers.
  - The events (`onTriggerClick` / `onFileChange` / `onDrop` /
    `onDragStateChange` / `onRemove` / `onRetry` / `onDownload` / `onPreview`)
    are Elm channels — Vue listeners never become DOM attributes (no byte
    impact). `onFileChange` fires on the input's `change`; read the picked
    `File`s through ports, run `handleFileAddition`'s pure steps
    (`sliceForMax` + `pendingFile` + `appendFile`), then submit.

**Accepted edges (documented divergences):**

1.  `file : File` is dropped from `FileInfo` — Elm has no `File`. Thumbnail
    resolution (`createImageDataUrl` / `URL.createObjectURL`) is caller-side:
    write the resolved URL into `thumbnailUrl`. `environmentSupportFile ≡
    true` (every targeted browser supports it).
2.  XHR + `customRequest` + `onBeforeUpload` / `onFinish` / `onError` rewrites
      - directory-entry (`webkitGetAsEntry`) traversal are host ports; the
        module exposes only the pure transitions (`markUploading` /
        `markFinished` / `markError` / `markRemoved`, `filesToSubmit`).
3.  `draggerInside` is explicit (a pure tree cannot introspect the slot for
    `uploadDraggerKey`); `abstract` renders a Fragment — upstream teleports
    the input to `body`, the port returns `[ inputNode, slot ]` for the caller
    to place.
4.  `onRemove` carries the file **id** (upstream passes `{ file, fileList,
    index }` — the caller derives those); the trigger's `options`-object slot
    is dropped (wire drag/click messages directly).
5.  RTL is dropped (`rtlEnabled` defaults false, house precedent).
6.  `scheduleDoChange` / `nextTick` serialisation is unnecessary in a
    synchronous pure render.
7.  `defaultUpload` auto-submit after addition is the caller's
    responsibility — `filesToSubmit` is the selection rule, nothing
    auto-fires.
8.  The `value = ''` reset of the `<input>` after a change is a host DOM
    command (Elm holds no element ref).
9.  The image-card thumbnail's `NImage` is embedded through `Element.layoutWith`
    (`display:contents` wrapper) — elm-ui has no public `Element → Html`. The
    `NImage`-in-`NImageGroup` context is the same approximation `NUI.Image`
    documents (no group registration, `data-group-id=""`).
10. `imageGroupOptions` is accepted for API parity but is inert: upstream's
    `NImageGroup` renders a Fragment (its preview container is teleported to
    `body`), so it adds no in-flow node to the file list — mount
    `NUI.ImageGroup.view` yourself with the file urls.

Fidelity notes: the `n-upload-file--info-status` / `--success-status` classes
are emitted upstream with no cssr rule (only `--error-status` has one), as is
`n-upload-file-info__action--text-type`; the icon glyphs are byte-verbatim
(9 private constants). The action buttons are icon-only `NUI.Button`s carrying
`varOverrides = { paddingMedium, heightMedium, iconSizeMedium }`
(`UploadFile.tsx:21-25`); they always render an empty `n-button__content`
(the `NUI.Button` content-span behaviour, shared with `NUI.InputNumber`).
[oracle D13] The root and (abstract) file-list class arrays omit Naive UI's
inline-theme `themeClass` (house-wide: the inline-theme-optimisation class
never lands in this port; no-op under the default theme).

\`never lands in this port; no-op under the default theme).

Upstream refs: `upload/src/Upload.tsx` (render :655-680, cssVars :507-561,
`doChange` :331-366, `handleFileAddition` :367-433, `submit` :434-480),
`UploadTrigger.tsx`, `UploadFileList.tsx`, `UploadFile.tsx`,
`UploadDragger.tsx`, `UploadProgress.tsx`, `utils.ts`, `icons.tsx`.

Upstream's error-handler transition — **status only** (the latched

Upstream's abort-handler transition: `status: 'removed'` (the `file: null`

`percentage` set. The percentage LATCH lives with the caller (upstream keeps

values.name: matchType
values.comment:
Upstream `matchType` (`utils.ts:145`), byte-faithful:

    name =
        name.toLowerCase ()

    mimeType =
        mimeType.toLocaleLowerCase ()

    accept =
        accept.toLocaleLowerCase ()

`toLocaleLowerCase` and `toLowerCase` coincide for ASCII, and Elm's
`String.toLower` is an ASCII fold — the accept/mime lowercasing is modelled
with it. An atom starting with `.` is a suffix match on the name; an atom
containing `/` is a mime match with `*` wildcards on either side; any other
atom (no dot, no slash — an "invalid type") matches everything.

values.name: pendingFile
values.comment:

`status: 'pending'`, `url` / `thumbnailUrl` `null`.

values.name: settle

Upstream `createSettledFileInfo`: normalises every optional field with

values.name: sliceForMax
values.comment:
Upstream's `max` slice in `handleFileAddition`: keep the first
`max - currentLen` incoming files. No `max` keeps every incoming file.

Accepted edge (oracle R1): when `max - currentLen` is negative, JS
`arr.slice(0, negative)` counts from the END (a from-end prefix) while this
port returns `[]` (List.take semantics) — unreachable inside the component,
because `handleFileAddition` only runs while `!maxReached`, so the cap is
always ≥ 1 there.

(Design surface named this `sliceForMax`; the port returns the sliced list —
the operation upstream actually performs — rather than the bare count, so the
`Nothing` case has a meaningful value.)

name: NUI.Watermark
comment:
Naive UI's `Watermark` (`n-watermark`) — the tiled text / image overlay,
rebuilt on elm-ui.

    import Element
    import NUI.Theme as Theme
    import NUI.Watermark exposing (defaults)

    NUI.Watermark.view Theme.default
        { defaults | content = Just "Naive UI" }
        [ Element.text "The watermarked content" ]

(Record updates bind `defaults` to a local first — see `NUI.Button`.)

DOM (`Watermark.tsx` render):

    div.n-watermark-container [--global-rotate] [--fullscreen] [--selectable]
      style = zIndex (iff global-rotate AND fullscreen)
      ├─ …children (the watermarked content)         — iff not the bare branch
      └─ div.n-watermark [--global-rotate] [--fullscreen]
           style = transform? zIndex? background-size
                   background-position? background-image

When `fullscreen` and no `globalRotate`, upstream returns the watermark node
BARE (no container, children dropped); the port does the same (`view`'s
children are ignored in that branch).

**The canvas seam.** Upstream draws the tile on a runtime `<canvas>`
(`fillText` / `drawImage` → `toDataURL`) and tiles it as a background image.
There is no canvas in pure Elm, so the port rebuilds the tile as an SVG and
base64-encodes it in-library (the `NUI.Qrcodegen` precedent — reimplementing
upstream's JS image math purely):

  - `content` — an SVG tile of exactly the canvas dimensions
    (`(xGap + width) × (yGap + height)`), one `<text>` per line with the
    upstream font stack / colour, inside the upstream `rotate` transform.
    Empty or absent `content` is upstream's third branch (`clearRect`) — a
    blank tile, so the overlay is present but invisible.
  - `image` — referenced directly: `url(<image>)` composed into the same
    `cross` doubling and the same `background-size` tiling. Upstream
    re-rasterises the image onto the tile canvas (applying `imageOpacity`,
    `imageWidth` / `imageHeight` scaling and the offsets); those three props
    are kept for API parity but the pure render cannot apply them — the
    display matches when the image's natural size fits the tile.

Divergences from upstream (documented): the MIME prefix is
`data:image/svg+xml` where the canvas emits `data:image/png`; the tile is
rendered at ratio 1 (upstream multiplies every canvas coordinate by
`devicePixelRatio` — identical display at ratio 1); `textAlign` `Center` /
`Right` anchor on the mark box (`xOffset` .. `xOffset + width`) where
upstream measures the text with `measureText` and anchors on the measured
box — identical when the longest line is exactly `width` wide, and `Left`
is exact; the `debug` rects are drawn in the SVG tile only (the image path
has no tile to draw on, and the grey outline is dropped on the empty tile
— upstream's `clearRect` wipes it); and the root sits inside a bare elm-ui wrapper
`div` carrying the caller `attributes` (the `NUI.Table` root shape), with
each child embedded through a `display: contents` wrapper (the
`NUI.Descriptions` seam — there is no public `Element` → `Html`).

Not ported: nothing else — `onFontsReady` re-rendering and the
`isBrowser` / `warnOnce` guards are runtime plumbing around the canvas.

@docs Options, TextAlign, containerStyle, defaults, tileDataUrl, view, watermarkStyle

unions.name: TextAlign
unions.comment:
Upstream `textAlign` — `'left' | 'center' | 'right'`; anchors each line
inside the mark box (see the canvas-seam note above).

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The watermark options (upstream `watermarkProps`): `selectable` defaults
`True`, sizes are pixels, `rotate` / `globalRotate` are degrees, and the
font props feed the tile's `<text>` (upstream: the canvas font string).
`imageOpacity` / `imageWidth` / `imageHeight` are API parity only — see the
canvas-seam note.
aliases.type: { debug : Basics.Bool, cross : Basics.Bool, fullscreen : Basics.Bool, width : Basics.Int, height : Basics.Int, zIndex : Basics.Int, xGap : Basics.Int, yGap : Basics.Int, yOffset : Basics.Int, xOffset : Basics.Int, rotate : Basics.Float, textAlign : NUI.Watermark.TextAlign, image : Maybe.Maybe String.String, imageOpacity : Basics.Float, imageWidth : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int, imageHeight : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int, content : Maybe.Maybe String.String, selectable : Basics.Bool, fontSize : Basics.Int, fontFamily : Maybe.Maybe String.String, fontStyle : String.String, fontVariant : String.String, fontWeight : Basics.Int, fontColor : String.String, fontStretch : String.String, lineHeight : Basics.Int, globalRotate : Basics.Float, attributes : List.List (Element.Attribute msg) }

values.name: containerStyle
values.comment:
The container's inline declarations — just the `z-index` the fullscreen /
global-rotate branch needs (upstream moves it off the overlay there), empty
otherwise.

values.name: defaults
values.comment:
Naive UI's defaults (`width` / `height` 32, `zIndex` 10, `fontSize` 16,
`fontWeight` 400, `rotate` 0, `lineHeight` 16 degrees of a default 32px tile,
selectable, not fullscreen, no cross, no debug, no content).

values.name: tileDataUrl
values.comment:
The tile as a `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` URL — what upstream's
`canvas.toDataURL()` stood for: an SVG of the canvas dimensions with the
`content` lines as `<text>` (absent / empty content is the blank tile,
upstream's `clearRect` branch), base64-encoded in-library. `view`'s overlay
backgrounds itself with it.

values.name: view
values.comment:
The watermark — the container `div` wrapping the children plus the tiled
overlay `div` (or the overlay alone, when `fullscreen` without
`globalRotate` — upstream's bare return), inside the bare elm-ui wrapper
that carries the caller `attributes` (the `NUI.Table` root shape).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Watermark.Options msg -> List.List (Element.Element msg) -> Element.Element msg

values.name: watermarkStyle
values.comment:
The overlay's inline declarations in upstream's style-object order
(see the full note above).
values.type: NUI.Theme.Theme -> NUI.Watermark.Options msg -> List.List ( String.String, String.String )
